# Design decisions for Commit 1 that changed the DB

### Decision 1: `CloseIssue` becomes a wrapper over a new `CloseIssueWithReason`

**Decision:** The close logic moves into a new `CloseIssueWithReason` in `services/issue/status.go`. `CloseIssue` keeps its signature and calls it with an empty reason, with a code comment marking it as a backwards-compatibility step.
**Alternatives Considered:** Change `CloseIssue`'s signature and update all nine call sites.
**Rationale:** Automatic closes (commit keywords, merged PRs, branch deletion) have no reason to give. The wrapper leaves them untouched.
**Consequences:** Two entry points for closing an issue. New code that should record a reason must call `CloseIssueWithReason`; the comment on `CloseIssue` points there.

### Decision 2: Whitespace-only "other" text counts as empty

**Decision:** The "other" text is trimmed before the empty check (AC3).
**Alternatives Considered:** Check the raw text, so any non-empty string, including only spaces, passes.
**Rationale:** Text should be trimmed to avoid blank reason strings.
**Consequences:** Needs its own test case next to the empty-text case.

### Decision 3: Store the reason as a Go integer enum plus two non-null columns

**Decision:** Add three columns to `issue`: `close_reason`, `close_reason_text` and `close_duplicate_issue_id`.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) A single `close_reason_text` column holding either a fixed reason or the "other" text. (b) Nullable columns, with NULL meaning no reason. (c) A database-level ENUM type.
**Rationale:** (a) can't tell "other: not planned" apart from the real "not planned." (b) makes every consumer handle NULL, while `NOT NULL DEFAULT` fills existing rows in the same `ALTER TABLE` (c) doesn't exist in Gitea: enums are Go integer types stored as plain integer columns (`CommentType`, `ReviewType`, `XRefAction`), because the four supported databases don't share an ENUM type.
**Consequences:** The database only holds numbers, so the meaning of each value lives in Go and values must never be renumbered. Nothing in the database restricts the values, so validation must reject anything outside the list. The close comment stores its own copy of the reason (Decision 4), so the issue can hold the current reason while each close comment keeps the one it was closed with.

### Decision 4: Close comments store their reason in `CommentMetaData`, not new columns

**Decision:** A close comment's reason, "other" text and duplicate target, go into the existing `CommentMetaData` JSON field instead of new `comment` columns. AC1 is amended to match: the migration only adds columns to `issue`.
**Alternatives Considered:** The same three columns on `comment` as on `issue`, as AC1 was first written.
**Rationale:** The field's own code comment says to put all non-index metadata there (`models/issues/comment.go`, added upstream in #29311), and later features followed it (the CODEOWNERS marker). It holds data that never changes after insert, which is AC6's rule that an earlier close comment keeps its reason.
**Consequences:** SQL can't filter, sort or index comments by close reason: nothing in `models/` queries inside JSON, and the four databases write JSON queries differently. That's acceptable because comments are only read one issue at a time.
--

# Design decisions for Commit 3 that implemented rules in the model layer

**Decision:** Closing with "completed", "not planned", "duplicate" or no reason while also sending text is rejected with `ErrInvalidCloseReasonText`. Whitespace-only text still counts as no text (Decision 2).
**Alternatives Considered:** Silently discard the text and close with the chosen reason.
**Rationale:** A close carries exactly one reason, and text belongs only to "other". A form or API client that sends both has a bug.
**Consequences:** The close form in #54 has to clear the text box when a reason other than "other" is picked, and API clients in #55 get a 400 if they send both.
--

# Design decisions for Commit 8 that implemented the backend half of the web close path

### Decision 6: The web close form carries the reason in this issue; the UI inputs come in #54

**Decision:** The backend half of the web close path is done in #53. `CreateCommentForm` gains the reason fields, and `NewComment` in `routers/web/repo/issue_comment.go` calls `CloseIssueWithReason` and shows a flash message when the reason is refused. #54 only adds the inputs to the template and the display. Bulk close on the issue list (`UpdateIssueStatus`) keeps closing with no reason, and the API stays with #55.
**Alternatives Considered:** Leave the handler on `CloseIssue` and let #54 wire the form, the handler and the template together.
**Rationale:** Reading the request, building `CloseReasonOptions` and turning refusals into a response are server-side work that can be tested by posting the form, with no HTML involved. It also fixes a silent failure: the handler only logs close errors other than open dependencies, so a refused reason would otherwise leave the issue open with no message.
**Consequences:** Until #54 adds the inputs, the form sends no reason and the close button behaves exactly as before. Refusals need a user-visible string in the locale file. Bulk close cannot record a reason.
--

TITLE: Select close reasons for Issues and PRs and show it under closed Issues and PRs in the UI.
STATE: OPEN
LABELS: enhancement, scope: medium
ASSIGNEES: ab-wm

### User Story

As a repository maintainer, I want a way to set a close reason for an issue and a PR so there is historical context for why the closing occurred. Furthermore, I want to be able to clearly and quickly see the reason behind the closing of an issue or PR in the UI.

### User Scenario

#### Writing the Reasons
A user who is attempting to close an issue or PR can either close the issue with a default reason by clicking the current "close issue/PR" button or by clicking the split button that will show a drop down to select from set responses:

| Reason | Special Semantics |
| --- | ---| 
| "Completed" | **Default** option for Issue. **NOT AVAILABLE FOR PR**. |
|"Not Planned" | **Default** for PR |
| "Duplicate" | Asks for the original issue number and links to the relevant issue |
| "Other" | Shows a text box to fill (required, and max 255 characters) (shown in plain text) |

This applies to the issue/PR bulk "Close" action button, but only "completed and not planned" are the possible reasons for issues and "not planned" for PRs.

The button text will reflect the chosen reason.

**Note: The choice/reason can be changed before closing the issue or PR**.

#### Display
Show the reason on the "close timeline comment." Closed items will also show a distinct icon/label per reason for quick visual feedback.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given an open issue, when the user clicks the main Close button without opening the dropdown, then it closes as "Completed"; an open PR closed the same way closes as "Not planned".
- [ ] AC2: Given an open issue, when the user opens the Close button's dropdown, then it offers Completed, Not planned, Duplicate and Other; for a PR it offers the same list without Completed, and merging a PR still needs no reason.
- [ ] AC3: Given a reason picked from the dropdown, when the user picks a different one before closing (with or without a comment typed), then the button text shows the latest choice and that reason is the one saved.
- [ ] AC4: Given "Duplicate" is chosen, when the number entered is not an issue or PR in the same repository, or is the item itself, then the close is refused with an error message and the item stays open; a valid number closes it, and the timeline links to the original.
- [ ] AC5: Given "Other" is chosen, when the text box is empty or longer than 255 characters, then the close is refused with an error message; otherwise the text is saved and the timeline shows it as plain text, with HTML and Markdown not rendered.
- [ ] AC6: Given several open issues selected on the Issues tab, when the user bulk-closes them as Completed or Not planned, then every selected issue closes with that reason; on the Pull Requests tab, the bulk dropdown offers only Not planned.
- [ ] AC7: Given an item closed with a reason, when its timeline is viewed, then the close event states the reason, e.g. "closed this as not planned", "closed this as a duplicate of #N" or "closed this: <text>".
- [ ] AC8: Given closed items with different reasons, when viewed in the issue or PR list and on the item's page, then each reason shows its own icon or label; items closed before this feature, which have no reason, look exactly as they do today.
- [ ] AC9: Given an item closed with a reason, when it is reopened, then the list and page no longer show the reason's icon or label, and the timeline keeps the earlier close event with its reason.
- [ ] AC10: Given the new dropdown, text box, error messages and timeline text, when a page shows them in English, then each string comes from a key in `options/locale/locale_en-US.json`, and no other locale file is changed.


### Out of Scope

- Pop up icon. Will be implemented alongside the API and automated changes in issue #55  since that impacts the API layer.
- Closing reason via Gitea's automated closing services: Same as above, to be implemented in issue #55.

### Open Questions

- Should marking something as duplicate require the user to input a number (with pop ups like in the issues and PR editors), or a drop-down.

TITLE: A way to store and retrieve "closed" reasons for issues and PRs
STATE: OPEN
LABELS: enhancement, scope: medium

### User Story

As a front-end developer, I want a way to store messages detailing issue and PR close reasons in the system so that I can create a display on the front end to show the reason why an issue or PR was closed, but there is no current way to store nor recover the reason behind their closing.

### User Scenario

For a front-end developer to implement the feature, there needs to be a clear way to send and receive information, as it would be ridiculous to expect the front end to directly communicate with the DB. A central function will be implemented along with supporting infrastructure (such as a predefined list and constraints) that the user will need to implement the desired features.

The finer details on _how_ the information is stored by the system is abstracted away, and so, this single set of functionality will permit each storage and retrieval of the issue messages. This will similarly be the user story of how the API will handle the messages.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a database with existing open and closed issues and PRs, when the migration runs, then the close-reason columns exist on the issue table and every existing issue and PR has an empty reason; existing close comments, which have no close-reason metadata, also read as having no reason.
- [ ] AC2: Given an open issue, when it is closed through the close service with a valid reason (completed, not planned, duplicate or other), then both the issue and its new close timeline comment store that reason.
- [ ] AC3: Given the reason "other", when the text is empty or longer than 255 characters, then the close is rejected with its own error and the issue stays open; valid text is stored exactly as entered.
- [ ] AC4: Given the reason "duplicate", when the target number does not exist in the same repository or is the issue itself, then the close is rejected with its own error; a valid target is stored, and the close comment has the target issue loaded (number, title, link).
- [ ] AC5: Given a pull request, when it is closed as "completed", then the close is rejected with its own error; the allowed-reasons list for a PR leaves out "completed" and an issue's list includes all four.
- [ ] AC6: Given an issue closed with a reason, when it is reopened, then the issue's reason is cleared and the earlier close comment keeps its reason.
- [ ] AC7: Given any existing close path (web, bulk, commit keyword, merged PR, branch deletion, API), when it closes an issue without a reason, then the close succeeds as before with an empty reason, and merging a PR still records no reason.



### Out of Scope

UI Displaying of information: Issue (#54 )
API access: Issue (#55 )
Issues for automatic closing of issues and PRs: Issue (#55 )

Other: Note that the pop ups on the UI will not show the reason since the message won't be written to the appropriate JSON field, for now. This will be addressed in the future (issue #55) to avoid touching the API under this issue.

### Open Questions

None

### Design Decisions
See below


### Scope

medium

TITLE: Let users choose a reason when closing an issue or pull request
STATE: OPEN

## Summary
In Gitea, a closed issue or pull request is simply "closed" — there's no way to tell whether it was fixed, rejected, a duplicate, or closed for some other reason. Maintainers end up writing "closing as duplicate of #12" in comments, and anyone browsing closed items later can't tell finished work from abandoned ideas.

This feature adds a **close reason** to issues and pull requests. The reason is chosen when closing, saved in the database, and shown on the issue/PR and in its timeline. Preset reasons cover the common cases, and an **Other** option lets the user type a custom reason. Items closed automatically (by a commit, a merged PR, a deleted branch, etc.) get a sensible reason too.

This helps maintainers triage faster, and helps contributors and project managers read a project's history accurately — for example, how much was actually completed versus declined.

## User story
As a repository maintainer, I want to choose why I'm closing an issue or pull request — from a list or by typing my own reason — so that anyone reading it later knows what happened without digging through comments.

## Proposed behavior

### Closing manually (web UI)
- The **Close** button on issues becomes a split button with a dropdown:
  - **Close as completed** (default)
  - **Close as not planned**
  - **Close as duplicate** — asks for the original issue number (e.g. `#12`)
  - **Close with other reason…** — shows a text box for a custom reason (required when chosen, max 255 characters)
- The **Close pull request** button gets the same dropdown **without "Completed"**, since a finished PR is *merged*, not closed. Options: **Not planned** (default), **Duplicate**, **Other…**. Merging stays a separate state and needs no reason.
- The **issue/PR list** bulk "Close" action offers the same reason choice (preset reasons only; one reason applied to all selected items).

### Saving and display
- A database migration adds to the `issue` table (which also stores PRs):
  - `close_reason` — `completed`, `not_planned`, `duplicate`, or `other`
  - `close_reason_text` — the custom text when the reason is `other`
  - `duplicate_of_id` — the original issue/PR when the reason is `duplicate`
- The same fields are stored on the close timeline comment, so every close/reopen in the history keeps its own reason.
- The timeline shows e.g. "closed this as not planned", "closed this as a duplicate of #12", or "closed this: *custom text*".
- Custom text is displayed as plain text (escaped, not rendered as Markdown/HTML).
- Closed items show a distinct icon/label per reason (e.g. "not planned" looks different from "completed").
- **Reopening** clears the current reason (the old reason stays visible in the timeline).
- Existing closed issues/PRs have no reason and display exactly as they do today.

### Automatic closing

| How it closes | Code path | Reason saved |
|---|---|---|
| Commit message keyword ("fixes #5") | `services/issue/commit.go` | Completed |
| Merged PR that references an issue | `services/pull/merge.go` | Completed (on the referenced issue) |
| PR auto-closed because its head branch was deleted | `services/pull/pull.go` (`AdjustPullsCausedByBranchDeleted`) | Not planned |
| PRs auto-closed because the repo's branches were removed | `services/pull/pull.go` (`CloseRepoBranchesPulls`) | Not planned |
| API call that closes without giving a reason | `routers/api/v1/repo/issue.go` | Completed (issues) / Not planned (PRs) |

### API
- Issue and pull request edit endpoints accept optional `close_reason` (`completed`, `not_planned`, `duplicate`, `other`), `close_reason_text`, and `duplicate_of` fields.
- Issue and PR JSON responses include `close_reason` and `close_reason_text` (similar to GitHub's `state_reason`).
- Invalid combinations are rejected with 422 (e.g. `other` with empty text, `duplicate` pointing at a nonexistent issue, `completed` on a PR).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A database migration adds the close-reason columns; existing issues and PRs are unaffected.
- [ ] Users can pick a preset reason or type a custom one when closing an issue or PR from its page.
- [ ] PRs do not offer "Completed"; merging still works without a reason.
- [ ] The bulk close action on issue/PR lists lets users pick a preset reason.
- [ ] "Duplicate" requires a valid issue/PR number in the same repository, and the timeline links to it.
- [ ] "Other" requires non-empty text (≤ 255 chars), which is saved and displayed escaped.
- [ ] Timeline and closed-item display show the reason; all new UI strings are in `locale_en-US.json`.
- [ ] Each automatic close path saves the reason listed in the table above.
- [ ] Reopening clears the current reason but keeps it in the timeline history.
- [ ] The API accepts, validates, and returns the close-reason fields for issues and PRs.
- [ ] Unit tests cover each reason, custom-text validation, each automatic path, and the migration.

## Implementation notes
- Every close goes through `issues_model.SetIssueAsClosed` (`models/issues/issue_update.go:51`), which currently only updates `is_closed` and `closed_unix`. The reason would be added there and passed down from `issue_service.CloseIssue` (`services/issue/status.go:17`) by each caller.
- Web routes: `routers/web/repo/issue_comment.go` (Close button) and `routers/web/repo/issue_list.go` (bulk close).
- Timeline close events are `CommentTypeClose` (`models/issues/comment.go:71`).
- Close button template: `templates/repo/issue/view_content.tmpl`.
- Possible follow-up: Gitea's GitHub migration test data already contains GitHub's `state_reason`, so a later issue could import close reasons when migrating from GitHub.

## Rough scope
**Large.** It touches every layer of Gitea — a database migration, the issue/PR model and services, several automatic-close paths, web UI in two places with custom-text input, the REST API, and tests — more than a single sprint of work.

## Source
Personal use and a feature gap compared to GitHub, which supports "Close as completed / not planned / duplicate". Our own team's tracker would benefit, since the current closed state can't tell finished work from declined work.

BODY:
Closes #53

## What changed and why

Gitea records *that* an issue or pull request was closed, but not *why*. This PR adds the backend for a close reason: completed, not planned, duplicate of another issue, or other (with a short description). #54 (UI) and #55 (API) build on it.

- Issues and pull requests can store a close reason. Existing ones start with none.
- The timeline entry for each close keeps its own copy of the reason. Reopening clears the issue's current reason, but the history keeps what each close said.
- An invalid reason is refused and the issue stays open:
  - A pull request can't be closed as completed.
  - "Other" needs a description of up to 255 characters.
  - A duplicate must point to another issue in the same repository.
- Every existing way of closing works as before and records no reason.
- The router for the close form on the issue page can now error messages related to invalid close reason, following existing functionality. The front end work, thus, does not need to modify this.
- Docs in `.claude-students` are updated.

## How the changes relate to the ACs

- **AC1:** after the migration, every existing issue, pull request and close entry reads as having no reason.
- **AC2:** closing with any of the four reasons stores it on the issue and in its close entry.
- **AC3:** a description that is empty, only spaces, or longer than 255 characters is refused, and the issue stays open. A valid description is stored exactly as typed.
- **AC4:** a duplicate that doesn't exist, is the issue itself, or is in another repository is refused. A valid one is stored, and its number, title and link can be shown.
- **AC5:** a pull request can't be closed as completed; issues can use all four reasons.
- **AC6:** reopening clears the issue's reason; the earlier close entry keeps its own.
- **AC7:** existing close paths are unchanged, and a merge records no reason.

## How it was tested

Mostly unit tests against the test database, plus one integration test that submits the real close form. To confirm the tests would catch mistakes, key lines were deliberately broken one at a time, and each break made a test fail.

| AC | What the tests check |
| --- | --- |
| AC1 | The migration on existing open and closed issues and PRs; a fresh install; old close entries |
| AC2 | Closing with each reason, directly and through the web form |
| AC3 | Empty, spaces-only and too-long descriptions are refused and the issue stays open; valid text is kept as typed |
| AC4 | Self, missing and other-repository duplicates are refused; a valid one is stored and loaded; a deleted target doesn't break the page |
| AC5 | The allowed reasons for issues and PRs; a PR closed as completed is refused |
| AC6 | Reopening after "other" and after "duplicate" |
| AC7 | Merging records no reason; the existing tests for the close button, the API, merging, commit keywords and branch deletion still pass |

The tests are in `models/issues/issue_close_reason_test.go`, `models/migrations/v1_27/v343_test.go`, `services/forms/repo_form_test.go`, `services/pull/merge_test.go` and `tests/integration/issue_test.go`.


**Verification run:** an automated run passed every build, lint and test check, and a code review covered correctness, regressions, databases, security, conventions, tests and docs. It found no defects against the acceptance criteria. The minor issues it found were fixed (comment wording, one misleading error message, two missing test cases, and doc inaccuracies).

## Known limitations

- Closing with a comment and a refused reason still posts the comment. This matches how the existing "blocked by dependencies" refusal behaves. A description that is too long is the exception: the form refuses the whole request, so nothing is posted.
- If the issue a duplicate points to is deleted later, the closed issue still refers to it, and the page treats it as not found.
- For #54: the duplicate target is loaded without checking whether the viewer may see it. It is always in the same repository, but #54 should check the viewer can read issues or pull requests before showing it.
- For #54 and #55: the reason names are only mapped on the web form. The API will need the same mapping.
- The 255-character limit uses Gitea's standard form length rule (`MaxSize`), which counts characters. MSSQL counts an emoji as two, so on MSSQL only, a description of more than about 127 emoji passes that rule but is too long for the column.


## AI assistance

Claude code draft the code, tests, docs and other changes. I made the decisions, refused to let claude commit on my behalf, and made commits as small as possible so I can review them. AI log present on the original issue #53.

PR written through back and forth between human and AI.

# Course workflow — issues, PRs, reviews, sprint deliverables

Course rules, not upstream Gitea ones. Source: the course site <https://csci-435-se.github.io/>
(Sprints pages) and `docs/sprint0/standards.md`. Everyone on the team, and every AI session, uses
the formats below so all issues and PRs look the same. The GitHub templates in `.github/` carry the
same formats; if they ever disagree with this page, fix the template.

AI disclosure has its own page: `AI-ASSISTANCE.md`.

## Current sprint: Sprint 1

- **Dates:** Sep 22 – Oct 8, 2026. Everything pushed and merged by **Oct 8, 11:59 PM**.
- **Points:** 100 (10% of the course grade).
- **Zero rule:** no merged PR (D4), no sprint report (D6) or no release (D7) means **0 for the
  whole sprint**.
- **Carries forward:** every Sprint 0 standard and convention still applies.

| # | Deliverable | Points | Who | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | Sprint backlog: a `Sprint 1` milestone with every selected issue on it | 10 | Team | GitHub milestone |
| D2 | Requirements spec for each issue (formats below), peer-reviewed by a teammate | 20 | Individual | Issue body |
| D3 | At least one non-trivial design decision per issue | 7 | Individual | Issue body |
| D4 | Code changes and PRs | 36 | Individual | PRs |
| D5 | AI logs | 7 | Individual | `ai-logs/sprint1/<github-username>/` |
| D6 | Sprint report | 10 | Team | `docs/sprint1/report.md` |
| D7 | Release: tag `v1.27.3-csci435-s1` plus a GitHub release | 2 | Team | Tags / Releases |
| D8 | Reflection survey | 8 | Individual | Blackboard/Zulip link |

- **D1 load:** each CSCI 435 student owns at least 2 medium issues; each CSCI 535 student owns at
  least 2 medium and 1 small. Every issue has exactly **one** assignee. Specs should be final by
  Sep 27.
- **D5:** conventions are in `ai-logs/README.md`. The folder must exist even if no AI was used. In
  that case, post an issue comment saying so. Log links go in **issue comments only**, never in PRs
  (`AI-ASSISTANCE.md`).
- **D7:** keep Sprint 0's base version (`v1.27.3-csci435-s0` → `v1.27.3-csci435-s1`), push the tag
  to origin, and write release notes listing the features, fixes and improvements.
- **Reviews:** each student reviews at least one PR per sprint. Over the semester, each student
  reviews every teammate at least once.
- **Extra credit:** up to 3 points per PR accepted by upstream Gitea.

## Branches and commits

- Branches: `feat/issue-<N>-short-description`, `fix/issue-<N>-short-description` or
  `chore/short-description` (`STUDENTS.md`). One issue per branch.
- Commit messages follow Conventional Commits and end with the issue number:
  `feat(repo): show empty state on releases page (#17)`. Add an
  `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer when AI helped; never `Co-Authored-By` or
  `Signed-off-by` (`AGENTS.md`). A human approves every commit before it is made.

### Before each implementation: sync with main

Every new branch starts from an up-to-date `main`. AI sessions run this before writing any code:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git switch -c feat/issue-<N>-short-description
```

To pick up new work on `main` for a branch that already exists, **merge, don't rebase**. Rebasing
or squashing after review has started is not allowed (`docs/sprint0/standards.md`):

```bash
git fetch origin
git merge origin/main
```

Do this before opening the PR and again if `main` moves while it is in review. Never merge another
feature branch into yours.

### After merge: clean up

A PR is merged with a merge commit once it is approved, every review comment is addressed and CI
passes. Then:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git branch -d feat/issue-<N>-short-description               # local branch
git push origin --delete feat/issue-<N>-short-description    # or GitHub's "Delete branch" button
git fetch --prune                                            # drop stale remote-tracking refs
```

Also check that the issue closed (via `Closes #N`), is on the sprint milestone, and has its AI
Assistance comment. Then run `specstory sync` and file the session's log (see `ai-logs/README.md`).

## Issue format: feature (user story)

Template: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/user-story.yaml`. The user story must meet INVEST: Independent,
Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable.

```markdown
## User Story
As a <role>, I want <capability> so that <benefit>.

## User Scenario
<A short concrete walk-through: who, where in the UI, what they do, what they see.>

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given <state>, when <action>, then <observable result>.
- [ ] AC2: ...
- [ ] AC3: ...            (at least 3; each has a clear pass/fail result)

## Out of Scope
- <What this issue deliberately does not do.>

## Open Questions
- <Unresolved questions, or "None".>

## Design Decision
**Decision:** <what was chosen>
**Alternatives Considered:** <at least one other option>
**Rationale:** <why this one>
**Consequences:** <trade-offs, follow-up work, what it makes harder>

## Scope
small | medium | large, and matching `scope:` label
```

## Issue format: bug report

Template: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug-report.yaml`.

```markdown
## Observed Behavior
## Expected Behavior
## Steps to Reproduce
1. ...
## Additional Information
<Version or commit, browser/OS, logs, screenshots.>
## Design Decision
<Same four fields as above: Decision, Alternatives Considered, Rationale, Consequences.>
```

- **Design Decision (D3):** fill it in once you've picked an approach, before opening the PR. Put
  a second decision under another `### Decision 2` heading. If a PR changes the decision, update
  the issue body.
- **Peer review (D2):** a teammate reads the spec and comments `Spec reviewed — <notes>` on the
  issue before implementation starts.

## Pull request format

Template: `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Title uses Conventional Commits, e.g.
`fix(issues): keep label filter after search`. Description sections:

1. `Closes #<N>`, which links the issue and closes it on merge.
2. **What changed:** the change in your own words.
3. **Why:** the problem, and which acceptance criteria (AC1…) it satisfies.
4. **How it was tested / Test strategy:** tests added or updated and why these ones. Name any
   change that can't be tested automatically and how it was checked by hand. Every behaviour change
   needs a new or updated test.
5. **CI / manual verification:** CI status, or the commands run and their results.
6. **Design:** one line pointing at the Design Decision in the issue, or a note on how it changed.
7. **AI assistance:** format in `AI-ASSISTANCE.md` §2, with **no log link**.

Per-PR grading (20 points): correctness against the acceptance criteria 6, test strategy with
explanation 5, description quality 4, CI or manual verification 3, review rubric posted 2.

## Code review rubric

The reviewer posts this as a **PR comment**, as well as the GitHub review itself. A copy-paste copy
is in `.github/code-review-rubric.md`, so keep the two in sync. Pull the branch and test it when you
can, say what you checked, and mark each point as required or optional
(`docs/community-governance.md`). Score each row against the issue's acceptance criteria. Anything
below 7 needs a note saying what would raise it.

```markdown
### Code Review — @reviewer-username

**Checked:** <what you ran or tried>

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correctness — implements issue requirements | | |
| Test coverage — tests present and meaningful | | |
| Code quality — style, naming, no duplication | | |
| Documentation — comments and PR description clear | | |
| AI transparency — evidence of human verification if AI used | | |
| Overall — merge as-is? | | |
```

## Sprint report (D6) sections

`docs/sprint<N>/report.md`, following `docs/sprint0/report.md`:

- Team: names, GitHub usernames, project name, repository link.
- Sprint overview.
- Backlog: milestone link, plus a table of title, owner, points, scope and status.
- Requirements and design: when specs were done, what surprised you, design rationale.
- Completed issues: title, owner, PR link, author, reviewer, what changed.
- Test strategy, including untestable changes and why.
- AI tool usage per member: tools, session count, AI log folder link, and 2–3 sentences on lessons
  learned.
- Release: tag and release link.
- Risks and retrospective: what worked, what slowed the team down, Sprint 2 changes.
- Sprint 2 plan: initial ideas and carryover issues.

# AI assistance disclosure — required format

Course rule, not an upstream Gitea one. Every contributor discloses their own AI use per issue,
**even when no AI was used**. Source: the course AI Log Instructions page and `CONTRIBUTING.md`
(AI Contribution Policy). Two separate places, both required. The rest of the PR and issue
format is in `COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`.

## 1. A comment on the issue

Posted by each contributor on the **issue** they worked, once their work is done. One comment per
person — never edit someone else's. Add later sessions by editing your own table.

```markdown
### AI Assistance — @your-github-username

**Role in this issue:** Implementation

| # | Tool | Log | What AI helped with |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | claude-code | [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/blob/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md) | Confirmed the files found during concept location, drafted the template change and tests, ran them |

**Attachments:** [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl/](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/tree/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl)
```

- **Role** is one of Implementation, Code review, Testing, Other — pick the ones that apply and
  delete the rest, do not leave the slash list in place.
- **Tool** is the tool's name, e.g. `claude-code`, `claude-web`.
- **Log** is a full `https://github.com/...` link to the filed log. Relative paths break in issue
  comments. File naming is in `ai-logs/README.md`.
- **Attachments** only when the log has a companion folder; otherwise drop the line.
- **No AI used?** Keep the heading and role line and write `No AI used` in place of the table.

## 2. A short section in the pull request description — no log link

Reviewers read the PR, and the review rubric scores "AI transparency", so the PR says how AI was
used and how you verified it. It does **not** link or cite the AI log: from Sprint 1 on, logs are
referenced in **issue comments only**, never in PR descriptions or PR comments (Sprint 1 page, D5).

```markdown
## AI assistance

Claude Code (claude-opus-5) drafted the handler and tests following the existing register/delete
code; I reviewed every line, ran the tests, checked the page by hand, and can explain each change.
AI log: see the AI Assistance comment on the linked issue.
```

Name the model, say what AI did and what you did, and point at the issue comment for the log.

## Rules that make a disclosure wrong

- **Placeholders left in**: `@your-github-username` or the full `Implementation / Code review /
  Testing / Other` list means the comment was pasted unread.
- **A log link in a PR description or PR comment.** Log links live in the issue comment only.
- **A log link that 404s.** Until the log is merged to `main`, link the branch that holds it; switch
  to the `main` link once merged.
- **A log folder that is not your GitHub username** — `ai-logs/sprint1/jdonohue/` is wrong when the
  account is `Jack-Donohue`.
- **Claiming work AI did as your own, or the reverse.** The claim must match the log.
- **AI-written replies to reviewer questions on your own issue or PR.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` forbids it:
  the questions are for you.

## For AI agents drafting an issue or PR

Put section 2 in every PR description you draft, and draft the section 1 issue comment
separately, both filled in from the session you actually ran — never with placeholders. You may
draft the wording, but say plainly that the human must review and edit it before posting, and leave
the issue comment for them to post under their own account.
==========
# AI Logs

This folder holds every AI session for each sprint, one folder per student. The course rules are on
the [AI Log Instructions](https://csci-435-se.github.io/ai-logs/) page and the current sprint page
at <https://csci-435-se.github.io/>. This README is the team's shared convention for following them.

## What to log

Every AI session tied to this project: code, debugging, tests, reviews, drafting issues and PRs,
design discussion, the sprint report. That includes sessions that went nowhere. Purely academic
questions unrelated to the project don't need logging.

## Structure

```
ai-logs/
  sprint1/
    <github-username>/                          ← exact GitHub username, matching case
      .gitkeep                                  ← the folder must exist even if you used no AI
      YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md
      YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>/           ← attachments (images, etc.), optional
```

Team folders: `ab-wm`, `arjunsb26`, `CarsonRackley`, `controlled-opposition`, `Jack-Donohue`,
`vvchopra`.

## Naming

`YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`

- **Date:** the day the session started.
- **Sprint folder:** the sprint that date falls in, not the sprint the work is for.
- **Tool:** one of the course identifiers: `claude-code`, `claude-web`, `claude-desktop`, `cursor`,
  `gemini-cli`, `codex-cli`, `copilot`, `chatgpt`, `other-<name>`. Claude Code run inside VS Code is
  `claude-code`.
- **Slug:** lowercase words joined with hyphens that say what the session did. Put the issue number
  first when there is one: `issue-52-impl`, `issue-52-spec`, `pr-61-review`, `sprint1-report`.
  Replace auto-generated slugs such as `local-command-caveat...`.
- **Formats:** `.md` is preferred; `.txt` and `.json` are also accepted. No `.docx`, `.pdf`, `.html`
  or share links.

## Capturing a session

| Tool | How |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code (terminal or VS Code), other agentic CLIs | Start it with [SpecStory](https://specstory.com/): `specstory run claude`, from the repo root. Forgot? Run `specstory sync` afterwards; it back-fills from Claude Code's local history. Then copy from `.specstory/history/` (git-ignored) into your folder and rename it to the convention. |
| Web chat (claude.ai, ChatGPT, Gemini, ...) | Install a browser chat exporter and export the session as Markdown right after it ends. Include any files you pasted in as context. |
| Claude Desktop | SpecStory doesn't capture it. Copy the conversation into a `.md` file by hand. |

At the end of each sprint, run `specstory sync` once more and re-copy. A log copied mid-session is
incomplete.

## Content

- The **tool and AI model** used (SpecStory writes both).
- The **complete** prompt and response history. For agentic tools, that includes file edits and
  commands (SpecStory includes them). Logs with missing responses or truncated histories are
  **invalid**. Don't hand-write, summarise or trim a log; only rename it.
- Attachments (screenshots, snippets) go in a folder with the log's name minus `.md`.
- Log **every** session, including ones that went nowhere. Grading is on how complete the record
  is, not on whether AI helped.

## Where logs are referenced

- **Issue comments only.** Each contributor posts their own `### AI Assistance — @username` comment
  on the issue, with full `https://github.com/...` links to their logs. Format:
  [`.claude-students/AI-ASSISTANCE.md`](../.claude-students/AI-ASSISTANCE.md).
- **Not** in PR descriptions or PR comments. The PR has a short AI-use note with no log link. The
  AI Log Instructions page says "Issue/PR comments", but the Sprint 1 page narrows this to issue
  comments only, and the sprint page wins.
- Each teammate posts their own comment, including reviewers who used AI to review.
- No AI used? Post an issue comment saying so, and keep your folder with its `.gitkeep`.
- The sprint report lists each member's tools, session count, folder link, and 2–3 sentences on
  lessons learned.

95	# Workflow authoring reference
96	A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.
97	When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.
98	Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
99	- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
100	- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
101	- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
102	- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
103	- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify
104	For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.
105	**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workf
106	Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.
107	Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
108	  export const meta = {
109	    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
110	    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
111	    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
112	      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
113	      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
114	    ],
115	  }
116	  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
117	  phase('Scan')
118	  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
119	  ...
120	The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.
121	Script body hooks:
122	- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns
123	- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
124	- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
125	- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
126	- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
127	- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
128	- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or stati
129	- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unk
130	Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
131	Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().
132	Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.
133	Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.
134	Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.
135	DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.
136	A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
137	- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
138	- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
139	- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison
140	A barrier is NOT justified by:
141	- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
142	- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
143	- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.
144	Smell test: if you wrote
145	  const a = await parallel(...)
146	  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
147	  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
148	that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.
149	Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.
150	When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
151	  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
152	  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
153	  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))
154	Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
155	  const bugs = []
156	  while (bugs.length < 10) {
157	    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
158	    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
159	    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
160	  }
161	Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
162	  const bugs = []
163	  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
164	    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
165	    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
166	    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
167	  }
168	Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
169	  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
170	  let dry = 0
171	  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
172	    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
173	      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
174	    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
175	    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
176	    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
177	    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
178	      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
179	        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
180	        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
181	    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
182	  }
183	  return confirmed
184	  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.
185	Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
186	- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
187	    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
188	      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
189	    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
190	- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
191	- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
192	- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
193	- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
194	- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
195	- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.
196	Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.
197	These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).
198	Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

133	diff --git a/models/issues/issue_close_reason.go b/models/issues/issue_close_reason.go
134	new file mode 100644
135	index 0000000000..77ed1293a0
136	--- /dev/null
137	+++ b/models/issues/issue_close_reason.go
138	@@ -0,0 +1,141 @@
139	+// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
140	+// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
141	+
142	+package issues
143	+
144	+import (
145	+	"fmt"
146	+	"slices"
147	+	"strings"
148	+	"unicode/utf8"
149	+
150	+	"gitea.dev/modules/util"
151	+)
152	+
153	+// CloseReason records why an issue or pull request was closed.
154	+// It is stored as an integer, so existing values must never be renumbered.
155	+type CloseReason int
156	+
157	+const (
158	+	CloseReasonNone       CloseReason = iota // 0
159	+	CloseReasonCompleted                     // 1
160	+	CloseReasonNotPlanned                    // 2
161	+	CloseReasonDuplicate                     // 3
162	+	CloseReasonOther                         // 4
163	+)
164	+
165	+// CloseReasonUnknown is never stored: it stands for an unrecognised reason name, so that Validate rejects it.
166	+const CloseReasonUnknown CloseReason = -1
167	+
168	+// CloseReasonTextMaxLength matches the VARCHAR(255) close_reason_text column and the close form's MaxSize(255)
169	+// rule. Validate counts characters the same way MaxSize does, so paths that skip the form get the same limit.
170	+// MSSQL's NVARCHAR counts UTF-16 units instead, so text with many emoji can pass this limit and still not fit.
171	+const CloseReasonTextMaxLength = 255
172	+
173	+// AllowedCloseReasons lists the reasons a person can pick when closing.
174	+// A pull request is completed by merging, so it cannot be closed as completed.
175	+func AllowedCloseReasons(isPull bool) []CloseReason {
176	+	if isPull {
177	+		return []CloseReason{CloseReasonNotPlanned, CloseReasonDuplicate, CloseReasonOther}
178	+	}
179	+	return []CloseReason{CloseReasonCompleted, CloseReasonNotPlanned, CloseReasonDuplicate, CloseReasonOther}
180	+}
181	+
182	+// CloseReasonOptions is the reason a person gives when closing an issue or pull request.
183	+type CloseReasonOptions struct {
184	+	Reason         CloseReason
185	+	Text           string // only for CloseReasonOther
186	+	DuplicateIndex int64  // only for CloseReasonDuplicate: the number of the issue it duplicates, in the same repository
187	+}
188	+
189	+// Validate checks the options for an issue or pull request, without looking anything up;
190	+// SetIssueAsClosed checks that the duplicate target exists.
191	+// No reason at all is valid, so close paths that give none keep working.
192	+func (opts CloseReasonOptions) Validate(isPull bool) error {
193	+	if opts.Reason != CloseReasonNone && !slices.Contains(AllowedCloseReasons(isPull), opts.Reason) {
194	+		return ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed{Reason: opts.Reason, IsPull: isPull}
195	+	}
196	+
197	+	if opts.Reason == CloseReasonDuplicate {
198	+		if opts.DuplicateIndex <= 0 {
199	+			return ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate{Index: opts.DuplicateIndex, Detail: "no issue number given"}
200	+		}
201	+	} else if opts.DuplicateIndex != 0 {
202	+		return ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate{Index: opts.DuplicateIndex, Detail: "an issue number is only allowed with the duplicate reason"}
203	+	}
204	+
205	+	hasText := strings.TrimSpace(opts.Text) != "" // whitespace-only counts as no text
206	+	if opts.Reason != CloseReasonOther {
207	+		if hasText {
208	+			return ErrInvalidCloseReasonText{Reason: opts.Reason, Detail: "text is only allowed with the other reason"}
209	+		}
210	+		return nil
211	+	}
212	+	if !hasText {
213	+		return ErrInvalidCloseReasonText{Reason: opts.Reason, Detail: "text is empty"}
214	+	}
215	+	if utf8.RuneCountInString(opts.Text) > CloseReasonTextMaxLength {
216	+		return ErrInvalidCloseReasonText{Reason: opts.Reason, Detail: fmt.Sprintf("text is longer than %d characters", CloseReasonTextMaxLength)}
217	+	}
218	+	return nil
219	+}
220	+
221	+// ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed represents a reason that is out of range, or not allowed for the issue or pull request.
222	+type ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed struct {
223	+	Reason CloseReason
224	+	IsPull bool
225	+}
226	+
227	+// IsErrCloseReasonNotAllowed checks if an error is a ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed.
228	+func IsErrCloseReasonNotAllowed(err error) bool {
229	+	_, ok := err.(ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed)
230	+	return ok
231	+}
232	+
233	+func (err ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed) Error() string {
234	+	return fmt.Sprintf("close reason is not allowed for this %s [reason: %d]", util.Iif(err.IsPull, "pull request", "issue"), err.Reason)
235	+}
236	+
237	+func (err ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed) Unwrap() error {
238	+	return util.ErrInvalidArgument
239	+}
240	+
241	+// ErrInvalidCloseReasonText represents close reason text that is empty, too long, or sent with a reason other than CloseReasonOther.
242	+type ErrInvalidCloseReasonText struct {
243	+	Reason CloseReason
244	+	Detail string
245	+}
246	+
247	+// IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText checks if an error is a ErrInvalidCloseReasonText.
248	+func IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText(err error) bool {
249	+	_, ok := err.(ErrInvalidCloseReasonText)
250	+	return ok
251	+}
252	+
253	+func (err ErrInvalidCloseReasonText) Error() string {
254	+	return fmt.Sprintf("invalid close reason text: %s [reason: %d]", err.Detail, err.Reason)
255	+}
256	+
257	+func (err ErrInvalidCloseReasonText) Unwrap() error {
258	+	return util.ErrInvalidArgument
259	+}
260	+
261	+// ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate represents a duplicate target that is missing, is the issue itself, or is not in the same repository.
262	+type ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate struct {
263	+	Index  int64
264	+	Detail string
265	+}
266	+
267	+// IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate checks if an error is a ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate.
268	+func IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate(err error) bool {
269	+	_, ok := err.(ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate)
270	+	return ok
271	+}
272	+
273	+func (err ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate) Error() string {
274	+	return fmt.Sprintf("invalid duplicate target: %s [index: %d]", err.Detail, err.Index)
275	+}
276	+
277	+func (err ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate) Unwrap() error {
278	+	return util.ErrInvalidArgument
279	+}

304	+func TestIssueCloseReasonPersists(t *testing.T) {
305	+	require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
306	+
307	+	other := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 1})
308	+	assert.Equal(t, issues_model.CloseReasonNone, other.CloseReason) // fixtures set no reason, so this is the column default
309	+	assert.Empty(t, other.CloseReasonText)
310	+	assert.Zero(t, other.CloseDuplicateIssueID)
311	+
312	+	other.CloseReason = issues_model.CloseReasonOther
313	+	other.CloseReasonText = "superseded by a new design"
314	+	require.NoError(t, issues_model.UpdateIssueCols(t.Context(), other, "close_reason", "close_reason_text"))
315	+
316	+	duplicate := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 2})
317	+	duplicate.CloseReason = issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate
318	+	duplicate.CloseDuplicateIssueID = 1
319	+	require.NoError(t, issues_model.UpdateIssueCols(t.Context(), duplicate, "close_reason", "close_duplicate_issue_id"))
320	+
321	+	// reload and compare: bean conditions skip unmapped and zero-valued fields, so they can't catch a missing column
322	+	other = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 1})
323	+	assert.Equal(t, issues_model.CloseReasonOther, other.CloseReason)
324	+	assert.Equal(t, "superseded by a new design", other.CloseReasonText)
325	+
326	+	duplicate = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 2})
327	+	assert.Equal(t, issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate, duplicate.CloseReason)
328	+	assert.EqualValues(t, 1, duplicate.CloseDuplicateIssueID)
329	+}

345	+func TestCloseReasonOptionsValidate(t *testing.T) {
346	+	cases := []struct {
347	+		name   string
348	+		opts   issues_model.CloseReasonOptions
349	+		isPull bool
350	+		isErr  func(error) bool // nil when the options are valid
351	+	}{
352	+		{name: "no reason", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{}},
353	+		{name: "no reason on a pull request", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{}, isPull: true},
354	+		{name: "completed issue", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonCompleted}},
355	+		{name: "not planned pull request", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonNotPlanned}, isPull: true},
356	+		{name: "duplicate with a number", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate, DuplicateIndex: 3}},
357	+		{name: "other with text", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther, Text: "superseded"}},
358	+		{name: "other with 255 two-byte characters", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther, Text: strings.Repeat("é", 255)}},
359	+		{name: "whitespace-only text with another reason", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonCompleted, Text: " "}},
360	+
361	+		{name: "completed pull request", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonCompleted}, isPull: true, isErr: issues_model.IsErrCloseReasonNotAllowed},
362	+		{name: "out of range", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: 99}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrCloseReasonNotAllowed},
363	+		{name: "other with no text", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText},
364	+		{name: "other with whitespace-only text", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther, Text: " \t\n"}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText},
365	+		{name: "other with 256 characters", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther, Text: strings.Repeat("a", 256)}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText},
366	+		{name: "text with another reason", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonNotPlanned, Text: "because"}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText},
367	+		{name: "text with no reason", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Text: "because"}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText},
368	+		{name: "duplicate with no number", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate},
369	+		{name: "duplicate with a negative number", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate, DuplicateIndex: -1}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate},
370	+		{name: "number with another reason", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonNotPlanned, DuplicateIndex: 3}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate},
371	+		{name: "number with no reason", opts: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{DuplicateIndex: 3}, isErr: issues_model.IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate},
372	+	}
373	+	for _, c := range cases {
374	+		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
375	+			err := c.opts.Validate(c.isPull)
376	+			if c.isErr == nil {
377	+				assert.NoError(t, err)
378	+				return
379	+			}
380	+			assert.True(t, c.isErr(err), "unexpected error: %v", err)
381	+			assert.ErrorIs(t, err, util.ErrInvalidArgument)
382	+		})
383	+	}
384	+}

394	+		{name: "other with text", reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther, Text: "superseded"}, wantText: "superseded"},
395	+		{name: "other text is stored as entered", reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther, Text: "  superseded by #4  "}, wantText: "  superseded by #4  "},
396	+		{name: "whitespace-only text is not stored", reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonNotPlanned, Text: " "}},
397	+	}

409	+			assert.True(t, issue.IsClosed)

411	+
412	+			comment = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Comment{ID: comment.ID}) // reloaded, so the metadata went through JSON
413	+			assert.Equal(t, issues_model.CommentTypeClose, comment.Type)
414	+			assert.Equal(t, want, comment.MetaCloseReason())
415	+		})

480	+func TestReopenIssueClearsReason(t *testing.T) {
481	+	cases := []struct {
482	+		name   string
483	+		reason issues_model.CloseReasonOptions
484	+	}{
485	+		{name: "other with text", reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOther, Text: "superseded"}},
486	+		{name: "duplicate", reason: issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Reason: issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate, DuplicateIndex: 4}},
487	+	}
488	+	for _, c := range cases {
489	+		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
490	+			require.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())
491	+			issue := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 1})
492	+			doer := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
493	+
494	+			closeComment, err := issues_model.CloseIssue(t.Context(), issue, doer, c.reason)
495	+			require.NoError(t, err)
496	+			reopenComment, err := issues_model.ReopenIssue(t.Context(), issue, doer)
497	+			require.NoError(t, err)
498	+
499	+			issue = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 1})
500	+			assert.False(t, issue.IsClosed)
501	+			assert.Equal(t, issues_model.CloseReasonNone, issue.CloseReason)
502	+			assert.Empty(t, issue.CloseReasonText)
503	+			assert.Zero(t, issue.CloseDuplicateIssueID)
504	+
505	+			closeComment = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Comment{ID: closeComment.ID})
506	+			assert.Equal(t, c.reason.Reason, closeComment.MetaCloseReason().Reason, "the close comment keeps its reason")
507	+			assert.Equal(t, c.reason.Text, closeComment.MetaCloseReason().Text)
508	+			require.NoError(t, closeComment.LoadCloseDuplicateIssue(t.Context()))
509	+			assert.Equal(t, c.reason.Reason == issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate, closeComment.CloseDuplicateIssue != nil)
510	+
511	+			reopenComment = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Comment{ID: reopenComment.ID})
512	+			assert.Equal(t, issues_model.CommentTypeReopen, reopenComment.Type)
513	+			assert.Nil(t, reopenComment.CommentMetaData)
514	+		})
515	+	}
516	+}

879	 // CloseIssue close an issue.
880	+// It records no reason and is kept for backwards compatibility: callers with no reason to give keep using it,
881	+// such as commit keywords, merged pull requests closing the issues they reference, bulk close and the API.

=================== docs/templates.md
---

# templates — the Go HTML templates and their helpers

**Read when:** editing a page's markup, adding a template, or needing a template function.
**Not here:** the handler that renders it -> `routers-web.md`; classes -> `frontend-css.md`; behaviour -> `frontend-js.md`.

## Responsibilities

Server-rendered HTML, composed with Go's `html/template`. `modules/templates` owns the renderer and
every function templates can call.

| Directory | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `base/` | the page skeleton: `head.tmpl`, `head_script.tmpl`, `head_navbar.tmpl`, `footer.tmpl`, `paginate.tmpl`, `alert.tmpl` |
| `shared/` | reusable partials: `issuelist.tmpl` and its row partial `issuelist_items.tmpl`, `combomarkdowneditor.tmpl`, `actions/`, `secrets/`, `webhook/`, `user/` |
| `repo/`, `user/`, `org/`, `admin/`, `explore/`, `projects/`, `package/` | one directory per page area |
| `mail/` | email bodies |
| `status/` | error pages |
| `devtest/` | the `/devtest` component gallery, also driven by the e2e tests |
| `custom/` | site-admin override hooks — intentionally near-empty |
| `swagger/` | the generated API spec (`v1_json.tmpl`), see `routers-api-v1.md` |

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `modules/templates/helper.go` | `newFuncMapWebPage` — the whole set of page template functions, including `dict`, `Iif` and `Eval` |
| `modules/templates/util_render.go`, `util_render_comment.go` | markup and comment rendering helpers |
| `modules/templates/util_date.go`, `util_avatar.go`, `util_string.go`, `util_slice.go`, `util_dict.go` | the rest of the function set, grouped by kind |
| `modules/templates/htmlrenderer.go` | `TplName` and the renderer |
| `modules/templates/scopedtmpl/` | the scoped-template machinery behind partial rendering |
| `templates/base/head_script.tmpl` | emits `window.config`, including `pageData` |

## Conventions & invariants

- A template is addressed by its path under `templates/` without the extension, as a
  `templates.TplName` constant in the handler — `"repo/issue/list"` is
  `templates/repo/issue/list.tmpl` (`routers-web.md`).
- **The handler's `ctx.Data` is the only data channel.** A template cannot reach anything the
  handler did not put there, and `ctx.RootData` inside a template context is that same data.
- Data destined for JavaScript goes through `ctx.PageData`, which `base/head_script.tmpl` emits as
  `window.config.pageData` — a separate channel from `ctx.Data`.
- **Every user-visible string is a locale key**, written `{{ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.issues.new"}}` or
  `ctx.Locale.TrN` for plurals. Never a literal. Keys are added only to
  `options/locale/locale_en-US.json`; the other locales come from Crowdin.
- Composition is `{{template "base/head" .}}` style includes. New shared markup goes in `shared/`,
  not copied between areas.
- `dict` is lowercase for historical reasons; new template functions get uppercase names
  (`helper.go` says so at the definition).
- `dict` treats the key `"."` specially: `dictMerge` in `modules/templates/util_dict.go` flattens
  that argument's map into the new one. So `dict "." $ "Issues" $subset` hands a partial the whole
  root context with one key replaced — but `"." $` **must come first**, or the merge overwrites the
  replacement instead. `templates/repo/issue/list_grouped.tmpl` renders each group this way.
- Mail templates use a different, smaller function set — `mailBodyFuncMap` and
  `mailSubjectTextFuncMap` in `modules/templates/mail.go`. A helper added for pages is not
  available in `templates/mail/`.
- Class attributes are written as one readable unit including their conditionals
  (`frontend-css.md`).
- Hook frontend behaviour up declaratively with `data-global-init` / `data-global-click`
  attributes rather than inline script (`frontend-js.md`).
- `.tmpl` files are tab-indented (`.editorconfig`).

## Recipes

**Add a page's template.** Create the `.tmpl` under the matching area directory, include
`base/head` and `base/footer`, declare the `TplName` constant in the handler, and add every string
as a locale key.

**Share markup between pages.** Put the partial in `templates/shared/` and include it from both
places. Two near-identical partials in two area directories is the thing to avoid.

**Add a template function.** Add it to the map returned by `newFuncMapWebPage` in
`modules/templates/helper.go` and implement it in the matching `util_*.go`. Prefer passing prepared data from the handler — a function that
does database work at render time is a performance bug.

**See a component in isolation.** Run Gitea in development mode and open `/devtest`.

## Gotchas

- A misspelled key in `ctx.Data` renders as empty, not as an error. Check the handler when
  something is silently blank.
- A missing locale key renders the key itself — visible, but easy to miss in a rarely-hit branch.
- `templates/swagger/v1_json.tmpl` is generated. Edit the swagger comments and run
  `make generate-swagger` instead (`routers-api-v1.md`).
- `templates/custom/` is for deployment overrides, not a place to put course code.

## Related

- `routers-web.md` — `TplName` and `ctx.Data`
- `frontend-css.md`, `frontend-js.md` — the classes and attributes used here
