Yes, I went along with you. Having checked the code, your reason for B doesn't hold up against how Gitea handles defaults.

## What Gitea does

Gitea has a layered pattern for "which option does a button start on", and the page never makes that choice itself:

- **The merge button.** Which merge style it starts on comes from the server.
  - The code has a built-in fallback: "merge" (`models/repo/repo_unit.go`).
  - A site admin can change it in `app.ini` (`DEFAULT_MERGE_STYLE`), and a repo admin can change it in the repo's settings.
  - The page handler checks that the chosen style is actually allowed, then hands it to the page. The page only displays it.
- **The "Update branch" split button**, the one we're copying, works the same way. There's a built-in fallback, a repo setting on top of it, and the page handler picks the main option (`routers/web/repo/issue_view.go`). The template just displays it.

## On "no consumer can change it"

A default on the server doesn't lock anyone in:
- Any consumer can always send a reason explicitly.
- A consumer can even keep its own default. The API's update-branch endpoint deliberately uses "merge" rather than the repo's default, so older API clients keep working (`routers/api/v1/repo/pull.go`). That also answers your API question: if #55 wants different behaviour, it can have it.

If the need to change the default ever does come up, Gitea's usual answer is a setting layered on the built-in default. That only works when the default already lives on the server. A default written into the template would have to be moved there first.

## The case for B

There's one consumer today, no setting is planned, and it's one line in the template. That's a fair argument for writing less code. It isn't an argument for more flexibility, though, which was your reason for choosing it.

## My recommendation

Follow Gitea's pattern: a built-in default kept next to the reasons, which the page handler passes to the page. That was the original option A. Adding a setting in #54 would be scope creep, but this is where one would plug in later.

It's your call: keep B, or switch to A. Step 1 is the same either way, because the default only shows up in step 2. I'll update Decision 2 once you've decided.

```text
<!-- markdownlint-disable MD029 -->
<!-- Rules are numbered continuously 1-15 across the sections below; check.sh error
     messages and all 34 docs cite them by number, so the sequence must not restart. -->

# Maintenance rules

Five people maintain one shared set of docs. These rules exist so the set stays *one* set. Read
them before editing anything in `.claude-students/`. Rules marked **[checked]** are enforced by
`./.claude-students/check.sh`.

## Scope discipline

1. **Upstream wins.** `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/guidelines-*.md` are authoritative.
   Docs here summarise them and link to them; they never restate a rule differently and never
   contradict one. A contradiction is a bug in this folder, not in the project.
2. **One fact, one home.** Every fact lives in exactly one doc — the one whose `scope:` owns that
   path. Everywhere else, link to it. Duplicated facts are how five maintainers end up with five
   different answers.
3. **Durability test.** Record a fact only if it (a) took more than one discovery step to find and
   (b) will still be true after the next upstream merge. A one-off workaround, a sprint detail or
   anything about your own task fails this test — that belongs in `ai-logs/`.
4. **No process notes.** No TODOs, no open questions, no first person, no student names, no dates
   other than `verified-at`. This is a map of the code, not a journal.

## Form

5. **Template only [checked].** Use the `## ` headings from `_TEMPLATE.md`, all of them, in that
   order, with nothing added. If a section has nothing to say, write one line saying so.
6. **120-line cap [checked].** Going over means the scope is too broad. Split the doc, and add the
   new `INDEX.md` row in the same commit. `INDEX.md` itself is capped at 60 lines.
7. **Cite or delete [checked, partially].** Every claim names a repo path. A claim with no path is
   unverifiable by the next reader — delete it.
8. **Symbols, not line numbers [checked].** Write `models/db/context.go` → `WithTx`, never
   `models/db/context.go:143`. Line numbers rot at the next upstream merge and a stale number is
   worse than no number. Code fences stay at 10 lines or fewer — point at the file instead of
   copying it.
9. **Repo-relative paths [checked].** `models/db/context.go`, never `/home/you/gitea/models/...`.
10. **Whitespace [checked].** No trailing whitespace, LF endings, final newline — same as the rest
    of the repo (`.editorconfig`).

## Change control

11. **One universal set.** These docs live on `main` and nowhere else. Never keep a personal copy,
    a per-student folder, or a long-lived branch of them.
12. **Changes land by PR**, titled `docs(context): <subject>` per `AGENTS.md` Conventional Commits,
    with an `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer and no `Co-Authored-By` or
    `Signed-off-by`.
13. **Fix in place.** If you discover while working that a doc is wrong or incomplete, correct it
    in the *same* PR as your code change and update `verified-at` to the commit you checked
    against. Leaving a doc stale for someone else to hit is the exact failure this folder exists to
    prevent. This rule applies to AI sessions too.
14. **New docs need three things in one commit [checked]:** the file, its `INDEX.md` row, and a
    `scope:` that does not overlap any existing doc's. If the scope overlaps, you wanted to edit
    that doc, not add one.
15. **`./.claude-students/check.sh` passes before you push [checked].** It is dependency-free and
    finishes in under a second.

## The guide layer (rules 16-22)

`guide/` holds a plain-English page for each reference page in `docs/`, same filename. It exists so
a person new to Go and to this codebase can get oriented. It is **derived**, not independent.

16. Every guide carries `source:`, `source-hash:` and `verified-at:` in its frontmatter **[checked]**.
17. A guide's `source:` names a real `docs/*.md` with the **same filename** **[checked]**.
18. `source-hash:` is the first 16 characters of `sha256sum docs/<name>.md`. If the reference page
    changes and the guide is not regenerated, `check.sh` reports **drift** **[checked]**. Regenerating
    means: reread the reference page, rewrite the guide, update the hash and `verified-at`.
19. Guide headings match `guide/_TEMPLATE.md` exactly and in order **[checked]**.
20. Guides are capped at **200 lines**, code fences at **30** **[checked]** — teaching needs more room
    than reference does.
21. **A guide adds explanation, vocabulary and worked steps. It adds no new facts.** Every repo path
    a guide cites must also be cited by its source page **[checked]**. If you need a fact the
    reference page lacks, add it *there* first, which bumps the hash and forces the guide to be
    regenerated in the same commit — exactly the intended order.
22. `guide/START-HERE.md` has no source page. It is exempt from rules 17, 18 and 21, and is where
    cross-cutting material lives that no single reference page owns.

**Never fix a fact in `guide/`.** If the two layers disagree, the reference page is the truth and
the guide is stale: fix `docs/`, regenerate the guide, ship both in one PR. A disagreement is a bug
report against `docs/`, not an editing job in `guide/`.

**Known limitation:** a hand-edit to a guide that only rewords prose is not mechanically
detectable. Rule 21 catches invented facts; rule 18 catches a stale guide; review catches the rest.

## Updating `verified-at`

`verified-at` is the short SHA the doc was last checked against, from `git rev-parse --short HEAD`.
Bump it whenever you confirm or correct a doc. A doc whose `verified-at` is far behind `main` has
not been checked recently — treat its details as hints and confirm them in the code before relying
on them.
```

```markdown
# Issue #54 — design decisions

Entries marked *(proposed)* are not decided yet.

### Decision 1: The reason names are kept in one place, next to the reasons

**Decision:** The words the page uses for each reason (`completed`, `not_planned`, `duplicate`, `other`) are listed once, beside the reasons themselves, and every part of the page uses that list. In #53 the list lived on the close form.
**Alternatives Considered:** Keep the list on the close form, and give bulk close its own copy.
**Rationale:** The close button, bulk close and the page's menu all need the same words. With one list they can't drift apart, and #55's API can reuse it.
**Consequences:** Renaming a word breaks anything still sending the old one. Reviews keep their own list on their form, so both styles exist in the codebase.

### Decision 2: The server decides which reason the close button starts on

**Decision:** An issue's close button starts on completed and a pull request's on not planned (AC1). The default is kept next to the reasons and handed to the page by the server; the page only shows it. A close with no reason still records none.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) The page picks the default itself. (b) Treat a close with no reason as the default.
**Rationale:** This is how Gitea handles buttons that start on a choice: the merge button and the "Update branch" button both get their default from the server, from a built-in value that settings can override. It doesn't lock anyone in, since any consumer can still send a reason of its own. (a) would have to move to the server before a setting could ever change it. (b) would change what "no reason" means, and automatic closes rely on it meaning none.
**Consequences:** A setting to change the default can be added later on top of the built-in one, the way `DEFAULT_MERGE_STYLE` works for merges. The API in #55 can use the same default or keep its own, as the API's branch update already does.

```

```text
# services/forms and services/convert — request in, DTO out

**Read when:** adding a form POST to a web page, or returning a model through the API.
**Not here:** route registration -> `routers-web.md` / `routers-api-v1.md`; the DTO structs themselves live in `modules/structs`.

## Responsibilities

- `services/forms/` — one struct per HTML form, with binding and validation rules. Used only by
  the web layer.
- `services/convert/` — turns model structs into the `modules/structs` API types. Used by the API
  layer, and anywhere else an API-shaped payload is needed (webhooks, notifications).

The API layer does **not** use `services/forms`: it binds `modules/structs` option types directly.

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `services/forms/repo_form.go` | the repo/issue/PR forms, e.g. `CreateIssueForm` |
| `services/forms/user_form.go`, `auth_form.go`, `org.go`, `admin.go` | forms for the other areas |
| `services/convert/convert.go` | the general converters (`ToEmail`, `ToBranch`, `ToTag`, ...) |
| `services/convert/issue.go` | `ToAPIIssue`, `ToAPIIssueList`, `ToLabel`, `ToTrackedTime` |
| `services/convert/pull.go`, `pull_review.go`, `repository.go`, `user.go` | one file per domain |
| `modules/web/middleware/binding.go` | `Validate`, which every form's `Validate` delegates to |
| `modules/validation/binding.go` | `AddBindingRules` — registers the custom binding rules |

## Conventions & invariants

**Forms**

- A form is a plain struct with `binding:"..."` tags: `binding:"Required;MaxSize(255)"`. Field
  names map from the request through `util.ToSnakeCase` (`modules/web/middleware/binding.go`), so
  `CloseReasonText` binds `close_reason_text`. A plural acronym does not survive it —
  `AssigneeIDs` would become `assignee_i_ds` — which is why that field carries `form:"assignee_ids"`.
- A choice among named options arrives as a string, and a method on the form maps it to the
  model's integer enum, falling back to an unknown value that is then rejected:
  `SubmitReviewForm.ReviewType`, `CreateCommentForm.CloseReasonOptions` (`services/forms/repo_form.go`).
  The stored numbers never appear in the request.
- A form that needs the standard error handling implements
  `Validate(req *http.Request, errs binding.Errors) binding.Errors` and returns
  `middleware.Validate(errs, ctx.Data, f, ctx.Locale)` — copy the body from a neighbouring form
  verbatim; it is boilerplate, not a decision.
- Validation messages are locale keys, resolved through `ctx.Locale` by `middleware.Validate`.
  `validation.AddBindingRules` is called once from `registerWebRoutes` and registers the custom
  rules; a new rule goes there, not into the form.
- The route wires the form with `web.Bind(forms.XxxForm{})` and the handler reads it back with
  `web.GetForm(ctx)`, type-asserted to the form type.

**Converters**

- Naming is `To<Thing>` for the plain conversion and `To<Thing>List` for a slice. Where both an
  internal and an API-facing variant exist, the API one is `ToAPI<Thing>`.
- A converter whose output depends on permissions or needs more queries takes
  `(ctx context.Context, doer *user_model.User, model *T)` — `ToAPIIssue` is the pattern. Pass the
  real doer, never `nil`, unless the neighbouring call sites do. A pure value conversion takes just
  the model (`ToEmail`, `ToTag`).
- Converters return `modules/structs` types. They must not query for anything a caller could have
  loaded; a converter that fans out queries per item turns a list endpoint into an N+1.

## Recipes

**Add a field to a form.** Add the struct field with its `binding` tag, add the locale key for any
new validation message to `options/locale/locale_en-US.json`, then read it in the handler from
`web.GetForm(ctx)`. Existing forms have tests in `services/forms/repo_form_test.go` — extend them
rather than adding an integration test.

**Expose a new model field over the API.** Add the field to the `modules/structs` type, set it in
the matching `services/convert` function, and check whether the swagger response registration in
`routers/api/v1/swagger/` already covers the struct (it usually does). Then
`make generate-swagger`.

## Gotchas

- Two binding mechanisms with similar names: `web.Bind` (web, `services/forms` types) and the
  local `bind` helper in `routers/api/v1/api.go` (API, `modules/structs` types). Using the web one
  on an API route silently binds nothing useful.
- `web.GetForm` returns `any`. A wrong type assertion panics at request time, not compile time —
  match the type in `web.Bind` exactly.
- Adding a field to a `modules/structs` type without setting it in the converter ships a field
  that is always the zero value, and swagger will still document it as present.
- A binding error message starts with the field's label: the `locale:"…"` tag, or else the key
  `form.<FieldName>` (`modules/web/middleware/binding.go` → `Validate`). A field with a rule but no
  tag or key shows the raw key to the person; `CreateCommentForm.CloseReasonText` sets the tag.

## Related

- `routers-web.md` — where `web.Bind` is attached
- `routers-api-v1.md` — the swagger registration these DTOs need
```

```text
- Error types come in the three-part shape: `ErrIssueNotExist` struct, `IsErrIssueNotExist(err)`,
  and `Unwrap() error` returning a `modules/util` sentinel such as `util.ErrNotExist`, so
  `errors.Is` works across layers.
- Comment kinds are the `CommentType` iota in `comment.go` (`CommentTypeComment` is a plain
  comment, `CommentTypeReview` a review, plus many state-change kinds). Rendering branches on it —
  adding a value means handling it in the templates too.
- New non-index data on a comment goes in the `Comment.CommentMetaData` JSON field, not a new
  column, as its code comment in `comment.go` says. It is written once at insert and never changed,
  and SQL cannot filter or index on it.
- A close comment snapshots the issue's reason in `CommentMetaData`. Read it with
  `Comment.MetaCloseReason()` (`models/issues/comment.go`), which returns no reason when the comment has no metadata, as every
  close comment written before the columns existed does.
- A close as duplicate takes the target's per-repository number; `SetIssueAsClosed` (`models/issues/issue_update.go`) resolves it
  with `GetIssueByIndex` in the issue's own repository and stores the global ID.
  `Comment.LoadCloseDuplicateIssue` loads the target with its repository; a deleted target returns
  `ErrIssueNotExist`. Reopening (`setIssueAsReopen`, the only code that reopens) clears the issue's
  reason, text and target; the close comment keeps its snapshot.

## Recipes
```

Read the models-issues guide conventions

```text
test, and an `Unwrap()` that returns a shared sentinel like `util.ErrNotExist`. That third part is
what lets a handler ask "is this a not-found error?" without importing every model package — and it
is what turns a missing issue into a 404 instead of a 500.

**Comment kinds are an enum**, and rendering branches on it. A plain comment and a review are both
comments with different kinds, as are all the "closed this", "added a label" timeline entries.
Adding a kind means handling it in the templates too, or it renders as nothing.

**Extra data on a comment goes in its metadata, not a new column.** `Comment` has a JSON field,
`CommentMetaData`, and its code comment in `comment.go` asks for any new non-index data to go there.
It is written once, when the comment is created, and never changed — which suits a timeline, where
each entry records what was true at that moment. The cost is that SQL cannot search, sort or index
on anything inside it.

**A close comment keeps its own copy of the reason.** The issue's reason describes the *current*
close; the comment's copy, in `CommentMetaData`, describes *that* close and never changes. Read it
with `Comment.MetaCloseReason()` rather than reaching into the metadata yourself: close comments
written before this feature existed have no metadata at all, and the method turns that into "no
reason" instead of an error.

**A duplicate is typed as a number but stored as an ID.** Closing as a duplicate of `#12` looks
`#12` up in the issue's own repository (`GetIssueByIndex`, inside `SetIssueAsClosed`), so a number
from another repository is refused. What gets stored is that issue's global ID. `Comment.LoadCloseDuplicateIssue` turns the ID back into the
issue, repository included; if the target has since been deleted, it reports "not found" instead
of breaking the page.
```
</details></tool-use>

```bash
# guide/models-issues.md

old_row = "| `models/issues/issue_close_reason.go` | Why an issue or pull request was closed: the `CloseReason` values, which ones each kind may use, and the check that refuses a bad one. Saved in three columns on `Issue`. |"
new_row = "| `models/issues/issue_close_reason.go` | Why an issue or pull request was closed: the `CloseReason` values and their names, which ones each kind may use, and the check that refuses a bad one. Saved in three columns on `Issue`. |"
assert old_row in s
s = s.replace(old_row, new_row)
anchor = "**A close comment keeps its own copy of the reason.**"
para = ("**A close reason travels as a word, not a number.** The database stores each reason as a number,\n"
        "but forms and pages send its name instead: `not_planned`, not `2`. `CloseReason.String` turns a\n"
        "reason into its name and `AsCloseReason` turns a name back, the same way `CommentType.String` and\n"
        "`AsCommentType` work for comment kinds. Because pages send these names, a name can no more be\n"
        "changed than its number can.\n\n")
assert anchor in s
s = s.replace(anchor, para + anchor)
lines = s.split("\n")
assert lines[2].startswith("source-hash:") and lines[3].startswith("verified-at:")
lines[2] = "source-hash: " + srchash("models-issues")
lines[3] = "verified-at: 85a296b0ad"
open(p, "w").write("\n".join(lines))

# guide/services-forms-and-convert.md
p = ".claude-students/guide/services-forms-and-convert.md"
s = open(p).read()
old = ("**A choice arrives as a word, and the form turns it into a number.** When a person picks one of a\n"
       "few options, the request carries a name such as `approve` or `not_planned`, and a method on the\n"
       "form maps it to the model's integer enum: `SubmitReviewForm.ReviewType` and\n"
       "`CreateCommentForm.CloseReasonOptions` in `services/forms/repo_form.go`. Anything unrecognised maps\n"
       "to an \"unknown\" value that is then refused. The numbers stored in the database never travel\n"
       "through the page.\n")
new = ("**A choice arrives as a word, and the form turns it into a number.** When a person picks one of a\n"
       "few options, the request carries a name such as `approve` or `not_planned`, and a method on the\n"
       "form maps it to the model's integer enum, as `SubmitReviewForm.ReviewType` in\n"
       "`services/forms/repo_form.go` does. Anything unrecognised maps to an \"unknown\" value that is then\n"
       "refused. When other code needs the same words, the list lives in the model instead and the form\n"
       "just asks it: `CreateCommentForm.CloseReasonOptions` calls `AsCloseReason` in\n"
       "`models/issues/issue_close_reason.go`. Either way, the numbers stored in the database never travel\n"
       "through the page.\n")
assert old in s, "forms guide paragraph not found"
s = s.replace(old, new)
lines = s.split("\n")
assert lines[2].startswith("source-hash:") and lines[3].startswith("verified-at:")
lines[2] = "source-hash: " + srchash("services-forms-and-convert")
lines[3] = "verified-at: 85a296b0ad"
open(p, "w").write("\n".join(lines))
EOF
```

```text
 // CloseReasonUnknown is never stored: it stands for an unrecognised reason name, so that Validate rejects it.
 const CloseReasonUnknown CloseReason = -1
 
+// closeReasonNames are what forms and pages send instead of the stored numbers, so existing names must never change.
+// CloseReasonNone has no name: an empty name means no reason.
+var closeReasonNames = map[CloseReason]string{
+	CloseReasonCompleted:  "completed",
+	CloseReasonNotPlanned: "not_planned",
+	CloseReasonDuplicate:  "duplicate",
+	CloseReasonOther:      "other",
+}
+
+// String returns the reason's name, or "" for no reason.
+func (r CloseReason) String() string {
+	return closeReasonNames[r] // a map rather than CommentType's slice, so CloseReasonUnknown can't index out of range
+}
+
+// AsCloseReason returns the reason with the given name; an empty name means no reason,
+// and an unknown one returns CloseReasonUnknown so that Validate rejects it.
+func AsCloseReason(name string) CloseReason {
+	if name == "" {
+		return CloseReasonNone
+	}
+	for reason, reasonName := range closeReasonNames {
+		if reasonName == name {
+			return reason
+		}
+	}
+	return CloseReasonUnknown
+}
+
 // CloseReasonTextMaxLength matches the VARCHAR(255) close_reason_text column and the close form's MaxSize(255)
 // rule. Validate counts characters the same way MaxSize does, so paths that skip the form get the same limit.
 // MSSQL's NVARCHAR counts UTF-16 units instead, so text with many emoji can pass this limit and still not fit.
```

```text
  border-color: var(--color-green-dark-2);
}

.ui.buttons {
  display: inline-flex;
  flex-direction: row;
  font-size: 0;
  vertical-align: baseline;
  margin: 0 0.25em 0 0;
}

/* btn is a plain button without any opinionated styling, it only uses flex for vertical alignment like ".ui.button" in base.css */

.btn {
  background: transparent;
  border-radius: var(--border-radius);
  border: none;
  color: inherit;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
}

.btn:hover,
.btn:active {
  background: none;
  border: none;
}

a.btn,
a.btn:hover {
  color: inherit;
}

.btn.tiny {
  font-size: 12px;
}

.btn.small {
  font-size: 13px;
}

/* By default, Fomantic UI doesn't support "bordered" buttons group, but Gitea would like to use it.
And the default buttons always have borders now (not the same as Fomantic UI's default buttons, see above).
It needs some tricks to tweak the left/right borders with active state */

.ui.buttons .button {
  border-right: none;
  border-radius: 0;
  flex-shrink: 0;
  margin: 0;
}
.ui.buttons .button:first-child {
  border-left: none;
  margin-left: 0;
  border-top-left-radius: var(--border-radius);
  border-bottom-left-radius: var(--border-radius);
}
.ui.buttons .button:last-child {
  border-top-right-radius: var(--border-radius);
  border-bottom-right-radius: var(--border-radius);
}

.ui.buttons .button:hover {
  border-color: var(--color-secondary-dark-2);
}

.ui.buttons .button:hover + .button {
  border-left: 1px solid var(--color-secondary-dark-2);
}

/* TODO: these "tw-hidden" selectors are only used by "blame.tmpl" buttons: Raw/Normal View/History/Unescape, need to be refactored to a clear solution later */
.ui.buttons .button:first-child,
.ui.buttons .button.tw-hidden:first-child + .button {
  border-left: 1px solid var(--color-light-border);
}

.ui.buttons .button:last-child,
.ui.buttons .button:nth-last-child(2):has(+ .button.tw-hidden) {
  border-right: 1px solid var(--color-light-border);
}

.ui.buttons .button.active {
  border-left: 1px solid var(--color-light-border);
.ui.menu .ui.dropdown .menu .active.item {
  border-left: none;
}

/* Automatically float dropdown menu right on last menu item */
.ui.menu .right.menu .dropdown:last-child > .menu:not(.left),
.ui.menu .right.dropdown.item > .menu:not(.left),
.ui.buttons > .ui.dropdown:last-child > .menu:not(.left) {
  left: auto;
  right: 0;
}

.ui.button.dropdown .menu {
  min-width: 100%;
}
```

```text
**Give the frontend a string.** Prefer a `data-locale-<name>` attribute or the page data from the
handler. Only genuinely general text belongs in the global object, which every page loads.

## Traps, and what they look like

**A raw key like `repo.issues.new` appears in the interface.** That key is missing from the English
file. It is visible — but easy to ship if it only renders in a branch you did not click through.

**Your carefully translated French string disappears after a while.** You edited a generated locale
file. The sync overwrote it.

**Your locale change does not show up at all.** The locale files are compiled into the binary, so a
change needs a rebuild — editing the file and refreshing does nothing.

**You rename a key to something tidier and every language loses that string.** Changing a key's
*text* is fine, and translators pick it up. Changing the *key itself* invalidates every existing
translation of it, because the platform tracks strings by key. Renaming is expensive; do it only for
a real reason.

**A user sees English inside an otherwise translated page.** Either a literal was written directly,
or an error was built without the translatable wrapper.

## Where to go next

- `docs/i18n.md` (in this folder) — the reference page this was written from
- `templates.md` — where most strings are used
- `frontend-js.md` — the TypeScript side
```
</details></tool-use>

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-09-30 02:39:15Z)**_

You're right, it isn't working. It should drop down, and I missed this: my tests only checked that the menu is in the page's HTML, not that you can see it. I didn't look at it in a browser.

**Why it doesn't show:** the menu opens, but it gets clipped. The Close button row sits inside a `.field.footer` box, and `web_src/css/repo.css` gives that box `overflow: hidden`. That hides anything that sticks out of the box, including a menu that pops out below it. The "Update branch" split button I copied isn't inside that box, which is why it works there.

**Why the rule is there:** it came over in 2023 from the old Less stylesheets. In old CSS layouts, a box with floated buttons needed `overflow: hidden` to wrap around them. Both places that use `.field.footer` today (this comment form and the code-review comment form in `templates/repo/diff/comment_form.tmpl`) now lay their buttons out with flex, so the rule looks like it no longer does anything.

**How to fix it, your call:**
- **A (my recommendation): delete the rule** from `repo.css`. That's the cleanest fix, since it seems to serve no purpose anymore. The risk is that it also affects the code-review comment form, so that form needs a quick look: PR → Files changed → comment on a line.
- **B: override it only for this footer**, with a utility class on the one footer in `view_content.tmpl`. It has to be the `!important` form, because the existing rule's selector is more specific. This changes nothing else, but it leaves a rule that does nothing and adds an override to work around it.

Either way, this belongs in the step 2 commit, so hold off committing until it's fixed.

To avoid this next time: Chromium is installed, so I can check the UI myself in a headless browser before handing a step over. For that I'd need a test account on your local instance, or I can use the e2e test setup.

```text
import type {FomanticInitFunction} from '../../types.ts';
import {generateElemId, queryElems} from '../../utils/dom.ts';

const ariaPatchKey = '_giteaAriaPatchDropdown';
const fomanticDropdownFn = $.fn.dropdown;

// use our own `$().dropdown` function to patch Fomantic's dropdown module
export function initAriaDropdownPatch() {
  if ($.fn.dropdown === ariaDropdownFn) throw new Error('initAriaDropdownPatch could only be called once');
  $.fn.dropdown = ariaDropdownFn;
  $.fn.fomanticExt.onDropdownAfterFiltered = onDropdownAfterFiltered;
  (ariaDropdownFn as FomanticInitFunction).settings = fomanticDropdownFn.settings;
}

// the patched `$.fn.dropdown` function, it passes the arguments to Fomantic's `$.fn.dropdown` function, and:
// * it does the one-time element event attaching on the first call
// * it delegates the module internal functions like `onLabelCreate` to the patched functions to add more features.
function ariaDropdownFn(this: any, ...args: Parameters<FomanticInitFunction>) {
  const ret = fomanticDropdownFn.apply(this, args);

  for (let el of this) {
    // dropdown will replace '<select class="ui dropdown"/>' to '<div class="ui dropdown"><select (hidden)></select><div class="menu">...</div></div>'
    // so we need to correctly find the closest '.ui.dropdown' element, it is the real fomantic dropdown module.
    el = el.closest('.ui.dropdown');
    if (!el[ariaPatchKey]) {
      // the elements don't belong to the dropdown "module" and won't be reset
      // so we only need to initialize them once.
      attachInitElements(el);
    }

    // if the `$().dropdown()` is called without arguments, or it has non-string (object) argument,
    // it means that such call will reset the dropdown "module" including internal settings,
    // then we need to re-delegate the callbacks.
    const $dropdown = $(el);
    const dropdownModule = $dropdown.data('module-dropdown');
    if (!dropdownModule.giteaDelegated) {
      dropdownModule.giteaDelegated = true;
      delegateDropdownModule($dropdown);
    }
  }
  return ret;
}

// make the item has role=option/menuitem, add an id if there wasn't one yet, make items as non-focusable
// the elements inside the dropdown menu item should not be focusable, the focus should always be on the dropdown primary element.
function updateMenuItem(dropdown: HTMLElement, item: HTMLElement) {
  if (!item.id) item.id = generateElemId('_aria_dropdown_item_');
  item.setAttribute('role', (dropdown as any)[ariaPatchKey].listItemRole);
  item.setAttribute('tabindex', '-1');
  for (const el of item.querySelectorAll('a, input, button')) el.setAttribute('tabindex', '-1');
}
/**
 * make the label item and its "delete icon" have correct aria attributes
 * @param {HTMLElement} label
 */
function updateSelectionLabel(label: HTMLElement) {
  // the "label" is like this: "<a|div class="ui label" data-value="1">the-label-name <i|svg class="delete icon"/></a>"
  if (!label.id) {
    label.id = generateElemId('_aria_dropdown_label_');
  }
```

```text
## Framework usage

Mixing frameworks arbitrarily makes code hard to maintain. Recommended combinations:

- Vue3
- Vanilla JavaScript
- Fomantic-UI (jQuery), deprecated, we vendored a specific version with a lot of changes.

Avoid combinations such as Vue with Fomantic-UI.
Vue components may reuse Fomantic-UI CSS classes for visual consistency.
Use Go templates for simple or SEO-relevant pages and Vue for complex, interactive pages.
Gitea uses Vue 3 **without** JSX to keep HTML and JavaScript separate.

> [!NOTE]
> Fomantic-UI is not an accessibility-friendly framework. Gitea patches some ARIA
> behavior, but accessibility work is ongoing — prefer semantic HTML and test
> keyboard/screen-reader behavior where you can.

## Gitea-specific conventions

- Keep features in their own files or directories.
- Use kebab-case for HTML `id`s and classes, ideally with 2-3 feature keywords.
- Prefix classes to avoid short-name conflicts between different frameworks.
- Create a new class name when overriding framework styles instead of editing the framework's own classes,
  or fix the framework's source to fix all cases.
```
</details></tool-use>

```cjs
// Measures the comment-form footers with and without the `.field.footer { overflow: hidden }` rule.
const {chromium} = require('/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/node_modules/@playwright/test');

const BASE = 'http://localhost:3000';
const OUT = __dirname;
const RULE_OFF = '.repository.view.issue .comment-list .comment .ui.form .field.footer { overflow: visible !important; }';

// every element inside each affected footer, with its box; plus whether the footer clips anything
const measure = (page) => page.evaluate(() => {
  const footers = [...document.querySelectorAll('.repository.view.issue .comment-list .comment .ui.form .field.footer')];
  return footers.map((f, i) => {
    const r = f.getBoundingClientRect();
    const kids = [...f.querySelectorAll('*')].filter((el) => el.getClientRects().length).map((el) => {
      const b = el.getBoundingClientRect();
      return `${el.tagName.toLowerCase()}.${[...el.classList].join('.')} ${Math.round(b.x)},${Math.round(b.y)} ${Math.round(b.width)}x${Math.round(b.height)}`;
    });
    return {
      footer: i, visible: r.width > 0 && r.height > 0,
      box: `${Math.round(r.width)}x${Math.round(r.height)}`,
      overflowsX: f.scrollWidth > f.clientWidth, overflowsY: f.scrollHeight > f.clientHeight,
      kids,
    };
  });
});

// opens the close reason menu and hit-tests its middle: clipped means the point lands on something else
const menuSeen = async (page) => {
  const dropdown = page.locator('#comment-form .ui.buttons .ui.dropdown');
  if (!await dropdown.count()) return 'no dropdown';
  await dropdown.click();
  await page.waitForTimeout(600); // fomantic's open animation
  const res = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const menu = document.querySelector('#comment-form .ui.buttons .ui.dropdown .menu');
    const b = menu.getBoundingClientRect();
    const hit = document.elementFromPoint(b.x + b.width / 2, b.y + b.height / 2);
    return {menuBox: `${Math.round(b.width)}x${Math.round(b.height)}`, visible: getComputedStyle(menu).display !== 'none', hitsMenu: Boolean(hit && menu.contains(hit))};
  });
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await page.waitForTimeout(300);
  return res;
};

(async () => {
  const browser = await chromium.launch({executablePath: '/usr/bin/chromium'});
  const results = {};
  for (const width of [1280, 375]) {
    const page = await browser.newPage({viewport: {width, height: 900}});
    await page.goto(`${BASE}/user/login`);
    await page.fill('#user_name', 'ai');
    await page.fill('#password', 'aiaiaiai');
    await Promise.all([page.waitForNavigation(), page.click('form.ui.form button.ui.primary.button')]);

    for (const [name, path] of [['issue', '/ai/close-reason-check/issues/1'], ['pr', '/ai/close-reason-check/pulls/2']]) {
      for (const state of ['rule on', 'rule off']) {
        await page.goto(BASE + path);
        if (state === 'rule off') await page.addStyleTag({content: RULE_OFF});
        const reply = page.locator('.comment-list .comment-form-reply').first(); // shows the review reply form, which also has the footer
        if (await reply.count()) { await reply.click(); await page.waitForTimeout(300); }
        await page.locator('#comment-form').scrollIntoViewIfNeeded();
        const key = `${width}px ${name} ${state}`;
        results[key] = {footers: await measure(page), menu: await menuSeen(page)};
        await page.locator('#comment-form .ui.buttons .ui.dropdown').click().catch(() => {});
        await page.waitForTimeout(600);
        await page.screenshot({path: `${OUT}/${width}-${name}-${state.replace(' ', '-')}.png`, clip: await page.locator('#comment-form').boundingBox().then((b) => ({x: 0, y: Math.max(0, b.y - 20), width, height: Math.min(900, b.height + 260)}))});
        await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
      }
    }
    await page.close();
  }
  await browser.close();
  console.log(JSON.stringify(results, null, 1));
})().catch((err) => { console.error(err); process.exit(1); });

```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-09-30 02:48:04Z)**_

Confirmed: the rule does nothing on today's pages except hide the new menu.

- **Where it applies:** its selector matches exactly one element in Gitea, the footer of the comment box on issue and PR pages. The only other `.field.footer` is the review reply form (`templates/repo/diff/comment_form.tmpl`). That footer doesn't sit inside a `.comment`, so the rule never reached it; in the browser its overflow is already `visible`.
- **Layout:** I logged in as `ai` in headless Chromium and loaded an issue page and a PR page, at desktop (1280px) and phone (375px) widths. Switching the rule off moved or resized nothing in the footer: all 11–12 elements kept the same position and size. Nothing overflows the footer with the rule on or off, so there's nothing for it to clip.
- **The menu:** with the rule on, the menu opens but a click in its middle lands on something else, because it's clipped. With the rule off, it shows and works. You can compare the screenshots `1280-issue-rule-on.png` and `1280-issue-rule-off.png` in my scratchpad folder, `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-mont9393-Documents-CSCI435-gitea/0dcab0b9-aa95-4cfb-a2d8-9e4fd6a2a830/scratchpad/`.
- **History:** the rule came in with upstream #11139 in 2020, when the footer lined its buttons up a different way. In April 2025, upstream #34227 switched both footers to a flex row, which doesn't need the rule, and the rule was left behind.

I didn't measure the closed-issue footer (Reopen button only). It uses the same markup with one button fewer, so there's still nothing for the rule to clip.

## Gitea's current dropdown patterns

- **Fomantic `.ui.dropdown`** is the standard for menus in server-rendered pages; 103 templates use it.
  - Every page sets each one up automatically through `initGlobalDropdown` (`web_src/js/features/common-page.ts`). Gitea also patches it for screen readers (`web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts`).
  - Adding `jump` (29 templates) means clicking an item does something, like opening a link, instead of becoming the selected value.
  - Adding `custom` (5 templates) means the feature sets the dropdown up itself.
- **Split button** (`ui buttons` plus `ui dropdown icon button`): only the "Update branch" button uses this, set up by `initRepoPullRequestUpdate`. Ours copies it.
- **Tippy popups** (`createTippy` with `theme: 'menu'`) are for a few small menus built in TypeScript, like the line-number menu in the code view (`repo-code.ts`). They're attached to the page body, so no parent box can clip them.
- **Vue components** draw their own menus, the PR merge form for example.

Fomantic's JavaScript is officially deprecated (`docs/guidelines-frontend.md`), but its dropdown is still how template menus are built, and no newer template pattern has replaced it. So step 2 follows the current pattern.

## Fixing it, your call

- **A (my recommendation): delete the rule.** It's confirmed to do nothing else, and it only ever touched this one footer.
- **B: override it for this footer only.** That leaves a rule that does nothing, plus an override to work around it.
- **C: make our menu a tippy popup.** It can't be clipped, so no CSS change is needed. But it breaks from the "Update branch" pattern, and the menu wouldn't open at all until step 3's TypeScript exists.

For these checks I created a throwaway repo, `ai/close-reason-check`, with an issue and a PR. I'd like to keep it for the browser checks in the next steps, and you can delete it any time.

```markdown
# Issue #54 — design decisions

Entries marked *(proposed)* are not decided yet.

### Decision 3: A leftover style that hid the close menu is removed

**Decision:** The comment box's button row had a style that cut off anything reaching outside it (`overflow: hidden` in `web_src/css/repo.css`), which hid the close reason menu. The style is deleted.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Keep the style and override it for this row only. (b) Build the menu as a popup attached to the whole page, which no box can cut off, as a few of Gitea's small menus are.
**Rationale:** The style dates from a 2020 layout of this row that was replaced in 2025, and it applies to nothing else. Checked in the browser, removing it changes nothing on the page except letting the menu show. (a) would keep a style that does nothing and add a second one to cancel it. (b) would break from the "Update branch" split button this menu copies.
**Consequences:** If anything in the row ever does reach outside it, such as a very long translated button label on a phone, it will now show instead of being cut off.
```

```text
## Traps, and what they look like

**Your stylesheet has no effect whatsoever.** You did not add the `@import` to `index.css`. Nothing
warns you — the file simply is not part of the build.

**Your class works in development and vanishes in the built site.** Tailwind scans the files listed
in its config and removes classes it cannot find. A class assembled in JavaScript — sticking a
prefix and a variable together — is invisible to that scan and gets purged. Always write the full
class name literally, even if that means a few more lines.

**A Tailwind utility you know exists does not work.** Two possibilities: you left off the `tw-`
prefix, or it is in the blocklist in the config, which is deliberate.

**You change a colour and one theme looks broken.** You used a literal colour instead of a theme
variable.

**You edit something in `web_src/css/modules/` expecting the third-party framework.** That folder is
Gitea's *replacement* for it. The vendored original is elsewhere, under `web_src/fomantic/`.

**Your style is overridden and you cannot see why.** Before reaching for `!important`, check whether
you are fighting a `gt-` helper — those use it deliberately and will win.

**You invent a new `--color-` name in a theme file and the build rejects it.** `tailwind.config.ts`
and `stylelint.config.ts` learn the list of valid colour names by reading `base.css` and the two
`theme-gitea-*` files, and nothing else. A name that appears only in your theme is unknown to both:
`make lint-css` fails, and no `tw-` utility is generated for it. A theme may freely *change* an
existing colour — it may not add one.
```

```markdown
### Decision 4: The old close button strings are deleted

**Decision:** "Close Issue", "Close Pull Request" and "Close with Comment" are deleted from `locale_en-US.json`, since the close button now names its reason and nothing else uses them. The other languages are left for the translation platform to clean up (AC10).
```

```text
  // Expected user interactions for dropdown with aria support:
  // * user can use Tab to focus in the dropdown, then the dropdown menu (list) will be shown
  // * user presses Tab on the focused dropdown to move focus to next sibling focusable element (but not the menu item)
  // * user can use arrow key Up/Down to navigate between menu items
  // * when user presses Enter:
  //    - if the menu item is clickable (eg: <a>), then trigger the click event
  //    - otherwise, the dropdown control (low-level code) handles the Enter event, hides the dropdown menu

  // TODO: multiple selection is only partially supported. Check and test them one by one in the future.

  const textSearch = dropdown.querySelector<HTMLElement>('input.search');
  const focusable = textSearch || dropdown; // the primary element for focus, see comment above
  if (!focusable) return;

  // as a combobox, the input should not have autocomplete by default
...
    }
  };

  dropdown.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    if (e.isComposing) return;
    // here it must use keydown event before dropdown's keyup handler, otherwise there is no Enter event in our keyup handler
    if (e.key === 'Enter') {
      const elItem = menu.querySelector<HTMLElement>(':scope > .item.selected, .menu > .item.selected');
      // if the selected item is clickable, then trigger the click event.
      // we can not click any item without check, because Fomantic code might also handle the Enter event. that would result in double click.
      if (elItem?.matches('a, .js-aria-clickable') && !elItem.matches('.tw-hidden, .filtered')) {
        e.preventDefault();
        elItem.click();
      }
    }
  });

  // use setTimeout to run the refreshAria in next tick (to make sure the Fomantic UI code has finished its work)
  // do not return any value, jQuery has return-value related behaviors.
  // when the popup is hiding, it's better to have a small "delay", because there is a Fomantic UI animation
  // without the delay for hiding, the UI will be somewhat laggy and sometimes may get stuck in the animation.
  const deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem = (delay = 0) => { setTimeout(refreshAriaActiveItem, delay) };
  (dropdown as any)[ariaPatchKey].deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem = deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem;
  dropdown.addEventListener('keyup', (e) => { if (e.key.startsWith('Arrow')) deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem(); });
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-09-30 14:15:29Z)**_

## Step 3: picking a reason (TypeScript)

**What it does (AC3):** choosing an item in the ▾ menu switches the Close button to that reason:
- The button text changes to "Close as not planned", or "Close as not planned with comment" once a comment is typed.
- The hidden `close_reason` field switches to match, so that's the reason that gets saved.
- Nothing is sent until the button itself is clicked.
- Reopen has no menu, so nothing changes there.

**What changes**
- **Template** (`view_content.tmpl`): each menu item carries its own two button texts, taken from the locale file. The button already holds its current pair the same way (`data-status`, `data-status-and-comment`), and it's the standard way to hand translated text to TypeScript (`i18n.md`).
- **TypeScript** (`web_src/js/features/repo-issue.ts`): on a pick, it copies the item's texts onto the button, sets the hidden field, and refreshes the text. The refresh already exists: `initSingleCommentEditor` rewrites the button text from those two attributes whenever the comment box changes.
- **Tests**:
  - A Vitest test, run against a simulated page, that picks a reason and checks the hidden field and both texts, with and without a comment.
  - A headless browser run by me: pick "Not planned" with the mouse and with the keyboard, close, and confirm the database recorded not planned. The page itself only shows the reason from step 5.
- **Docs:** `frontend-js.md` gets whichever pattern you pick below.

**Heads-up:** until step 4 adds the number and text boxes, closing as Duplicate or Other is refused with #53's error message, and the issue stays open. That's expected in between, but say if you'd rather merge steps 3 and 4.

**Where to see it:** on an open issue, pick "Not planned" from the ▾ and the button reads "Close as not planned". Type a comment and it becomes "…with comment". With the keyboard: Tab to the ▾, use the arrow keys, then press Enter.

## Decisions for step 3

1. **How the page notices a pick**
   - **A: Fomantic's own change callback** (`onChange`), as the "Update branch" button does (`initRepoPullRequestUpdate` in `repo-issue-pull.ts`). Mouse and keyboard are both covered automatically. The catch is that it builds on Fomantic's JavaScript, which Gitea's frontend guidelines call deprecated, and the Vitest test can't exercise that hookup, because Fomantic doesn't run there.
   - **B (my recommendation): a plain click listener on the items.** Each item gets the `js-aria-clickable` class, so Gitea's dropdown patch turns Enter into a click; that's how the comment "⋯" menu works (`context_menu.tmpl`). No Fomantic JavaScript is involved, and the Vitest test can click the real items. The catch is that keyboard support depends on that one class, which a later edit could drop without noticing. The Vitest test would guard it.

   Both are current patterns: the "Update branch" code was touched in 2025 and 2026, and `js-aria-clickable` dates from 2024.
2. **Where the code lives**
   - **A (my recommendation): inside `initSingleCommentEditor`.** That function already decides what the Close button says, so one place stays in charge of the text.
   - **B: its own small feature, switched on by a `data-global-init` attribute in the template.** That's the wiring `frontend-js.md` prefers for new code. But then two pieces of code would both write the button text, and typing in the comment box would have to not undo a picked reason.

Tell me your choices and I'll start.

```text
export function initTabSwitcher(tabItemContainer: Element) {
  // Clicking a `.item[data-tab]` menu item activates the matching `.ui.tab[data-tab=...]` panel
  // This design is from Fomantic UI, and it has problems like :
  // * The panel selector is global, callers should make sure the "data-tab" values don't conflict on the same page
  const tabItems = tabItemContainer.querySelectorAll('.item[data-tab]');

      const elPanel = document.querySelector(`.ui.tab[data-tab="${CSS.escape(tabName)}"]`)!;
      queryElemSiblings(elPanel, '.ui.tab', (el) => el.classList.remove('active'));
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-09-30 14:24:14Z)**_

Both questions have factual answers, and in both cases your pushback changes the picture.

## 1. Fomantic and consistency

**The menu itself is shared either way.** Opening, closing, keyboard movement and the screen-reader patch come from the same `.ui.dropdown` in both options, so any central fix reaches this menu under A or B.

**The only difference is how the code hears the pick,** and neither approach is what "most of the program" does:
- Fomantic's `onChange` is used in about 5 places, including "Update branch", the edit-history dropdown and the repo-owner picker.
- Plain click listeners are also used in about 5: the issue-list bulk toolbar, the sidebar branch menu, the branch picker and the language menu.

**About "a single update updates everything":** there won't be one from Fomantic. Upstream #33845 (2025) says "We would never update or build fomantic again." Changes now arrive in two ways:
- **Gitea's own patches**, like the screen-reader one. These wrap Fomantic, so A and B benefit equally.
- **Rewriting a module.** The only rewrite so far, tabs (`web_src/js/modules/fomantic/tab.ts`), kept the markup and switched to plain clicks, and every place calling the old Fomantic function had to be rewritten.

So under a dropdown rewrite, A would be updated together with the other `onChange` callers, which keeps it consistent with them, as you say. B wouldn't need touching.

My revised view: this is closer than I made it sound. I still lean B, because it survives a rewrite and its test can click the real items. But A is a defensible choice for matching the only other split button. Your call.

## 2. Where the code lives

**One) Does a pattern back B?** For the wiring, yes: 31 features are switched on with `data-global-init`, including the "Update branch" split button. What has no precedent is the other half: a separate feature that follows what's typed in the comment box. Every feature that reacts to the editor does it right where the editor is set up (`repo-issue.ts`, `repo-issue-edit.ts`). It is possible, since the editor's "content changed" and "upload" events travel up the page and the editor can be looked up from its box (`getComboMarkdownEditor`). It just hasn't been done anywhere yet.

**Two) Should the existing code move with it?** Yes. If it's B, the clean version moves the Close/Reopen button's existing code out of `initSingleCommentEditor` into that one feature. Then one place owns everything the button does: its text with and without a comment, being disabled during an upload, and the reason. `initSingleCommentEditor` keeps only the Comment button. That also removes the "two writers" problem I raised. The cost is that #54 would then refactor existing upstream code, which makes the diff and the review bigger, and it would be the first feature to follow the editor from outside.

So the real choice is:
- **A (my recommendation for #54): add the reason to `initSingleCommentEditor`.** Everything that reacts to the editor lives there today, and it's the smaller change a week before the deadline.
- **B: move the whole Close/Reopen button into its own `data-global-init` feature.** It's the preferred wiring with one owner, at the cost of a refactor and a first-of-its-kind pattern. It could also be done later, as its own follow-up.

Tell me what you pick for 1 and 2.

```typescript
import {ComboMarkdownEditor, getComboMarkdownEditor} from './comp/ComboMarkdownEditor.ts';

// The close/reopen button in an issue or pull request's comment form: its text says whether the typed
// comment is posted with it, and it is disabled while files upload. The editor's events bubble up to the form.
export function initRepoIssueStatusButton(elButtons: HTMLElement) {
  const statusButton = elButtons.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('#status-button')!;
  const elForm = elButtons.closest('form')!;
  const elEditor = elForm.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.combo-markdown-editor')!;
  const syncStatusButton = () => {
    const editor = getComboMarkdownEditor(elEditor); // null until the editor has initialized, so read the textarea until then
    const content = editor ? editor.value() : elEditor.querySelector('textarea')!.value;
    const statusText = statusButton.getAttribute(content.trim() ? 'data-status-and-comment' : 'data-status');
    statusButton.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.status-button-text')!.textContent = statusText;
    statusButton.disabled = Boolean(editor?.isUploading());
  };
  elForm.addEventListener(ComboMarkdownEditor.EventEditorContentChanged, syncStatusButton);
  elForm.addEventListener(ComboMarkdownEditor.EventUploadStateChanged, syncStatusButton);
  syncStatusButton(); // a comment the browser restored after a reload is already there
}
```

```typescript
function createForm(textareaValue = '') {

    <form>
      <div class="combo-markdown-editor"><textarea>${textareaValue}</textarea></div>
      <div class="ui buttons">
        <button id="status-button" data-status="Close as completed" data-status-and-comment="Close as completed with comment">
          <span class="status-button-text"></span>
        </button>
      </div>
    </form>
  `);
  const elEditor = elForm.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.combo-markdown-editor')!;
  const statusButton = elForm.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('#status-button')!;
  const editor = {content: textareaValue, uploading: false, value() { return this.content }, isUploading() { return this.uploading }};
  return {
    statusButton,
    buttonText: () => statusButton.querySelector('.status-button-text')!.textContent,
    init: () => initRepoIssueStatusButton(elForm.querySelector('.ui.buttons')!),
    attachEditor: () => { (elEditor as any)._giteaComboMarkdownEditor = editor },
    typeComment: (content: string) => {
      editor.content = content;
      elEditor.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('ce-editor-content-changed', {bubbles: true}));
    },
    setUploading: (uploading: boolean) => {
      editor.uploading = uploading;
      elEditor.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('ce-upload-state-changed', {bubbles: true}));
    },
  };
}

test('text follows whether a comment is typed', () => {

  expect(form.buttonText()).toBe('Close as completed with comment');
  form.typeComment('  ');
  expect(form.buttonText()).toBe('Close as completed');
});

test('disabled while files upload', () => {

  form.init();
  form.attachEditor();
  form.setUploading(true);
  expect(form.statusButton.disabled).toBe(true);
  form.setUploading(false);
  expect(form.statusButton.disabled).toBe(false);
});

test('a comment restored before the editor is ready counts', () => {

  form.init();
  expect(form.buttonText()).toBe('Close as completed with comment');
});
```

```typescript
import {ComboMarkdownEditor, getComboMarkdownEditor} from './comp/ComboMarkdownEditor.ts';

// The close/reopen button in an issue or pull request's comment form: its text says whether the typed
// comment is posted with it, and it is disabled while files upload. The editor's events bubble up to the form.
export function initRepoIssueStatusButton(elButtons: HTMLElement) {
  const statusButton = elButtons.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('#status-button')!;
  const elForm = elButtons.closest('form')!;
  const elEditor = elForm.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.combo-markdown-editor')!;
  const syncStatusButton = (content: string, isUploading: boolean) => {
    const statusText = statusButton.getAttribute(content.trim() ? 'data-status-and-comment' : 'data-status');
    statusButton.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.status-button-text')!.textContent = statusText;
    statusButton.disabled = isUploading;
  };
  const syncFromEditor = () => {
    const editor = getComboMarkdownEditor(elEditor)!; // these events only come from an initialized editor
    syncStatusButton(editor.value(), editor.isUploading());
  };
  elForm.addEventListener(ComboMarkdownEditor.EventEditorContentChanged, syncFromEditor);
  elForm.addEventListener(ComboMarkdownEditor.EventUploadStateChanged, syncFromEditor);
  // the editor attaches itself before its async init finishes, so start from the textarea, which holds any comment the browser restored
  syncStatusButton(elEditor.querySelector<HTMLTextAreaElement>('textarea.markdown-text-editor')!.value, false);
}
```

```typescript
          <span class="status-button-text"></span>
        </button>
      </div>
    </form>
  `);
  const elEditor = elForm.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.combo-markdown-editor')!;
  const statusButton = elForm.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('#status-button')!;
  // like the real editor, it is attached before its init finishes, and reading it before then throws
  const editor = {
    ready: false, content: textareaValue, uploading: false,
    value() { if (!this.ready) throw new Error('editor not initialized'); return this.content },
    isUploading() { if (!this.ready) throw new Error('editor not initialized'); return this.uploading },
  };
  (elEditor as any)._giteaComboMarkdownEditor = editor;
  return {
    statusButton,
    buttonText: () => statusButton.querySelector('.status-button-text')!.textContent,
    init: () => initRepoIssueStatusButton(elForm.querySelector('.ui.buttons')!),
    finishEditorInit: () => { editor.ready = true },
    typeComment: (content: string) => {
      editor.content = content;
      elEditor.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent(EventEditorContentChanged, {bubbles: true}));
    },
    setUploading: (uploading: boolean) => {
      editor.uploading = uploading;
      elEditor.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent(EventUploadStateChanged, {bubbles: true}));
    },
  };
}

test('text follows whether a comment is typed', () => {
  const form = createForm();
  form.init();
  expect(form.buttonText()).toBe('Close as completed');

  form.finishEditorInit();
  form.typeComment('looks done');
  expect(form.buttonText()).toBe('Close as completed with comment');
  form.typeComment('  ');
  expect(form.buttonText()).toBe('Close as completed');
});

test('disabled while files upload', () => {
  const form = createForm();
  form.init();
  form.finishEditorInit();
  form.setUploading(true);
  expect(form.statusButton.disabled).toBe(true);
  form.setUploading(false);
  expect(form.statusButton.disabled).toBe(false);
});

test('a comment restored before the editor is ready counts', () => {
  const form = createForm('restored draft');
  form.init(); // the editor is attached but not initialized yet
  expect(form.buttonText()).toBe('Close as completed with comment');
});
```

```text
## Traps, and what they look like

**The whole site gets slower after your change.** You added a page-load init without an early
return, so your feature's setup cost is now paid on every page in Gitea. The 500ms warning in the
console exists to catch exactly this.

**Your code works on load and not on new elements.** A comment posted without a page reload does not
get your behaviour. You used page-load init; use the declarative mechanism, which sees later
elements.

**Your `data-` attribute reads as undefined.** You used `dataset` and the property name was
silently camel-cased. Use `getAttribute` with the literal attribute name.

**Your request is rejected, usually as a 403.** You used a raw `fetch` and skipped the wrappers,
which is what adds the request token.

**Registering a global init function throws.** You registered it after the observer started.
Registration happens at module load; the observer starts last, on purpose.

**You build on Fomantic-UI because the existing code does.** It is the vendored jQuery library, and
it is deprecated. Do not start new features on it, and never mix its JavaScript with Vue — Vue may
use its CSS classes, but the two fight over who owns the DOM.

**You put a helper in `utils/` and it breaks in tests.** That folder is for pure helpers. Anything
reaching for `window` or searching the page belongs in `modules/` or `features/`.

---
scope: web_src/js/index.ts, web_src/js/features, web_src/js/modules, web_src/js/utils, web_src/js/webcomponents, web_src/js/markup, web_src/js/render

---
```

```markdown
# Issue #54 — design decisions

Entries marked *(proposed)* are not decided yet.

### Decision 5: The close/reopen button gets its own piece of page code

**Decision:** The code that sets the close/reopen button's text ("…with comment" once a comment is typed) and disables it during uploads moves out of the comment box's setup (`initSingleCommentEditor`) into its own feature, `web_src/js/features/repo-issue-status-button.ts`. It is switched on by a `data-global-init` attribute on the button in the template. Its behaviour doesn't change; choosing a reason is built on it in the next commit.
**Alternatives Considered:** Leave the button's code in the comment box's setup, and add reason picking there.
**Rationale:** `data-global-init` is the wiring Gitea prefers for new page code, and 31 features already use it, including the "Update branch" split button. Moving the button's existing code as well means one place decides everything the button shows, instead of two pieces of code writing the same text.
**Consequences:** It is the first feature to follow a comment box it did not set up. That relies on the box's events reaching the form, and on reading the box's text directly at start-up, because the editor is not ready yet at that point. The move also touches existing upstream code, so the change is bigger than the reason picking alone.
```

```typescript
import {ComboMarkdownEditor, getComboMarkdownEditor} from './comp/ComboMarkdownEditor.ts';

// The close/reopen button in an issue or pull request's comment form: its text says whether the typed
// comment is posted with it, and it is disabled while files upload. The editor's events bubble up to the form.
// While the item is open, the menu beside it picks the close reason: the button then takes that reason's texts.
export function initRepoIssueStatusButton(elButtons: HTMLElement) {
  const statusButton = elButtons.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('#status-button')!;
  const elForm = elButtons.closest('form')!;
  const elEditor = elForm.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.combo-markdown-editor')!;
  // the editor attaches itself before its async init finishes, so start from the textarea, which holds any comment the browser restored
  let content = elEditor.querySelector<HTMLTextAreaElement>('textarea.markdown-text-editor')!.value;
  let isUploading = false;
  const syncStatusButton = () => {
    const statusText = statusButton.getAttribute(content.trim() ? 'data-status-and-comment' : 'data-status');
    statusButton.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.status-button-text')!.textContent = statusText;
    statusButton.disabled = isUploading;
  };
  const syncFromEditor = () => {
    const editor = getComboMarkdownEditor(elEditor)!; // these events only come from an initialized editor
    content = editor.value();
    isUploading = editor.isUploading();
    syncStatusButton();
  };
  elForm.addEventListener(ComboMarkdownEditor.EventEditorContentChanged, syncFromEditor);
  elForm.addEventListener(ComboMarkdownEditor.EventUploadStateChanged, syncFromEditor);
  syncStatusButton();

  const elReasonMenu = elButtons.querySelector('.ui.dropdown > .menu');
  if (!elReasonMenu) return; // a closed item only offers reopening
  const reasonInput = elForm.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input[name="close_reason"]')!;
  // a plain click listener rather than the dropdown's onChange; the template marks the items js-aria-clickable, so Enter clicks them too
  elReasonMenu.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    const elItem = (e.target as Element).closest<HTMLElement>('.item[data-value]');
    if (!elItem) return;
    reasonInput.value = elItem.getAttribute('data-value')!;
    statusButton.setAttribute('data-status', elItem.getAttribute('data-status')!);
    statusButton.setAttribute('data-status-and-comment', elItem.getAttribute('data-status-and-comment')!);
    syncStatusButton();
  });
}

```

```markdown
# Issue #54 — design decisions

Entries marked *(proposed)* are not decided yet.

### Decision 6: Picking a reason is heard with a plain click listener, not Fomantic's change callback

**Decision:** The page notices a pick with an ordinary click listener on the menu's items. Each item carries the class `js-aria-clickable`, which makes Gitea's dropdown patch turn Enter on a highlighted item into a click, so the keyboard works too. Fomantic still opens, closes and highlights the menu.
**Alternatives Considered:** Fomantic's `onChange` callback, as the "Update branch" split button uses.
**Rationale:** Gitea froze Fomantic in 2025 (upstream #33845) and replaces it by rewriting modules. The one rewrite so far, tabs, kept the markup and switched to plain click listeners, and code calling Fomantic had to be rewritten. A click listener keeps working through such a rewrite, and the page's tests can click the real items, which they can't do with Fomantic's callback.
**Consequences:** Keyboard picking depends on the `js-aria-clickable` class, which only two of Gitea's menus use. The page's integration test checks every item carries it, so a later edit can't drop it unnoticed. It also departs from the only other split button, which still uses `onChange`.

```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-09-30 15:15:26Z)**_

Your step 3 commit is in. Here's step 4. It has the open question from your issue plus two smaller choices, and I won't start until you've picked.

## Step 4: the boxes for Duplicate and Other

**What it does (AC4, AC5):**
- Picking **Duplicate** shows a number box for the original issue or PR.
- Picking **Other** shows a text box for the reason, capped at 255 characters.
- Every other reason shows neither box.

The server already checks what's typed and refuses bad input with #53's messages ("The duplicate must be another issue or pull request in this repository…", "The description is not valid…"), and the item stays open. So step 4 is only about the page. The link to the original issue in the timeline comes in step 5.

**What changes**
- **Template:** the two boxes, hidden by default, with their labels in the locale file. The text box reuses the existing "Close reason description" label, which is already what the error message calls it.
- **Feature** (`repo-issue-status-button.ts`): a pick shows the box that reason needs and hides the other.
- **Tests:**
  - Vitest for showing and hiding.
  - The page's integration test checks both boxes' attributes.
  - Closing through the page's own form as a valid duplicate, and as Other with valid text, both succeed.
  - A browser check by me.
- **Docs:** whatever the chosen pattern needs.

## Decisions for step 4

1. **The duplicate input** (your open question)
   - **A (my recommendation): a plain number box.** The backend already takes the number and refuses a wrong one with a message. Gitea's other number inputs are the same kind of box: the time tracker's hours, and the label order in the label editor.
   - **B: a search picker** like the sidebar's dependency picker, which shows titles as you type. It's much more code: a search request and its own dropdown. #53's Decision 7 also says a picker would have to send the number, not the ID.
2. **Boxes for reasons that aren't picked**
   - **A (my recommendation): switch them off while hidden.** A switched-off (disabled) box isn't sent, which respects #53's rule that text or a number only goes with its own reason. Switching back to Other also keeps what you'd typed. And a plain comment can never trip the 255-character check because of a hidden box.
   - **B: empty them** when you switch away, which loses what was typed.
3. **Closing with an empty box**
   - **A (my recommendation): let the server refuse** with #53's message. The catch, #53's known limitation, is that a typed comment is posted before the close is refused.
   - **B: have the browser stop the click** before anything is sent, by marking the visible box `required`. But both buttons submit the same form, so the Comment button would also need a `formnovalidate` attribute; otherwise a plain comment would be blocked while Duplicate or Other is picked. No Gitea template uses that attribute, and the browser's warning would appear in the browser's language, not Gitea's.

What I'd assume unless you say otherwise:
- The box sits in a row just above the buttons, right-aligned, and only shows when needed.
- Placeholders read "Issue or pull request number" and "Why is it being closed?".

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-09-30 15:21:11Z)**_

Both answers came out in favour of your instincts.

## 1. Reusing the `#` suggestions

It can be reused, and it's a better fit than either option I gave you. The `#` list in a comment box is GitHub's `<text-expander>` element, set up by `initTextExpander` (`web_src/js/features/comp/TextExpander.ts`). Its search, `matchIssue`, already does what AC4 needs: it only looks in the current repository, and it leaves out the item you're on.

**How it would work:** the duplicate box becomes a one-line text box wrapped in `<text-expander keys="#">`, set up by the same function. You'd type `#` followed by a number or words from a title, and the same list as in comments appears (icon, `#number`, title). Picking an entry fills in `#12`.

**What it takes**, two small changes to shared code:
- `initTextExpander` only looks for a `textarea`, since it was written for the comment box. It would need to accept a one-line input as well. Every comment box goes through this function, but nothing changes for them.
- The box would then hold text like `#12`, not a plain number. So #53's form field (`close_duplicate_index`, which currently only accepts a number) would take text and read the number out of it. `12` would work too, just without the list, and anything else is refused with #53's duplicate message. The field keeps its name, so #53's tests still pass as they are.

So the choice for the duplicate input is now:
- **A: a plain number box.** No suggestions.
- **B (my recommendation now): reuse the `#` suggestions** as described above.

## 2. Noted
Hidden boxes are switched off, and there's no decision entry.

## 3. How Gitea handles input errors

It does both, with the server as the authority:
- **The server always checks.** 107 form fields carry `binding:"Required…"`, and a failed check comes back as a message.
- **The browser stops obvious mistakes early** in 91 templates, using `required`, `pattern` or `maxlength` on single-purpose forms like the label editor (`label_edit_modal.tmpl`). These are forms with one submit button.
- **This comment form does it differently,** because two buttons share it: it disables the button that can't succeed. The Comment button stays disabled while the box is empty (`repo-issue.ts`), and Close/Reopen is disabled while a file uploads. That's also why `required` would cause trouble here: it would block the Comment button too.

That gives a third option for empty boxes, and it's my recommendation:
- **A: the server refuses** with #53's message, after posting any typed comment.
- **B: `required` on the box**, plus `formnovalidate` on the Comment button.
- **C (my recommendation): disable the Close button while the picked reason's box is empty**, the same way the Comment button works. Nothing is sent, so there's no half-posted comment. The server still refuses a wrong number or text that's too long, and the text box also gets `maxlength="255"`, like the label editor's name field.

Pick 1 and 3, and I'll start.

```typescript
import '@github/text-expander-element';
import {ComboMarkdownEditor, getComboMarkdownEditor} from './comp/ComboMarkdownEditor.ts';
import {initTextExpander} from './comp/TextExpander.ts';
import {toggleElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';

// The close/reopen button in an issue or pull request's comment form: its text says whether the typed
// comment is posted with it, and it is disabled while files upload. The editor's events bubble up to the form.
// While the item is open, the menu beside it picks the close reason: the button then takes that reason's texts,
// and a reason that needs more (a duplicate's number, an "other" description) shows its box above the buttons.
export function initRepoIssueStatusButton(elButtons: HTMLElement) {
  const statusButton = elButtons.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('#status-button')!;
  const elForm = elButtons.closest('form')!;
  const elEditor = elForm.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.combo-markdown-editor')!;
  const reasonFields = elForm.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[data-close-reason-field]'); // none on a closed item
  const reasonFieldInput = (elField: HTMLElement) => elField.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input')!;
  // the editor attaches itself before its async init finishes, so start from the textarea, which holds any comment the browser restored
  let content = elEditor.querySelector<HTMLTextAreaElement>('textarea.markdown-text-editor')!.value;
  let isUploading = false;
  const syncStatusButton = () => {
    const statusText = statusButton.getAttribute(content.trim() ? 'data-status-and-comment' : 'data-status');
    statusButton.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.status-button-text')!.textContent = statusText;
    // like the comment button with an empty comment: closing can't succeed while the picked reason's box is empty
    const isReasonFieldEmpty = Array.from(reasonFields, reasonFieldInput).some((el) => !el.disabled && !el.value.trim());
    statusButton.disabled = isUploading || isReasonFieldEmpty;
  };
  const syncFromEditor = () => {
    const editor = getComboMarkdownEditor(elEditor)!; // these events only come from an initialized editor
    content = editor.value();
    isUploading = editor.isUploading();
    syncStatusButton();
  };
  elForm.addEventListener(ComboMarkdownEditor.EventEditorContentChanged, syncFromEditor);
  elForm.addEventListener(ComboMarkdownEditor.EventUploadStateChanged, syncFromEditor);
  syncStatusButton();

  const elReasonMenu = elButtons.querySelector('.ui.dropdown > .menu');
  if (!elReasonMenu) return; // a closed item only offers reopening
  const reasonInput = elForm.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input[name="close_reason"]')!;
  for (const elField of reasonFields) {
    reasonFieldInput(elField).addEventListener('input', syncStatusButton);
    const elExpander = elField.querySelector('text-expander');
    if (elExpander) {
      initTextExpander(elExpander); // the same # suggestions as in the comment box
      elExpander.addEventListener('text-expander-committed', syncStatusButton); // picking a suggestion fires no input event
    }
  }
  // a plain click listener rather than the dropdown's onChange; the template marks the items js-aria-clickable, so Enter clicks them too
  elReasonMenu.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    const elItem = (e.target as Element).closest<HTMLElement>('.item[data-value]');
    if (!elItem) return;
    reasonInput.value = elItem.getAttribute('data-value')!;
    statusButton.setAttribute('data-status', elItem.getAttribute('data-status')!);
    statusButton.setAttribute('data-status-and-comment', elItem.getAttribute('data-status-and-comment')!);
    for (const elField of reasonFields) {
      const isNeeded = elField.getAttribute('data-close-reason-field') === reasonInput.value;
      toggleElem(elField, isNeeded);
      reasonFieldInput(elField).disabled = !isNeeded; // a disabled box keeps what was typed but is not sent
      if (isNeeded) reasonFieldInput(elField).focus();
    }
    syncStatusButton();
  });
}

```

```cjs
  const suggestions = box('duplicate').locator('.suggestions li');
  result.suggestions = await suggestions.allInnerTexts();
  await page.screenshot({path: __dirname + '/duplicate-suggestions.png', clip: {x: 0, y: (await box('duplicate').boundingBox()).y - 30, width: 1280, height: 330}});
  await suggestions.filter({hasText: '#1'}).first().click();
  await page.waitForTimeout(300);
  result.afterSuggestion = {value: await box('duplicate').locator('input').inputValue(), closeDisabled: await page.locator('#status-button').isDisabled()};
  await Promise.all([page.waitForNavigation(), page.locator('#status-button').click()]);
  await page.waitForTimeout(500);
  result.issue4After = (await page.locator('#status-button .status-button-text').innerText()).trim();

  // issue #5: other with text
  await page.goto(`${REPO}/issues/5`);

  result.errors = errors;
```
