				{{- svg "octicon-git-merge" 16 "tw-text-purple" -}}
			{{- else -}}
				{{- template "shared/close_reason_icon" dict "Reason" .CloseReason "IsPull" true "For" "list" -}}

			{{- end -}}
		{{- end -}}
	{{- end -}}
{{- else -}}
	{{- if .IsClosed -}}

	{{- else -}}

	{{- end -}}
{{- end -}}

```text
#!/usr/bin/env node
import {readdirSync, readFileSync, globSync} from 'node:fs';
import {parse, relative} from 'node:path';
import {fileURLToPath} from 'node:url';
import {exit} from 'node:process';

const knownSvgs = new Set<string>();
for (const file of readdirSync(new URL('../public/assets/img/svg', import.meta.url))) {
  knownSvgs.add(parse(file).name);
}

const rootPath = fileURLToPath(new URL('..', import.meta.url));
let hadErrors = false;

for (const file of globSync(fileURLToPath(new URL('../templates/**/*.tmpl', import.meta.url)))) {
  const content = readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
  for (const [_, name] of content.matchAll(/svg ["'`]([^"'`]+)["'`]/g)) {
    if (!knownSvgs.has(name)) {
      console.info(`SVG "${name}" not found, used in ${relative(rootPath, file)}`);
      hadErrors = true;
    }
  }
}

exit(hadErrors ? 1 : 0);
```

```text
> Fomantic-UI is not an accessibility-friendly framework. Gitea patches some ARIA
> behavior, but accessibility work is ongoing — prefer semantic HTML and test
> keyboard/screen-reader behavior where you can.

## Gitea-specific conventions

- Keep features in their own files or directories.
- Use kebab-case for HTML `id`s and classes, ideally with 2-3 feature keywords.
- Prefix classes to avoid short-name conflicts between different frameworks.
- Create a new class name when overriding framework styles instead of editing the framework's own classes,
  or fix the framework's source to fix all cases.
- Prefer semantic elements such as `<button>` over generic `<div>`s.
- Avoid `!important`; when it is unavoidable, document why.
- Prefix custom DOM events with `ce-`.

## CSS

Prefer Tailwind utility classes with the `tw-` prefix, and the `flex-*` layout
helpers over per-child margins. Gitea also ships a small set of custom helpers:
`gt-` for general helpers and `g-` for framework-level helpers (see
`web_src/css/helpers.css`); use these only when a Tailwind utility does not exist.

Write class attributes as a single readable unit in templates:

```html
<div class="flex-text-inline {{if .IsFoo}}tw-hidden{{end}}"></div>
```

## TypeScript

- Use `import type` for type-only imports.
- Prefer `@ts-expect-error` over `@ts-ignore`.
- Use the `!` non-null assertion (rather than `?.`/`??`) when a value is known to always exist.
- Only mark a function `async` when it actually uses `await` or returns a `Promise`.
  Avoid async event listeners; if unavoidable, call `e.preventDefault()` before the
  first `await`. For a deliberately un-awaited call, assign it: `const _promise = asyncFoo()`.

## Data fetching

Use the `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE` wrappers from
[`web_src/js/modules/fetch.ts`](../web_src/js/modules/fetch.ts).
```

```text
  // * mobile event sequence: focus -> mousedown -> mouseup -> click
  // Fomantic may stop propagation of blur event, use capture to make sure we can still get the event
  let ignoreClickPreEvents = 0, ignoreClickPreVisible = 0;
  dropdown.addEventListener('mousedown', () => {
    ignoreClickPreVisible += isMenuVisible() ? 1 : 0;
    ignoreClickPreEvents++;
  }, {capture: true});
  dropdown.addEventListener('focus', () => {
    ignoreClickPreVisible += isMenuVisible() ? 1 : 0;
    ignoreClickPreEvents++;
    deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem();
  }, {capture: true});
  dropdown.addEventListener('blur', () => {
    ignoreClickPreVisible = ignoreClickPreEvents = 0;
    deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem(100);
  }, {capture: true});
  dropdown.addEventListener('mouseup', () => {
    setTimeout(() => {
      ignoreClickPreVisible = ignoreClickPreEvents = 0;
      deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem(100);
    }, 0);
  }, {capture: true});
  dropdown.addEventListener('click', (e: MouseEvent) => {
    if (isMenuVisible() &&
      ignoreClickPreVisible !== 2 && // dropdown is switch from invisible to visible
      ignoreClickPreEvents === 2 // the click event is related to mousedown+focus
    ) {
      e.stopPropagation(); // if the dropdown menu has been opened by focus, do not trigger the next click event again
    }
    ignoreClickPreEvents = ignoreClickPreVisible = 0;
  }, {capture: true});
}

// Although Fomantic Dropdown supports "hideDividers", it doesn't really work with our "scoped dividers"
// At the moment, "label dropdown items" use scopes, a sample case is:
// * a-label
// * divider
// * scope/1
// * scope/2
// * divider
// * z-label
// when the "scope/*" are filtered out, we'd like to see "a-label" and "z-label" without the divider.
export function hideScopedEmptyDividers(container: Element) {
  const visibleItems: Element[] = [];
  const curScopeVisibleItems: Element[] = [];
  let curScope: string = '', lastVisibleScope: string = '';
  const isDivider = (item: Element) => item.classList.contains('divider');
  const isScopedDivider = (item: Element) => isDivider(item) && item.hasAttribute('data-scope');
  const hideDivider = (item: Element) => item.classList.add('hidden'); // dropdown has its own classes to hide items
  const showDivider = (item: Element) => item.classList.remove('hidden');
  const isHidden = (item: Element) => item.classList.contains('hidden') || item.classList.contains('filtered') || item.classList.contains('tw-hidden');
  const handleScopeSwitch = (itemScope: string) => {
    if (curScopeVisibleItems.length === 1 && isScopedDivider(curScopeVisibleItems[0])) {
      hideDivider(curScopeVisibleItems[0]);
    } else if (curScopeVisibleItems.length) {
      if (isScopedDivider(curScopeVisibleItems[0]) && lastVisibleScope === curScope) {
        hideDivider(curScopeVisibleItems[0]);
        curScopeVisibleItems.shift();
      }
      visibleItems.push(...curScopeVisibleItems);
      lastVisibleScope = curScope;
    }
    curScope = itemScope;
    curScopeVisibleItems.length = 0;
  };

  // reset hidden dividers
  queryElems(container, '.divider', showDivider);

  // hide the scope dividers if the scope items are empty
  for (const item of container.children) {
    const itemScope = item.getAttribute('data-scope') || '';
    if (itemScope !== curScope) {
      handleScopeSwitch(itemScope);
    }
    if (!isHidden(item)) {
      curScopeVisibleItems.push(item);
    }
  }
  handleScopeSwitch('');

const {chromium} = require('/home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea/node_modules/@playwright/test');
(async () => {
  const b = await chromium.launch({executablePath: '/usr/bin/chromium'});
  const ctx = await b.newContext({viewport: {width: 375, height: 800}});
  const p = await ctx.newPage();
  await p.goto('http://localhost:3000/user/login');
  await p.fill('#user_name', 'ai'); await p.fill('#password', 'aiaiaiai');
  await p.click('form .ui.primary.button');

  await p.goto('http://localhost:3000/ai/close-reason-check/issues/29');
  await p.waitForSelector('#status-button');
  const cdp = await ctx.newCDPSession(p);
  await cdp.send('DOM.enable'); await cdp.send('CSS.enable');
  const {root} = await cdp.send('DOM.getDocument', {depth: -1});
  for (const sel of ['#comment-form .ui.buttons > .ui.dropdown', '#status-button']) {
    const {nodeId} = await cdp.send('DOM.querySelector', {nodeId: root.nodeId, selector: sel});
    const res = await cdp.send('CSS.getMatchedStylesForNode', {nodeId});
    console.log('==', sel);
    for (const m of res.matchedCSSRules) {
      const props = m.rule.style.cssProperties.filter(pp => /width|flex|^min|^max/.test(pp.name) && pp.value).map(pp => pp.name + ':' + pp.value);
      if (props.length) console.log(m.rule.selectorList.text.slice(0, 160), '|', (m.rule.media||[]).map(x=>x.text).join(','), '|', props.join('; '));
    }
  }
  await b.close();
})();

// Issues render issues page
func Issues(ctx *context.Context) {
	isPullList := ctx.PathParam("type") == "pulls"
	if isPullList {
		MustAllowPulls(ctx)
		if ctx.Written() {
			return
		}
		ctx.Data["Title"] = ctx.Tr("repo.pulls")
		ctx.Data["PageIsPullList"] = true
		prepareRecentlyPushedNewBranches(ctx)
		if ctx.Written() {
			return
		}
	} else {
		MustEnableIssues(ctx)
		if ctx.Written() {
			return
		}
		ctx.Data["Title"] = ctx.Tr("repo.issues")
		ctx.Data["PageIsIssueList"] = true
		ctx.Data["NewIssueChooseTemplate"] = issue_service.HasTemplatesOrContactLinks(ctx.Repo.Repository, ctx.Repo.GitRepo)
	}
	ctx.Data["BulkCloseReasons"] = issues_model.BulkCloseReasons(isPullList)
	ctx.Data["DefaultCloseReason"] = issues_model.DefaultCloseReason(isPullList)

	projectIDs := parseProjectIDsFromQuery(ctx)

	prepareIssueFilterAndList(ctx, ctx.FormInt64("milestone"), projectIDs, optional.Some(isPullList))
	if ctx.Written() {
		return
	}

	renderMilestones(ctx)
	if ctx.Written() {
		return
	}

	ctx.Data["CanWriteIssuesOrPulls"] = ctx.Repo.Permission.CanWriteIssuesOrPulls(isPullList)

	ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplIssues)
}

  You are reviewing part of a pull request in the Gitea course fork at /home/mont9393/Documents/CSCI435/gitea.
  Branch feat/issue-54-issue-reason-ui, HEAD 7865650a35; the base is origin/main (85a296b0ad). See the whole change with
  `git diff origin/main...HEAD` and one file with `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- <path>`; see the base with `git show origin/main:<path>`.
  
  THE FEATURE (#54): pick a close reason for an issue or pull request in the UI, and show it. #53 (already on main) added the backend: the reason is stored
  on the issue (Issue.CloseReason, CloseReasonText, CloseDuplicateIssueID) and in the close comment's metadata (Comment.MetaCloseReason()); reopening clears
  the issue's reason but the close comment keeps its own. The Go side of #54 was reviewed separately and found clean.
  
  ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
  AC1 plain Close closes an issue as Completed, a PR as Not planned. AC2 the dropdown offers Completed, Not planned, Duplicate, Other for an issue; the same
  without Completed for a PR; merging needs no reason. AC3 the last picked reason is the one saved and shown on the button. AC4 Duplicate: a number that is not
  an issue/PR in the same repo, or is the item itself, is refused with an error and the item stays open; a valid one closes and the timeline links to it.
  AC5 Other: empty or >255 chars refused; otherwise saved and shown as plain text (no HTML/Markdown rendering). AC6 bulk close on the Issues tab offers
  Completed/Not planned and every selected issue closes with it; the PR tab offers only Not planned. AC7 the timeline's close event states the reason, e.g.
  "closed this as not planned", "closed this as a duplicate of #N", "closed this: <text>". AC8 each reason has its own icon/label in lists and on the page;
  items with no reason look exactly as before. AC9 reopening removes the reason's look; the earlier close event keeps its reason. AC10 all new strings come
  from options/locale/locale_en-US.json only, and no other locale file changes.
  
  DELIBERATE DECISIONS (do not report these as bugs unless the implementation contradicts them):
  - The close button on an item's page is a split button: the main button names the reason ("Close as completed"), a ▾ dropdown lists the reasons; menu items
    carry js-aria-clickable so Enter clicks them (see web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts); picking is handled by a plain click listener, not Fomantic onChange.
  - Duplicate and Other open a small tippy popup under the buttons. Popup inputs leave the form while shown, so their values go into hidden form fields that
    are disabled (not sent) unless that reason is picked. An unusable value marks the field with Gitea's red "error" field style; the red message is not
    announced to screen readers (Gitea uses no aria-invalid anywhere) and letters in the number box get the red box with no message: accepted limitations.
  - An inline style rule `overflow: hidden` on the comment form footer was deleted from web_src/css/repo.css because it clipped the menu (Decision 3).

  THE FEATURE (#54): pick a close reason for an issue or pull request in the UI, and show it. #53 (already on main) added the backend: the reason is stored
  on the issue (Issue.CloseReason, CloseReasonText, CloseDuplicateIssueID) and in the close comment's metadata (Comment.MetaCloseReason()); reopening clears
  the issue's reason but the close comment keeps its own. The Go side of #54 was reviewed separately and found clean.
  
  ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
  AC1 plain Close closes an issue as Completed, a PR as Not planned. AC2 the dropdown offers Completed, Not planned, Duplicate, Other for an issue; the same
  without Completed for a PR; merging needs no reason. AC3 the last picked reason is the one saved and shown on the button. AC4 Duplicate: a number that is not
  an issue/PR in the same repo, or is the item itself, is refused with an error and the item stays open; a valid one closes and the timeline links to it.
  AC5 Other: empty or >255 chars refused; otherwise saved and shown as plain text (no HTML/Markdown rendering). AC6 bulk close on the Issues tab offers
  Completed/Not planned and every selected issue closes with it; the PR tab offers only Not planned. AC7 the timeline's close event states the reason, e.g.
  "closed this as not planned", "closed this as a duplicate of #N", "closed this: <text>". AC8 each reason has its own icon/label in lists and on the page;
  items with no reason look exactly as before. AC9 reopening removes the reason's look; the earlier close event keeps its reason. AC10 all new strings come
  from options/locale/locale_en-US.json only, and no other locale file changes.
  
  DELIBERATE DECISIONS (do not report these as bugs unless the implementation contradicts them):
  - The close button on an item's page is a split button: the main button names the reason ("Close as completed"), a ▾ dropdown lists the reasons; menu items
    carry js-aria-clickable so Enter clicks them (see web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts); picking is handled by a plain click listener, not Fomantic onChange.
  - Duplicate and Other open a small tippy popup under the buttons. Popup inputs leave the form while shown, so their values go into hidden form fields that
    are disabled (not sent) unless that reason is picked. An unusable value marks the field with Gitea's red "error" field style; the red message is not
    announced to screen readers (Gitea uses no aria-invalid anywhere) and letters in the number box get the red box with no message: accepted limitations.
  - An inline style rule `overflow: hidden` on the comment form footer was deleted from web_src/css/repo.css because it clipped the menu (Decision 3).
  - Old strings "Close Issue", "Close Pull Request", "Close with Comment" and the bulk toolbar's "Close" (repo.issues.action_close) were deleted as unused (Decision 4).
  - Icons (templates/shared/close_reason_icon.tmpl, Decision 8): completed = purple octicon-issue-closed; not planned = grey octicon-skip; duplicate = grey
    octicon-duplicate; other = grey octicon-note; no reason = red, exactly as before. The state label for "other" says just "Closed" (its text is in the
    timeline). The close event's badge has always used octicon-issue-closed for PRs too, and keeps doing so with no reason. A PR closed as not planned has the
    same icon as an issue closed as not planned. The hover popup on issue links (web_src/js/features/issue.ts) is NOT updated: that is #55, out of scope.
  - Timeline: "closed this as <strong>reason</strong>" like the lock reason's wording; a duplicate gets a detail line with an octicon-duplicate and a link
    "#N Title" (hidden when the server cleared CloseDuplicateIssue because the viewer can't read it); other gets a detail line with octicon-note and the text.
  - The list's bulk Close (templates/repo/issue/filter_actions.tmpl) is the same kind of split button; the PR tab's menu has one item, Not planned (Decision 9).

  FINDINGS:
  [0] (blocker) On screens under 768px wide, the new close-reason dropdown button covers the Comment button — web_src/css/repo.css:573
  A mobile rule already on main, `@media (max-width: 767.98px) { .repository.view.issue .comment-list .comment .content .form .button { width: 100%; margin: 0; } }`, now also matches the new `.ui.dropdown.icon.button` inside the `<div class="ui buttons">` wrapper (templates/repo/issue/view_content.tmpl:108-127). Gitea's `.ui.buttons .button { flex-shrink: 0 }` in web_src/css/modules/button.css stops the group's children from shrinking. So `#status-button` and the dropdown button are each as wide as the whole group (164px at 375px), and the dropdown spills out of the group over `#comment-button`. The dropdown is `position: relative`, so it sits on top and takes the taps. On main the status button was a direct child of the flex row, and the same rule just split the row between the two buttons. Removing `overflow: hidden` from the footer (Decision 3) is not what causes this. It affects every open issue or PR the viewer may close.
  Evidence: Headless Chromium, logged in as ai, with text typed so Comment is enabled. I called elementFromPoint at 15%, 50% and 85% across #comment-button. At 375px all three points hit the close-reason dropdown, on both ai/close-reason-check/issues/31 and ai/close-reason-demo/pulls/9. At 600px two of three hit it, at 767px one of three. Tapping the middle of Comment at 375px on ai/close-reason-check#31 (an issue I created for this test) opened the Completed/Not planned/Duplicate/Other menu and posted nothing: the API showed 0 comments afterwards and the issue still open. To compare with main, I put #status-button back as a direct child of the flex row in the DOM: all three points then hit Comment. In the screenshots at 375px the dropdown button is about 157px wide, and its ▾ shows through the middle of the word "Comment". CDP matched styles show `width:100%` from repo.css:573 on both #status-button and the dropdown.
  
  [1] (nit) The JS hook on the bulk close button is a js- class, not data-global-init like the item page's button — templates/repo/issue/filter_actions.tmpl:8
  The two new split buttons are wired up in different ways. The one on an item's page uses the declarative `data-global-init="initRepoIssueStatusButton"` (view_content.tmpl:108). The bulk one on the list uses a `js-issue-list-close-reason` class, picked up by `queryElems(document, '.js-issue-list-close-reason', initIssueListCloseReason)` inside initRepoIssueList. The course doc says new code should prefer `data-global-init` (.claude-students/docs/frontend-js.md, "Two ways to wire a feature, and new code should prefer the second"), and main follows that almost everywhere.
  Evidence: On origin/main, `registerGlobalInitFunc(` appears 32 times in web_src/js. The `queryElems(document, '.js-…')` pattern appears once (repo-common.ts:150, js-btn-clone-panel). This branch adds the second one, in repo-issue-list.ts:242.
  
  [2] (nit) Conditional classes are glued to the class before them, against the documented single-readable-unit style — templates/repo/issue/view_content.tmpl:119
  docs/guidelines-frontend.md and .claude-students/docs/frontend-css.md both ask for class attributes to be written as one readable unit: `class="flex-text-inline {{if .IsFoo}}tw-hidden{{end}}"`, with a space before the {{if}}. The new markup glues the condition onto the class before it in three places: view_content.tmpl:119 and filter_actions.tmpl:15 (`class="item js-aria-clickable{{if eq . $.DefaultCloseReason}} selected{{end}}"`), and close_reason_icon.tmpl:31 (`class="badge{{if $badgeClass}} {{$badgeClass}}{{end}}"`). Fomantic's `.ui.form .inline.field > :first-child { margin: 0 0.857em 0 0 }` (web_src/css/modules/form.css:359-362) gives the label an 11px right margin. The flex-text-block gap adds another 7px on top. That is the per-child margin plus flex gap that AGENTS.md's "prefer flex-* helpers over per-child margins" is meant to avoid. Here it also pushes the "#" at the end of the label away from the number it belongs to. Nothing in the JS reads `inline`; the red error style only needs `.field`.

new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..56d693e910
--- /dev/null
+++ b/templates/shared/close_reason_icon.tmpl
@@ -0,0 +1,32 @@
+{{/* The look of a closed issue or pull request by why it was closed: its icon in lists, its state label on its page,
+and the badge of its close event in the timeline. A close without a reason (from before close reasons, a merge,
+an automatic close) keeps the red closed look it always had. Purple means done, as for a merged pull request;
+grey means set aside, as for a draft or a skipped job.
+
+Template Attributes:
+* Reason: the issues.CloseReason, of the item for "list" and "label", of the close event for "badge"
+* IsPull: whether the item is a pull request
+* For: "list" (the icon alone), "label" (the state label with its text) or "badge" (the timeline badge)
+
+The hover popup on issue links (getIssueIcon in web_src/js/features/issue.ts) doesn't show reasons yet: it reads the API.
+*/}}
+{{- $reason := .Reason.String -}}
+{{- $icon := Iif .IsPull "octicon-git-pull-request-closed" "octicon-issue-closed" -}}
+{{- if eq .For "badge" -}}{{- $icon = "octicon-issue-closed" -}}{{- end -}}{{/* the close event's badge has always used it for pull requests too */}}
+{{- $iconClass := "tw-text-red" -}}{{- $labelColor := "red" -}}{{- $badgeClass := "tw-bg-red tw-text-white" -}}
+{{- if eq $reason "completed" -}}
+	{{- $icon = "octicon-issue-closed" -}}{{- $iconClass = "tw-text-purple" -}}{{- $labelColor = "purple" -}}{{- $badgeClass = "tw-bg-purple tw-text-white" -}}
+{{- else if eq $reason "not_planned" -}}
+	{{- $icon = "octicon-skip" -}}{{- $iconClass = "tw-text-text-light" -}}{{- $labelColor = "grey" -}}{{- $badgeClass = "" -}}
+{{- else if eq $reason "duplicate" -}}
+	{{- $icon = "octicon-duplicate" -}}{{- $iconClass = "tw-text-text-light" -}}{{- $labelColor = "grey" -}}{{- $badgeClass = "" -}}
+{{- else if eq $reason "other" -}}
+	{{- $icon = "octicon-note" -}}{{- $iconClass = "tw-text-text-light" -}}{{- $labelColor = "grey" -}}{{- $badgeClass = "" -}}
+{{- end -}}
+{{- if eq .For "list" -}}
+	{{- svg $icon 16 $iconClass -}}
+{{- else if eq .For "label" -}}
+	<div class="ui {{$labelColor}} label issue-state-label">{{svg $icon}} {{if and $reason (ne $reason "other")}}{{ctx.Locale.Tr (printf "repo.issues.closed_title_as.%s" $reason)}}{{else}}{{ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.issues.closed_title"}}{{end}}</div>
+{{- else -}}
+	<span class="badge{{if $badgeClass}} {{$badgeClass}}{{end}}">{{svg $icon}}</span>
+{{- end -}}

## Conventions & invariants

**Two ways to wire a feature, and new code should prefer the second.**

1. *Page-load init:* export `initFoo()` from a `features/` file and add it to the array in
   `index.ts`. Every function in that array runs on **every** page, so it must find its elements
   and return immediately when they are absent.
2. *Declarative:* `registerGlobalInitFunc('initFoo', (el) => {...})` in the module, and
   `data-global-init="initFoo"` on the element in the template. For clicks,
   `registerGlobalEventFunc('click', 'onFoo', ...)` with `data-global-click="onFoo"`. This covers
   elements added to the DOM later and runs once per element (guarded by an internal
   `_giteaGlobalInited` flag), so re-adding a node does not re-initialise it.

`registerGlobalSelectorFunc(selector, handler)` also exists, but `observer.ts` marks it as "less
efficient and less maintainable" — it is for element types already spread across many pages, not
for new work.

- **Ordering rule:** every `registerGlobalInitFunc` must run *before* `initGlobalSelectorObserver`,
  which `index.ts` deliberately calls last. Registering after it throws.
- **One function per element.** `callGlobalInitFunc` in `observer.ts` looks the attribute up as a
  whole string, so `data-global-init` names exactly one function — space-separating two is an open
  TODO there, not a feature. To add behaviour to an element that already has one (the new-issue
  title in `templates/repo/issue/new_form.tmpl` carries `autoFocusEnd`), put the attribute on a
  wrapper and query for the inner element.
- Data fetching goes through the `fetch.ts` wrappers, never a raw `fetch`.
- Show and hide with `.tw-hidden` plus `showElem` / `hideElem` / `toggleElem`. In Vue use
  `v-if`/`v-show` instead (`frontend-vue-components.md`).
- Use `node.getAttribute`, not `node.dataset` (camel-casing surprises), and never bind
  user-provided data onto a DOM node.
- Custom DOM events are prefixed `ce-`, declared as an exported constant next to their emitter —
  see `EventEditorContentChanged` in `features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts`.
- TypeScript, per `docs/guidelines-frontend.md`: `import type` for type-only imports,
  `@ts-expect-error` over `@ts-ignore`, `!` rather than `?.`/`??` when a value always exists, and
  `async` only on a function that actually awaits.
- One feature per file or directory; ids and classes are kebab-case with 2-3 feature keywords.

## Recipes

**Add behaviour to an element.** Register a global init func in the owning `features/` module and
put `data-global-init="yourFuncName"` on the element in its template. No change to `index.ts`.

**Add a whole-page feature.** New `features/<name>.ts` exporting `initName()`, an early return when
its root element is missing, then add the import and the array entry in `index.ts`.

```text
# Issue #54 — design decisions

Entries marked *(proposed)* are not decided yet.



### Decision 9: The list's Close button works like the one on an issue's page

**Decision:** When items are selected on the issue or pull request list, Close becomes the same button as on an item's page: it names its reason ("Close as completed"), and the ▾ beside it changes the reason before closing. The Issues tab offers Completed and Not planned, and the Pull Requests tab offers only Not planned, in the same kind of menu (AC6).
**Alternatives Considered:** A menu whose items close straight away, like the Labels and Milestone menus beside it; and on the Pull Requests tab, a plain "Close as not planned" button with no ▾.
**Rationale:** Closing works the same way everywhere, and the button always says what it will do. Both menus come from the reasons the model allows, leaving out Duplicate and Other, whose number or description belongs to a single item; so a new reason shows up without changing the page.
**Consequences:** The Pull Requests tab's menu holds a single item for now. A reason the server refuses, which only a hand-made request can send, is handled like a blocked dependency: the items before it stay closed, and the page shows no message until the toolbar's existing error bug is fixed.
```
</details></tool-use>

> Fomantic-UI is not an accessibility-friendly framework. Gitea patches some ARIA
> behavior, but accessibility work is ongoing — prefer semantic HTML and test
> keyboard/screen-reader behavior where you can.

## Gitea-specific conventions

- Keep features in their own files or directories.
- Use kebab-case for HTML `id`s and classes, ideally with 2-3 feature keywords.
- Prefix classes to avoid short-name conflicts between different frameworks.
- Create a new class name when overriding framework styles instead of editing the framework's own classes,
  or fix the framework's source to fix all cases.
- Prefer semantic elements such as `<button>` over generic `<div>`s.
- Avoid `!important`; when it is unavoidable, document why.
- Prefix custom DOM events with `ce-`.

## CSS

Prefer Tailwind utility classes with the `tw-` prefix, and the `flex-*` layout
helpers over per-child margins. Gitea also ships a small set of custom helpers:
`gt-` for general helpers and `g-` for framework-level helpers (see
`web_src/css/helpers.css`); use these only when a Tailwind utility does not exist.

Write class attributes as a single readable unit in templates:

```html
<div class="flex-text-inline {{if .IsFoo}}tw-hidden{{end}}"></div>
```

## TypeScript

- Use `import type` for type-only imports.
- Prefer `@ts-expect-error` over `@ts-ignore`.
- Use the `!` non-null assertion (rather than `?.`/`??`) when a value is known to always exist.
- Only mark a function `async` when it actually uses `await` or returns a `Promise`.
  Avoid async event listeners; if unavoidable, call `e.preventDefault()` before the
  first `await`. For a deliberately un-awaited call, assign it: `const _promise = asyncFoo()`.

## Data fetching

Use the `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE` wrappers from
[`web_src/js/modules/fetch.ts`](../web_src/js/modules/fetch.ts).
----
- Avoid `!important`; where it is unavoidable, leave a comment saying why. The existing `gt-`
  helpers use it deliberately, which is why they win over framework rules.
- Class and id names are kebab-case with two or three feature keywords, prefixed to avoid
  collisions between frameworks.
- In a template, write the class attribute as one readable unit rather than concatenating:

  ```html
  <div class="flex-text-inline {{if .IsFoo}}tw-hidden{{end}}"></div>
  ```

- `tw-hidden` is also the show/hide mechanism used by `showElem`/`hideElem` in
  `frontend-js.md` — do not reuse it as a generic styling class.

## Recipes
  replacement instead. `templates/repo/issue/list_grouped.tmpl` renders each group this way.
- Mail templates use a different, smaller function set — `mailBodyFuncMap` and
  `mailSubjectTextFuncMap` in `modules/templates/mail.go`. A helper added for pages is not
  available in `templates/mail/`.
- Class attributes are written as one readable unit including their conditionals
  (`frontend-css.md`).
- Hook frontend behaviour up declaratively with `data-global-init` / `data-global-click`
  attributes rather than inline script (`frontend-js.md`).
- `.tmpl` files are tab-indented (`.editorconfig`).
```

```text
===== rendering findings: 1
- [blocker] At phone widths the ▾ reason button covers the Comment button on any open issue or PR (templates/repo/issue/view_content.tmpl:108) introduced=True
  VERDICT real=True introduced=True deliberate=False sev=blocker
  why: s comes from the branch's wrapper, not from main. The split button is a deliberate decision, but nothing says the mobile overlap is.

The Reopen claim also holds: /issues/1 at 380px is 126x60 with the text wrapping to 3 lines, against 164x46 with main's markup. That is cosmetic only.

One small correction: the report says the problem stops at 768px. It is narrower than that, but not all fine above it. At 768-850px (sidebar layout, text typed), the group's 314px of non-shrinking width squeezes Comment to 42-95px, and its label is clipped ('ommen' in the screenshot at 800px). Main's markup keeps it at 103px. At 900px and up, and at 1280px, it is identical to main.

Severity: I keep it as a blocker. On the 360-380px phone widths that most phones use, every open issue or PR that the viewer can close loses its main Comment action: tapping where Comment should be opens the reason menu instead.
===== security-a11y findings: 0
checked: I found nothing to report. I checked the branch's markup for escaping and accessibility problems, both by reading the templates and on the local instance.

ESCAPING
- How the translation call handles values (modules/translation/i18n/localestore.go:152-166): ctx.Locale.Tr HTML-escapes any plain string it is given and passes only already-safe HTML through. The new timeline strings (repo.issues.closed_as.*) are given only .EventTag (a string, so escaped) and $createdStr (already-safe HTML), the same as the existing closed_at line.
- The Other text and the duplicate's title never go through Tr. They are printed directly in comments.tmpl:119 and :125. MetaCloseReason().Text is a plain string (models/issues/comment.go:785), so html/template escapes it.
- Every data-* and aria attribute the templates fill holds either a fixed reason name (data-value, data-close-reason) or a translated string (data-status, data-status-and-comment, data-locale-*, aria-label, placeholder). In an attribute, html/template strips tags from translated strings and escapes quotes. For example the server sends data-locale-self="Can&#39;t be a duplicate of itself". No template value lands in a script context.
- The 
===== conventions findings: 4
- [blocker] On screens under 768px wide, the new close-reason dropdown button covers the Comment button (web_src/css/repo.css:573) introduced=True
  desc: A mobile rule already on main, `@media (max-width: 767.98px) { .repository.view.issue .comment-list .comment .content .form .button { width: 100%; margin: 0; } }`, now also matches the new `.ui.dropdown.icon.button` inside the `<div class="ui buttons">` wrapper (templates/repo/issue/view_content.tmpl:108-127). Gitea's `.ui.buttons .button { flex-shrink: 0 }` in web_src/css/modules/button.css stops the group's children from shrinking. So `#status-button` and the dropdown button are each as wide as the whole group (164px at 375px), and the dropdown spills out of the group over `#comment-button`. The dropdown is `position: relative`, so it sits on top and takes the taps. On main the status button was a direct child of the flex row, and the same rule just split the row between the two buttons. Removing `overflow: hidden` from the footer (Decision 3) is not what causes this. It affects every open issue or PR the viewer may close.
  fix: In the same media block in repo.css, give the split button its own sizing, for example:
  .repository.view.issue .comment-list .comment .content .form .ui.buttons { width: 100%; }
  .repository.view.issue .comment-list .comment .content .form .ui.buttons > .button { width: auto; }
  .repository.view.issue .comment-list .comment .content .form .ui.buttons > .button:first-child { flex: 1; }
I injected exactly this CSS and checked it: at 375, 600 and 767px every point hits Comment, and the ▾ stays icon-wide. Another option is to narrow the old selector so it skips `.ui.buttons > .button`.
  VERDICT real=True introduced=True deliberate=False sev=blocker
  why: opdown's ▾ shows where Comment should be. PR #9 gives the same result at 375px (two of three points). To compare with main, I moved #status-button back to be a direct child of the flex row and removed the group in the DOM: all three points then hit Comment at 375, 600 and 767px, with the two buttons splitting the row (161/161 at 375px). The cause is the new button-group markup, not Decision 3 (the deleted overflow rule). On a phone, anyone who may close an open issue or PR cannot tap Comment, which is a real regression, so blocker is a fair severity. I did not repeat the reviewer's tap-and-post test, because the rules forbid creating comments in close-reason-demo; the hit tests and the screenshot are enough. Part 2 found one real bug, and it's my miss: **on a phone, the new ▾ button covers the Comment button.** I reproduced it myself:

| Screen width | Where a tap on "Comment" lands |
| --- | --- |
| 360px (most phones) | on the ▾; Comment isn't visible at all |
| 414px, 600px | on the ▾ |
| 800px | on Comment, but it's squeezed to 45px wide (103px on `main`) |
| 1280px | on Comment, same as `main` |

At 360px the comment form shows only "Close as completed with comment" and a wide ▾, with no Comment button. So on a phone, anyone who can close an open issue or PR can't post a comment.

**Cause:** step 2 wrapped the Close button in a button group. An older mobile rule in `repo.css` makes every button in that form full-width below 768px, and buttons inside a group can't shrink, so both halves of the group spill over Comment. My earlier phone checks looked at the popup and the menu, never the Comment button next to them. Two reviewers found it independently, and both skeptics confirmed it.

**How to fix it (your call):**
- **A (my lean):** add a rule for the button group inside the same mobile block of `repo.css`. The group takes its share of the row, the ▾ stays icon-sized, and the Close half shrinks and wraps its text. A reviewer tested this by injecting the CSS: Comment was fully tappable at 360, 375, 600 and 767px. It adds to Gitea's rule rather than changing it.
- **B:** narrow Gitea's existing mobile rule so it skips buttons inside a group. That edits a rule that was already on `main`.

Either way it's a new commit. I'd check it at several widths in the browser, and could also add a Playwright test at phone width, which CI would run. Do you want that test?

**Three small style points** (all confirmed, all cosmetic):
1. The bulk button is switched on with a `js-` class instead of `data-global-init`, which the course doc prefers for new code. I had copied the toolbar's other buttons.
2. Three `class="… {{if}}"` spots glue the conditional class to the previous one. Gitea's style guide wants a space before the `{{if}}`.
3. The duplicate popup has 18px between "Duplicate of #" and the number box, because a Fomantic `inline` margin and a flex gap add up.

**Clean:**
- **Escaping and accessibility:** no findings, including hostile text tried on your instance.
- **Rendering:** every page that uses the changed templates renders right, in light and dark themes.
- **Locale strings:** every key exists, and the deleted ones are used nowhere.
- **The CSS removal:** taking out `overflow: hidden` didn't affect anything else.

**Tokens:** Part 2 used about 562k (5 agents, about 19 minutes), so Parts 1 and 2 together come to about 920k.

How do you want to go: fix the phone bug now (A or B, with or without the test), and the three style points (all, some or none)? Or carry on with Part 3 (the TypeScript) first?

  const repoName = `e2e-issue-comment-${randomString(8)}`;

  await apiCreateRepo(request, {name: repoName, autoInit: false});

  await expect(page.getByRole('button', {name: 'Comment', exact: true})).toBeDisabled();
  await page.getByRole('button', {name: 'Close as completed'}).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('button', {name: 'Reopen Issue'})).toBeVisible();
});

function initRepoBranchTagSelector() {

    createApp(RepoBranchTagSelector, {elRoot}).mount(elRoot);

export function initBranchSelectorTabs() {
  const elSelectBranches = document.querySelectorAll('.ui.dropdown.select-branch');
  for (const elSelectBranch of elSelectBranches) {
    queryElems(elSelectBranch, '.reference.column', (el) => el.addEventListener('click', () => {
      hideElem(elSelectBranch.querySelectorAll('.scrolling.reference-list-menu'));
      showElem(el.getAttribute('data-target')!);
      queryElemChildren(el.parentNode!, '.branch-tag-item', (el) => el.classList.remove('active'));
      el.classList.add('active');
    }));
  }
}

export function initRepository() {
  registerGlobalInitFunc('initRepoPullMergeBox', initRepoPullMergeBox);
  registerGlobalInitFunc('initRepoPullRequestUpdate', initRepoPullRequestUpdate);
  registerGlobalInitFunc('initRepoIssueStatusButton', initRepoIssueStatusButton);

    const c = document.querySelector('#comment-button');

    const hit = cb ? document.elementFromPoint(cb.left + cb.width / 2, cb.top + cb.height / 2) : null;
    return {status: box('#status-button'), menu: box('#comment-form .ui.dropdown.icon.button'), comment: box('#comment-button'), commentHit: hit ? (hit === c || c.contains(hit)) : null};

        const page = await ctx.newPage();

      console.log(`${label.padEnd(12)} ${String(width).padStart(4)}px | branch: status ${fmt(b.status)} ▾ ${fmt(b.menu)} Comment ${fmt(b.comment)} hit=${b.commentHit} | main-like: status ${fmt(m.status)} Comment ${fmt(m.comment)} hit=${m.commentHit}`);
    }
  }
  await browser.close();
})();

export const timeoutFactor = Number(env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_TIMEOUT_FACTOR) || 1;

export function baseUrl() {
  return env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_URL?.replace(/\/$/g, '');
}

function apiAuthHeader(username: string, password: string) {
  return {Authorization: `Basic ${globalThis.btoa(`${username}:${password}`)}`};
}

export function apiHeaders() {
  return apiAuthHeader(env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER, env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_PASSWORD);
}

async function apiRetry(fn: () => Promise<{ok: () => boolean; status: () => number; text: () => Promise<string>}>, label: string) {
  const maxAttempts = 5;
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < maxAttempts; attempt++) {
    const response = await fn();
    if (response.ok()) return;
    if ([500, 502, 503].includes(response.status()) && attempt < maxAttempts - 1) {
      const jitter = Math.random() * 500;
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1000 * (attempt + 1) + jitter));
      continue;
    }
    throw new Error(`${label} failed: ${response.status()} ${await response.text()}`);
  }
}

export async function apiCreateRepo(requestContext: APIRequestContext, {name, autoInit = true, headers}: {name: string; autoInit?: boolean; headers?: Record<string, string>}) {
  await apiRetry(() => requestContext.post(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1/user/repos`, {
    headers: headers || apiHeaders(),
}

export async function loginUser(page: Page, username: string) {
  return login(page, username, testUserPassword);
}

export async function login(page: Page, username = env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER, password = env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_PASSWORD) {
  const response = await page.request.post('/user/login', {
    form: {user_name: username, password},
    maxRedirects: 0,
  });
  const status = response.status();
  if (status !== 302 && status !== 303) throw new Error(`login as ${username} failed: HTTP ${status}`);
}

**You invent a new `--color-` name in a theme file and the build rejects it.** `tailwind.config.ts`
and `stylelint.config.ts` learn the list of valid colour names by reading `base.css` and the two
`theme-gitea-*` files, and nothing else. A name that appears only in your theme is unknown to both:
`make lint-css` fails, and no `tw-` utility is generated for it. A theme may freely *change* an
existing colour — it may not add one.

**A dropdown opens, but its menu never appears.** The menu of a `ui dropdown` lives inside the
dropdown, so any box around it with `overflow: hidden` cuts it off. Nothing errors: the click works,
the menu is just invisible. Look for an `overflow: hidden` on a parent. The small menus built with
tippy (`web_src/js/modules/tippy.ts`) are attached to the page itself, so this never happens to them.

    16	// refused (the issue itself, or no such issue) is never sent with its comment; if the search fails, the server decides.
    17	function initDuplicatePreview(elPreview: HTMLElement, elInput: HTMLInputElement, onResize: () => void, onAccepted: (number: string) => void) {
    18	  const {ownerName, repoName, indexString} = parseIssueHref(window.location.href);
    19	  const elField = elPreview.closest('.field')!;
    20	  let wantedNumber = ''; // an answer that arrives for an older number is dropped
    21	  const show = (...children: Array<Node | string>) => {
    22	    elField.classList.remove('error');
    23	    elPreview.replaceChildren(...children);
    24	    toggleElem(elPreview, children.length > 0);
    25	    onResize(); // the popup grows or shrinks with the preview

    28	  const showError = (text: string) => {
    29	    show(createElementFromAttrs('span', {class: 'tw-text-red'}, text));
    30	    elField.classList.add('error');
    31	  };
    32	  const lookUp = debounce(async (number: string) => {
    33	    let issues: Issue[];
    34	    try {
    35	      issues = await matchIssue(ownerName, repoName, indexString, number);
    36	    } catch {
    37	      if (number !== wantedNumber) return;
    38	      show(); // no preview then, and the server checks the number on close
    39	      onAccepted(number);
    40	      return;
    41	    }
    42	    if (number !== wantedNumber) return;
    43	    const issue = issues.find((i) => String(i.number) === number);
    44	    if (issue) {
    45	      show(
    46	        createElementFromHTML(svg(getIssueIcon(issue), 16, [getIssueColorClass(issue)])),
    47	        `#${issue.number}`,

    49	      );
    50	      onAccepted(number);
    51	    } else {

    53	    }
    54	  }, 300); // the same delay as the # list

    56	  // a number box reads letters as '', so for those there is nothing to name and only the box is marked
    57	  const showUnusable = () => {
    58	    if (elInput.value) {

    60	    } else {
    61	      show();
    62	      elField.classList.add('error');
    63	    }
    64	  };
    65	  const update = () => {

    75	    } else {

    77	    }
    78	  };

    80	}

    84	// While the item is open, the menu beside it picks the close reason: the button then takes that reason's texts,

```text
1	---
2	scope: web_src/js/index.ts, web_src/js/features, web_src/js/modules, web_src/js/utils, web_src/js/webcomponents, web_src/js/markup, web_src/js/render

4	---
5	
6	# web_src/js — page features and how they get wired up
7	
8	**Read when:** adding or changing browser behaviour on a page.
9	**Not here:** Vue components -> `frontend-vue-components.md`; styling -> `frontend-css.md`; the HTML -> `templates.md`.
10	
11	## Responsibilities
12	
13	| Directory | Owns |
14	| --- | --- |
15	| `features/` | one file per page or feature (`repo-issue.ts`, `repo-diff.ts`, `repo-code.ts`), plus `features/admin/` and `features/comp/` for shared widgets |
16	| `modules/` | cross-cutting infrastructure: `fetch.ts`, `init.ts`, `observer.ts`, `i18n.ts`, `toast.ts`, `tippy.ts`, `fomantic.ts`, `clipboard.ts`, `codeeditor/` |
17	| `utils/` | pure helpers with no DOM assumptions: `dom.ts`, `html.ts`, `url.ts`, `time.ts`, `color.ts`, `string.ts` |
18	| `markup/`, `render/` | enhancing already-rendered content (anchors, mermaid, math) |
19	| `webcomponents/` | custom elements such as `relative-time`, `overflow-menu` |
20	
21	## Key files
22	
23	| Path | What it holds |
24	| --- | --- |
25	| `web_src/js/index.ts` | the entry point: imports fomantic and `../css/index.css`, then passes every `initXxx` to `callInitFunctions` |
26	| `web_src/js/modules/init.ts` | `callInitFunctions`, `InitPerformanceTracer` |
27	| `web_src/js/modules/observer.ts` | `registerGlobalInitFunc`, `registerGlobalEventFunc`, `registerGlobalSelectorFunc`, `initGlobalSelectorObserver` |
28	| `web_src/js/modules/fetch.ts` | `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` |
29	| `web_src/js/utils/dom.ts` | `showElem`, `hideElem`, `toggleElem`, `queryElems`, `createElementFromHTML` |
30	| `web_src/js/modules/i18n.ts` | `trN` — the frontend side of the locale system |
31	
32	## Conventions & invariants
33	
34	**Two ways to wire a feature, and new code should prefer the second.**
35	
36	1. *Page-load init:* export `initFoo()` from a `features/` file and add it to the array in
37	   `index.ts`. Every function in that array runs on **every** page, so it must find its elements
38	   and return immediately when they are absent.
39	2. *Declarative:* `registerGlobalInitFunc('initFoo', (el) => {...})` in the module, and
40	   `data-global-init="initFoo"` on the element in the template. For clicks,
41	   `registerGlobalEventFunc('click', 'onFoo', ...)` with `data-global-click="onFoo"`. This covers
42	   elements added to the DOM later and runs once per element (guarded by an internal
43	   `_giteaGlobalInited` flag), so re-adding a node does not re-initialise it.
44	
45	`registerGlobalSelectorFunc(selector, handler)` also exists, but `observer.ts` marks it as "less
46	efficient and less maintainable" — it is for element types already spread across many pages, not
47	for new work.
48	
49	- **Ordering rule:** every `registerGlobalInitFunc` must run *before* `initGlobalSelectorObserver`,
50	  which `index.ts` deliberately calls last. Registering after it throws.
51	- **One function per element.** `callGlobalInitFunc` in `observer.ts` looks the attribute up as a
52	  whole string, so `data-global-init` names exactly one function — space-separating two is an open
53	  TODO there, not a feature. To add behaviour to an element that already has one (the new-issue
54	  title in `templates/repo/issue/new_form.tmpl` carries `autoFocusEnd`), put the attribute on a
55	  wrapper and query for the inner element.
56	- Data fetching goes through the `fetch.ts` wrappers, never a raw `fetch`.
57	- Show and hide with `.tw-hidden` plus `showElem` / `hideElem` / `toggleElem`. In Vue use
58	  `v-if`/`v-show` instead (`frontend-vue-components.md`).
59	- Use `node.getAttribute`, not `node.dataset` (camel-casing surprises), and never bind
60	  user-provided data onto a DOM node.
61	- Custom DOM events are prefixed `ce-`, declared as an exported constant next to their emitter —
62	  see `EventEditorContentChanged` in `features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts`.
63	- TypeScript, per `docs/guidelines-frontend.md`: `import type` for type-only imports,
64	  `@ts-expect-error` over `@ts-ignore`, `!` rather than `?.`/`??` when a value always exists, and
65	  `async` only on a function that actually awaits.
66	- One feature per file or directory; ids and classes are kebab-case with 2-3 feature keywords.
67	
68	## Recipes
69	
70	**Add behaviour to an element.** Register a global init func in the owning `features/` module and
71	put `data-global-init="yourFuncName"` on the element in its template. No change to `index.ts`.
72	
73	**Add a whole-page feature.** New `features/<name>.ts` exporting `initName()`, an early return when
74	its root element is missing, then add the import and the array entry in `index.ts`.
75	
76	**Profile a slow page.** Append `?_ui_performance_trace=1` to the URL to print per-init timings.
77	`index.ts` already logs an error when total init exceeds 500ms.
78	
79	**Look up an issue by its number.** `matchIssue` (`utils/match.ts`) is the `#` list's search: a
80	number comes back first (`services/issue/suggestion.go` → `GetSuggestion`), the current issue is
81	left out, and only what the viewer may read is returned (`routers/web/repo/issue_suggestions.go`).
82	The duplicate close reason's preview in `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` uses it.
83	
84	**Run one test file.** `pnpm exec vitest <path-filter>` (`testing.md`).
85	
86	## Gotchas
87	
88	- Forgetting the early return in a page-load init means that feature's cost is paid on every page
89	  in Gitea, which is what the 500ms warning is there to catch.
90	- Fomantic-UI (jQuery) is vendored and deprecated. Do not build new features on it, and do not mix
91	  it with Vue — Vue may use its CSS classes but not its JavaScript.
92	- `utils/` is for pure helpers. A function that reaches for `window` or a global selector belongs
93	  in `modules/` or `features/`.
94	- A feature can follow a comment box it did not create: the editor's change and upload events
95	  bubble (`features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts`, `features/comp/EditorUpload.ts`), and
96	  `getComboMarkdownEditor` finds the editor, as `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` does. But
97	  the editor attaches itself before its async `init` finishes, and calling it before then throws;
98	  read its textarea until an event arrives.
99	- Enter on a Fomantic dropdown item only fires a `click` when the item is a link or carries
100	  `js-aria-clickable` (`web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts`), so a plain click listener on other
101	  items never hears a keyboard pick. `templates/repo/issue/view_content/context_menu.tmpl` and the
102	  close reason menu in `templates/repo/issue/view_content.tmpl` mark their items.
103	- After a click on a Fomantic dropdown item, the dropdown keeps the focus, so focusing something
104	  else from your click handler needs `setTimeout(..., 0)`.
105	- `createTippy` (`modules/tippy.ts`) moves a popup to `document.body`, so inputs in it leave their
106	  `<form>` and are not sent. Keep their values in hidden fields inside the form, as the close reason
107	  popups in `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` do.
108	
109	## Related
110	
111	- `frontend-vue-components.md` — when a feature should be a Vue app instead
112	- `templates.md` — where `data-global-init` attributes and `pageData` come from
113	- `frontend-css.md` — `tw-hidden` and the class conventions
114
```

+import {initIssueListCloseReason} from './repo-issue-list.ts';
+import {createElementFromHTML} from '../utils/dom.ts';
+
+// the markup the Issues tab's toolbar gets while open issues are listed
+function createCloseButtons() {
+  const elButtons = createElementFromHTML<HTMLElement>(`
+    <div class="ui red basic buttons" data-global-init="initIssueListCloseReason">
+      <button class="ui button issue-action" data-action="close" data-url="/user2/repo1/issues/status" data-close-reason="completed">Close as completed</button>
+      <div class="ui dropdown icon button">
+        <div class="menu">
+          <div class="item js-aria-clickable selected" data-value="completed" data-status="Close as completed">Completed</div>
+          <div class="item js-aria-clickable" data-value="not_planned" data-status="Close as not planned">Not planned</div>
+        </div>
+      </div>
+    </div>`);
+  initIssueListCloseReason(elButtons);
+  const closeButton = elButtons.querySelector('.issue-action')!;
+  const pick = (reason: string) => elButtons.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`.item[data-value="${CSS.escape(reason)}"]`)!.click();
+  return {elButtons, closeButton, pick};
+}
+
+test('picking a reason gives the Close button that reason and its text', () => {
+  const {closeButton, pick} = createCloseButtons();
+  pick('not_planned');
+  expect(closeButton.getAttribute('data-close-reason')).toEqual('not_planned');
+  expect(closeButton.textContent).toEqual('Close as not planned');
+  pick('completed'); // the reason can still be changed before closing
+  expect(closeButton.getAttribute('data-close-reason')).toEqual('completed');
+  expect(closeButton.textContent).toEqual('Close as completed');
+});
+
+test('a click in the menu that misses every item changes nothing', () => {
+  const {elButtons, closeButton} = createCloseButtons();
+  elButtons.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.menu')!.click();
+  expect(closeButton.getAttribute('data-close-reason')).toEqual('completed');
+  expect(closeButton.textContent).toEqual('Close as completed');
+});

     4	import {svg} from '../svg.ts';
     5	import {parseIssueHref} from '../utils.ts';
     6	import {createElementFromAttrs, createElementFromHTML, toggleElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';
     7	import {matchIssue} from '../utils/match.ts';
     8	import {debounce} from 'perfect-debounce';
     9	import type {Instance} from 'tippy.js';
    10	import type {Issue} from '../types.ts';
    11	
    12	type ReasonPopup = {reason: string, field: HTMLInputElement, elPopup: HTMLElement, elInput: HTMLInputElement, isUsable: () => boolean, markUnusable: () => void, tippy: Instance};
    13	
    14	// Shows the issue with the typed number beside the duplicate box, found by the same search as the comment box's # list,
    15	// which only returns what the viewer can read. A number is accepted once that issue is found, so a close that would be
    16	// refused (the issue itself, or no such issue) is never sent with its comment; if the search fails, the server decides.
    17	function initDuplicatePreview(elPreview: HTMLElement, elInput: HTMLInputElement, onResize: () => void, onAccepted: (number: string) => void) {
    18	  const {ownerName, repoName, indexString} = parseIssueHref(window.location.href);
    19	  const elField = elPreview.closest('.field')!;
    20	  let wantedNumber = ''; // an answer that arrives for an older number is dropped
    21	  const show = (...children: Array<Node | string>) => {
    22	    elField.classList.remove('error');
    23	    elPreview.replaceChildren(...children);
    24	    toggleElem(elPreview, children.length > 0);
    25	    onResize(); // the popup grows or shrinks with the preview
    26	  };
    27	  // a number that can't be used: Gitea's red "error" field around the box, and the reason in red beside it
    28	  const showError = (text: string) => {
    29	    show(createElementFromAttrs('span', {class: 'tw-text-red'}, text));
    30	    elField.classList.add('error');
    31	  };
    32	  const lookUp = debounce(async (number: string) => {
    33	    let issues: Issue[];
    34	    try {
    35	      issues = await matchIssue(ownerName, repoName, indexString, number);
    36	    } catch {
    37	      if (number !== wantedNumber) return;
    38	      show(); // no preview then, and the server checks the number on close
    39	      onAccepted(number);
    40	      return;
    41	    }
    42	    if (number !== wantedNumber) return;
    43	    const issue = issues.find((i) => String(i.number) === number);
    44	    if (issue) {
    45	      show(
    46	        createElementFromHTML(svg(getIssueIcon(issue), 16, [getIssueColorClass(issue)])),
    47	        `#${issue.number}`,
    48	        createElementFromAttrs('span', {class: 'gt-ellipsis'}, issue.title), // a text node, so a title can't inject markup
    49	      );
    50	      onAccepted(number);
    51	    } else {
    52	      showError(elPreview.getAttribute('data-locale-not-found')!.replace('%s', number));
    53	    }
    54	  }, 300); // the same delay as the # list
    55	  // text, or a number like 0, -3 or 1.5, gets the same error as a number with no issue;
    56	  // a number box reads letters as '', so for those there is nothing to name and only the box is marked
    57	  const showUnusable = () => {
    58	    if (elInput.value) {
    59	      showError(elPreview.getAttribute('data-locale-not-found')!.replace('%s', elInput.value));
    60	    } else {
    61	      show();
    62	      elField.classList.add('error');
    63	    }
    64	  };
    65	  const update = () => {
    66	    const isEmpty = !elInput.value && !elInput.validity.badInput; // text that isn't a number reads as '' too, but is "bad input"
    67	    const number = /^[1-9]\d*$/.test(elInput.value) ? elInput.value : '';
    68	    wantedNumber = number;
    69	    if (isEmpty) {
    70	      show();
    71	    } else if (!number) {
    72	      showUnusable();
    73	    } else if (number === indexString) {
    74	      showError(elPreview.getAttribute('data-locale-self')!);
    75	    } else {
    76	      lookUp(number);
    77	    }
    78	  };
    79	  return {update, showUnusable};
    80	}
    81	
    82	// The close/reopen button in an issue or pull request's comment form: its text says whether the typed
    83	// comment is posted with it, and it is disabled while files upload. The editor's events bubble up to the form.
    84	// While the item is open, the menu beside it picks the close reason: the button then takes that reason's texts,
    85	// and a reason that needs more (a duplicate's number, an "other" description) opens a small popup under the buttons.
    86	export function initRepoIssueStatusButton(elButtons: HTMLElement) {
    87	  const statusButton = elButtons.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('#status-button')!;
    88	  const elForm = elButtons.closest('form')!;
    89	  const elEditor = elForm.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.combo-markdown-editor')!;
    90	  // hidden fields filled from the popups; none on a closed item
    91	  const reasonFields = elForm.querySelectorAll<HTMLInputElement>('input[type="hidden"][data-close-reason]');
    92	  // the editor attaches itself before its async init finishes, so start from the textarea, which holds any comment the browser restored
    93	  let content = elEditor.querySelector<HTMLTextAreaElement>('textarea.markdown-text-editor')!.value;
    94	  let isUploading = false;
    95	  const syncStatusButton = () => {
    96	    const statusText = statusButton.getAttribute(content.trim() ? 'data-status-and-comment' : 'data-status');
    97	    statusButton.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.status-button-text')!.textContent = statusText;
    98	    statusButton.disabled = isUploading;
    99	  };
   100	  const syncFromEditor = () => {
   101	    const editor = getComboMarkdownEditor(elEditor)!; // these events only come from an initialized editor
   102	    content = editor.value();
   103	    isUploading = editor.isUploading();
   104	    syncStatusButton();
   105	  };
   106	  elForm.addEventListener(ComboMarkdownEditor.EventEditorContentChanged, syncFromEditor);
   107	  elForm.addEventListener(ComboMarkdownEditor.EventUploadStateChanged, syncFromEditor);
   108	  syncStatusButton();
   109	
   110	  const elReasonMenu = elButtons.querySelector('.ui.dropdown > .menu');
   111	  if (!elReasonMenu) return; // a closed item only offers reopening
   112	  const reasonInput = elForm.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input[name="close_reason"]')!;
   113	  let elPickedItem = elReasonMenu.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.item.selected')!;
   114	  const popups: ReasonPopup[] = [];
   115	
   116	  // the button reads the picked item's texts, or a popup's own texts once it is filled in ("Close as duplicate of #12")
   117	  const applyStatusTexts = () => {
   118	    let [text, textWithComment] = [elPickedItem.getAttribute('data-status')!, elPickedItem.getAttribute('data-status-and-comment')!];
   119	    const popup = popups.find((p) => p.reason === reasonInput.value);
   120	    if (popup?.elPopup.hasAttribute('data-locale-status') && popup.field.value) {
   121	      text = popup.elPopup.getAttribute('data-locale-status')!.replace('%s', popup.field.value);
   122	      textWithComment = popup.elPopup.getAttribute('data-locale-status-and-comment')!.replace('%s', popup.field.value);
   123	    }
   124	    statusButton.setAttribute('data-status', text);
   125	    statusButton.setAttribute('data-status-and-comment', textWithComment);
   126	    syncStatusButton();
   127	  };
   128	
   129	  for (const elPopup of elForm.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[data-close-reason-popup]')) {
   130	    const reason = elPopup.getAttribute('data-close-reason-popup')!;
   131	    const field = Array.from(reasonFields).find((el) => el.getAttribute('data-close-reason') === reason)!;
   132	    const elField = elPopup.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.field')!;
   133	    const elInput = elPopup.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input')!;
   134	    const isUsable = () => elInput.type === 'number' ? /^[1-9]\d*$/.test(elInput.value) : Boolean(elInput.value.trim());
   135	    const tippy = createTippy(elPopup, {
   136	      content: elPopup,
   137	      trigger: 'manual',
   138	      placement: 'bottom-end',
   139	      interactive: true,
   140	      hideOnClick: true,
   141	      getReferenceClientRect: () => elButtons.getBoundingClientRect(),
   142	    });
   143	    const elPreview = elPopup.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[data-close-duplicate-preview]');
   144	    const preview = elPreview ? initDuplicatePreview(elPreview, elInput, () => tippy.popperInstance?.update(), (number) => {
   145	      field.value = number;
   146	      applyStatusTexts();
   147	    }) : null;
   148	    // the popup lives outside the form while shown, so its input fills the form's hidden field, only with a usable value
   149	    elInput.addEventListener('input', () => {
   150	      elField.classList.remove('error'); // typing answers the error; the preview marks a number it can't use again
   151	      field.value = preview || !isUsable() ? '' : elInput.value; // a duplicate's number counts once the preview has accepted it
   152	      preview?.update();
   153	      applyStatusTexts();
   154	    });
   155	    // a duplicate says what it needs; the description box's own placeholder already asks for it
   156	    const markUnusable = preview ? preview.showUnusable : () => elField.classList.add('error');
   157	    elInput.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
   158	      if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === 'Escape') {
   159	        e.preventDefault(); // Enter only confirms the value; closing stays a deliberate click on the button
   160	        tippy.hide();
   161	        statusButton.focus();
   162	      }
   163	    });
   164	    popups.push({reason, field, elPopup, elInput, isUsable, markUnusable, tippy});
   165	  }
   166	
   167	  // a close whose popup has no usable value yet sends nothing, not even the comment, and reopens that popup instead,
   168	  // the way a browser points at a required field on submit
   169	  statusButton.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
   170	    const popup = popups.find((p) => p.reason === reasonInput.value);
   171	    if (!popup || popup.field.value) return;
   172	    e.preventDefault();
   173	    if (!popup.isUsable()) popup.markUnusable(); // otherwise it is being looked up, or its preview says why not
   174	    popup.tippy.show();
   175	    setTimeout(() => popup.elInput.focus(), 0);
   176	  });
   177	
   178	  // a plain click listener rather than the dropdown's onChange; the template marks the items js-aria-clickable, so Enter clicks them too
   179	  elReasonMenu.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
   180	    const elItem = (e.target as Element).closest<HTMLElement>('.item[data-value]');
   181	    if (!elItem) return;
   182	    elPickedItem = elItem;
   183	    reasonInput.value = elItem.getAttribute('data-value')!;
   184	    for (const popup of popups) {
   185	      const isNeeded = popup.reason === reasonInput.value;
   186	      popup.field.disabled = !isNeeded; // a disabled field is not sent; its popup keeps what was typed
   187	      if (isNeeded) {
   188	        popup.tippy.show();
   189	        setTimeout(() => popup.elInput.focus(), 0); // after the dropdown's own click handling, which keeps the focus on itself
   190	      } else {
   191	        popup.tippy.hide();
   192	      }
   193	    }
   194	    applyStatusTexts();
   195	  });
   196	}

+import {initIssueListCloseReason} from './repo-issue-list.ts';
+import {createElementFromHTML} from '../utils/dom.ts';
+
+// the markup the Issues tab's toolbar gets while open issues are listed
+function createCloseButtons() {
+  const elButtons = createElementFromHTML<HTMLElement>(`
+    <div class="ui red basic buttons" data-global-init="initIssueListCloseReason">
+      <button class="ui button issue-action" data-action="close" data-url="/user2/repo1/issues/status" data-close-reason="completed">Close as completed</button>
+      <div class="ui dropdown icon button">
+        <div class="menu">
+          <div class="item js-aria-clickable selected" data-value="completed" data-status="Close as completed">Completed</div>
+          <div class="item js-aria-clickable" data-value="not_planned" data-status="Close as not planned">Not planned</div>
+        </div>
+      </div>
+    </div>`);
+  initIssueListCloseReason(elButtons);
+  const closeButton = elButtons.querySelector('.issue-action')!;
+  const pick = (reason: string) => elButtons.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`.item[data-value="${CSS.escape(reason)}"]`)!.click();
+  return {elButtons, closeButton, pick};
+}
+
+test('picking a reason gives the Close button that reason and its text', () => {
+  const {closeButton, pick} = createCloseButtons();
+  pick('not_planned');
+  expect(closeButton.getAttribute('data-close-reason')).toEqual('not_planned');
+  expect(closeButton.textContent).toEqual('Close as not planned');
+  pick('completed'); // the reason can still be changed before closing
+  expect(closeButton.getAttribute('data-close-reason')).toEqual('completed');
+  expect(closeButton.textContent).toEqual('Close as completed');
+});
+
+test('a click in the menu that misses every item changes nothing', () => {
+  const {elButtons, closeButton} = createCloseButtons();
+  elButtons.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.menu')!.click();
+  expect(closeButton.getAttribute('data-close-reason')).toEqual('completed');
+  expect(closeButton.textContent).toEqual('Close as completed');
+});

@@ -0,0 +1,37 @@
+import {initIssueListCloseReason} from './repo-issue-list.ts';
+import {createElementFromHTML} from '../utils/dom.ts';
+
+// the markup the Issues tab's toolbar gets while open issues are listed
+function createCloseButtons() {
+  const elButtons = createElementFromHTML<HTMLElement>(`
+    <div class="ui red basic buttons" data-global-init="initIssueListCloseReason">
+      <button class="ui button issue-action" data-action="close" data-url="/user2/repo1/issues/status" data-close-reason="completed">Close as completed</button>
+      <div class="ui dropdown icon button">
+        <div class="menu">
+          <div class="item js-aria-clickable selected" data-value="completed" data-status="Close as completed">Completed</div>
+          <div class="item js-aria-clickable" data-value="not_planned" data-status="Close as not planned">Not planned</div>
+        </div>
+      </div>
+    </div>`);
+  initIssueListCloseReason(elButtons);
+  const closeButton = elButtons.querySelector('.issue-action')!;
+  const pick = (reason: string) => elButtons.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`.item[data-value="${CSS.escape(reason)}"]`)!.click();
+  return {elButtons, closeButton, pick};
+}
+
+test('picking a reason gives the Close button that reason and its text', () => {
+  const {closeButton, pick} = createCloseButtons();
+  pick('not_planned');
+  expect(closeButton.getAttribute('data-close-reason')).toEqual('not_planned');
+  expect(closeButton.textContent).toEqual('Close as not planned');
+  pick('completed'); // the reason can still be changed before closing
+  expect(closeButton.getAttribute('data-close-reason')).toEqual('completed');
+  expect(closeButton.textContent).toEqual('Close as completed');
+});
+
+test('a click in the menu that misses every item changes nothing', () => {
+  const {elButtons, closeButton} = createCloseButtons();
+  elButtons.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.menu')!.click();
+  expect(closeButton.getAttribute('data-close-reason')).toEqual('completed');
+  expect(closeButton.textContent).toEqual('Close as completed');
+});

```text
import {updateIssuesMeta} from './repo-common.ts';
import {toggleElem, queryElems, isElemVisible} from '../utils/dom.ts';
import {html, htmlRaw} from '../utils/html.ts';
import {confirmModal} from './comp/ConfirmModal.ts';
import {errorMessage} from '../modules/errors.ts';
import {showErrorToast} from '../modules/toast.ts';
import {createSortable} from '../modules/sortable.ts';
import {DELETE, POST} from '../modules/fetch.ts';
import {parseDom} from '../utils.ts';
import {fomanticQuery} from '../modules/fomantic/base.ts';
import {registerGlobalInitFunc} from '../modules/observer.ts';
import type {SortableEvent} from 'sortablejs';

function initRepoIssueListCheckboxes() {
  const issueSelectAll = document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('.issue-checkbox-all');
  if (!issueSelectAll) return; // logged out state
  const issueCheckboxes = document.querySelectorAll<HTMLInputElement>('.issue-checkbox');

  const syncIssueSelectionState = () => {
    const checkedCheckboxes = Array.from(issueCheckboxes).filter((el) => el.checked);
    const anyChecked = Boolean(checkedCheckboxes.length);
    const allChecked = anyChecked && checkedCheckboxes.length === issueCheckboxes.length;

    if (allChecked) {
      issueSelectAll.checked = true;
      issueSelectAll.indeterminate = false;
    } else if (anyChecked) {
      issueSelectAll.checked = false;
      issueSelectAll.indeterminate = true;
    } else {
      issueSelectAll.checked = false;
      issueSelectAll.indeterminate = false;
    }
    // if any issue is selected, show the action panel, otherwise show the filter panel
    toggleElem('#issue-filters', !anyChecked);
    toggleElem('#issue-actions', anyChecked);
    // there are two panels but only one select-all checkbox, so move the checkbox to the visible panel
    const panels = document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('#issue-filters, #issue-actions');
    const visiblePanel = Array.from(panels).find((el) => isElemVisible(el))!;
    const toolbarLeft = visiblePanel.querySelector('.issue-list-toolbar-left')!;
    toolbarLeft.prepend(issueSelectAll);
  };

  for (const el of issueCheckboxes) {
    el.addEventListener('change', syncIssueSelectionState);
  }

  issueSelectAll.addEventListener('change', () => {
    for (const el of issueCheckboxes) {
      el.checked = issueSelectAll.checked;
    }
    syncIssueSelectionState();
  });

  queryElems(document, '.issue-action', (el) => el.addEventListener('click',
    async (e: MouseEvent) => {
      e.preventDefault();

      const url = el.getAttribute('data-url')!;
      let action = el.getAttribute('data-action')!;
      let elementId = el.getAttribute('data-element-id')!;
      const issueIDList: string[] = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.issue-checkbox:checked'), (el) => (el.getAttribute('data-issue-id')!));
      const issueIDs = issueIDList.join(',');
      if (!issueIDs) return;

      // for assignee
      if (elementId === '0' && url.endsWith('/assignee')) {
        elementId = '';
        action = 'clear';
      }

      // for toggle
      if (action === 'toggle' && e.altKey) {
        action = 'toggle-alt';
      }

      // for delete
      if (action === 'delete') {
        const confirmText = el.getAttribute('data-action-delete-confirm')!;
        if (!await confirmModal({content: confirmText, confirmButtonColor: 'red'})) {
          return;
        }
      }

      try {
        await updateIssuesMeta(url, action, issueIDs, elementId, el.getAttribute('data-close-reason')); // only the Close button has one
        window.location.reload();
      } catch (err) {
        // FIXME: this logic (including updateIssuesMeta) is not right, should refactor to our JSONError framework
        const e = err as {responseJSON?: {error: string}};
        showErrorToast(e.responseJSON?.error ?? errorMessage(err));
      }
    },
  ));
}

// The bulk Close button names the reason it closes with, and the ▾ beside it changes that reason, like the close button
// on an item's page. As there, a plain click listener on the menu; its items are js-aria-clickable, so Enter clicks them too.
export function initIssueListCloseReason(elButtons: HTMLElement) {
  const closeButton = elButtons.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.issue-action[data-close-reason]')!;
  elButtons.querySelector('.menu')!.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    const elItem = (e.target as Element).closest<HTMLElement>('.item[data-value]');
    if (!elItem) return;
    closeButton.setAttribute('data-close-reason', elItem.getAttribute('data-value')!);
    closeButton.textContent = elItem.getAttribute('data-status');
  });
}

function initDropdownUserRemoteSearch(el: Element) {
  let searchUrl = el.getAttribute('data-search-url');
  const actionJumpUrl = el.getAttribute('data-action-jump-url')!;
  let selectedUsername = el.getAttribute('data-selected-username') || '';
  const $searchDropdown = fomanticQuery(el);
  const elMenu = el.querySelector('.menu')!;
  const elSearchInput = el.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('.ui.search input')!;
  const elItemFromInput = el.querySelector('.menu > .item-from-input')!;

  $searchDropdown.dropdown('setting', {
    fullTextSearch: true,
    selectOnKeydown: false,
    action: (_text: string, value: string) => {
      window.location.assign(actionJumpUrl.replace('{username}', encodeURIComponent(value)));
    },
  });

  const selectUsername = (username: string) => {
    queryElems(elMenu, '.item.active, .item.selected', (el) => el.classList.remove('active', 'selected'));
    elMenu.querySelector(`.item[data-value="${CSS.escape(username)}"]`)?.classList.add('selected');
  };

  type ProcessedResult = {value: string, name: string};
  const processedResults: ProcessedResult[] = []; // to be used by dropdown to generate menu items
  const syncItemFromInput = () => {
    const inputVal = elSearchInput.value.trim();
    elItemFromInput.setAttribute('data-value', inputVal);
    elItemFromInput.textContent = inputVal;
    const showItemFromInput = !processedResults.length && inputVal !== '';
    toggleElem(elItemFromInput, showItemFromInput);
    selectUsername(showItemFromInput ? inputVal : selectedUsername);
  };

    10	function sortAndReduce<T>(map: Map<T, number>): T[] {
    11	  const sortedMap = new Map(Array.from(map).sort((a, b) => a[1] - b[1]));

    15	export function matchEmoji(queryText: string): string[] {

    27	      const rankedIndex = index + aliasIndex;
    28	      results.set(mainAlias, existing ? existing - rankedIndex : rankedIndex);

    30	  }
    31

import {updateIssuesMeta} from './repo-common.ts';
import {toggleElem, queryElems, isElemVisible} from '../utils/dom.ts';
import {html, htmlRaw} from '../utils/html.ts';
import {confirmModal} from './comp/ConfirmModal.ts';
import {errorMessage} from '../modules/errors.ts';
import {showErrorToast} from '../modules/toast.ts';
import {createSortable} from '../modules/sortable.ts';
import {DELETE, POST} from '../modules/fetch.ts';
import {parseDom} from '../utils.ts';
