    12	type ReasonPopup = {reason: string, field: HTMLInputElement, elPopup: HTMLElement, elInput: HTMLInputElement, isUsable: () => boolean, markUnusable: () => void, tippy: Instance};
    13	
    14	// Shows the issue with the typed number beside the duplicate box, found by the same search as the comment box's # list,
    15	// which only returns what the viewer can read. A number is accepted once that issue is found, so a close that would be
    16	// refused (the issue itself, or no such issue) is never sent with its comment; if the search fails, the server decides.
    17	function initDuplicatePreview(elPreview: HTMLElement, elInput: HTMLInputElement, onResize: () => void, onAccepted: (number: string) => void) {
    18	  const {ownerName, repoName, indexString} = parseIssueHref(window.location.href);
    19	  const elField = elPreview.closest('.field')!;
    20	  let wantedNumber = ''; // an answer that arrives for an older number is dropped
    21	  const show = (...children: Array<Node | string>) => {
    22	    elField.classList.remove('error');
    23	    elPreview.replaceChildren(...children);
    24	    toggleElem(elPreview, children.length > 0);
    25	    onResize(); // the popup grows or shrinks with the preview
    26	  };
    27	  // a number that can't be used: Gitea's red "error" field around the box, and the reason in red beside it
    28	  const showError = (text: string) => {
    29	    show(createElementFromAttrs('span', {class: 'tw-text-red'}, text));
    30	    elField.classList.add('error');
    31	  };
    32	  const lookUp = debounce(async (number: string) => {
    33	    let issues: Issue[];
    34	    try {
    35	      issues = await matchIssue(ownerName, repoName, indexString, number);
    36	    } catch {
    37	      if (number !== wantedNumber) return;
    38	      show(); // no preview then, and the server checks the number on close
    39	      onAccepted(number);
    40	      return;
    41	    }
    42	    if (number !== wantedNumber) return;
    43	    const issue = issues.find((i) => String(i.number) === number);
    44	    if (issue) {
    45	      show(
    46	        createElementFromHTML(svg(getIssueIcon(issue), 16, [getIssueColorClass(issue)])),
    47	        `#${issue.number}`,
    48	        createElementFromAttrs('span', {class: 'gt-ellipsis'}, issue.title), // a text node, so a title can't inject markup
    49	      );
    50	      onAccepted(number);
    51	    } else {
    52	      showError(elPreview.getAttribute('data-locale-not-found')!.replace('%s', number));
    53	    }
    54	  }, 300); // the same delay as the # list
    55	  // text, or a number like 0, -3 or 1.5, gets the same error as a number with no issue;
    56	  // a number box reads letters as '', so for those there is nothing to name and only the box is marked
    57	  const showUnusable = () => {
    58	    if (elInput.value) {
    59	      showError(elPreview.getAttribute('data-locale-not-found')!.replace('%s', elInput.value));
    60	    } else {
    61	      show();
    62	      elField.classList.add('error');
    63	    }
    64	  };
    65	  const update = () => {
    66	    const isEmpty = !elInput.value && !elInput.validity.badInput; // text that isn't a number reads as '' too, but is "bad input"
    67	    const number = /^[1-9]\d*$/.test(elInput.value) ? elInput.value : '';
    68	    wantedNumber = number;
    69	    if (isEmpty) {
    70	      show();
    71	    } else if (!number) {
    72	      showUnusable();
    73	    } else if (number === indexString) {
    74	      showError(elPreview.getAttribute('data-locale-self')!);
    75	    } else {
    76	      lookUp(number);
    77	    }
    78	  };
    79	  return {update, showUnusable};
    80	}
    81	
    82	// The close/reopen button in an issue or pull request's comment form: its text says whether the typed
    83	// comment is posted with it, and it is disabled while files upload. The editor's events bubble up to the form.
    84	// While the item is open, the menu beside it picks the close reason: the button then takes that reason's texts,
    85	// and a reason that needs more (a duplicate's number, an "other" description) opens a small popup under the buttons.
    86	export function initRepoIssueStatusButton(elButtons: HTMLElement) {
    87	  const statusButton = elButtons.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('#status-button')!;
    88	  const elForm = elButtons.closest('form')!;
    89	  const elEditor = elForm.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.combo-markdown-editor')!;
    90	  // hidden fields filled from the popups; none on a closed item
    91	  const reasonFields = elForm.querySelectorAll<HTMLInputElement>('input[type="hidden"][data-close-reason]');
    92	  // the editor attaches itself before its async init finishes, so start from the textarea, which holds any comment the browser restored
    93	  let content = elEditor.querySelector<HTMLTextAreaElement>('textarea.markdown-text-editor')!.value;
    94	  let isUploading = false;
    95	  const syncStatusButton = () => {
    96	    const statusText = statusButton.getAttribute(content.trim() ? 'data-status-and-comment' : 'data-status');
    97	    statusButton.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.status-button-text')!.textContent = statusText;
    98	    statusButton.disabled = isUploading;
    99	  };
   100	  const syncFromEditor = () => {
   101	    const editor = getComboMarkdownEditor(elEditor)!; // these events only come from an initialized editor
   102	    content = editor.value();
   103	    isUploading = editor.isUploading();
   104	    syncStatusButton();
   105	  };
   106	  elForm.addEventListener(ComboMarkdownEditor.EventEditorContentChanged, syncFromEditor);
   107	  elForm.addEventListener(ComboMarkdownEditor.EventUploadStateChanged, syncFromEditor);
   108	  syncStatusButton();
   109	
   110	  const elReasonMenu = elButtons.querySelector('.ui.dropdown > .menu');
   111	  if (!elReasonMenu) return; // a closed item only offers reopening
   112	  const reasonInput = elForm.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input[name="close_reason"]')!;
   113	  let elPickedItem = elReasonMenu.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.item.selected')!;
   114	  const popups: ReasonPopup[] = [];
   115	
   116	  // the button reads the picked item's texts, or a popup's own texts once it is filled in ("Close as duplicate of #12")
   117	  const applyStatusTexts = () => {
   118	    let [text, textWithComment] = [elPickedItem.getAttribute('data-status')!, elPickedItem.getAttribute('data-status-and-comment')!];
   119	    const popup = popups.find((p) => p.reason === reasonInput.value);
   120	    if (popup?.elPopup.hasAttribute('data-locale-status') && popup.field.value) {
   121	      text = popup.elPopup.getAttribute('data-locale-status')!.replace('%s', popup.field.value);
   122	      textWithComment = popup.elPopup.getAttribute('data-locale-status-and-comment')!.replace('%s', popup.field.value);
   123	    }
   124	    statusButton.setAttribute('data-status', text);
   125	    statusButton.setAttribute('data-status-and-comment', textWithComment);
   126	    syncStatusButton();
   127	  };
   128	
   129	  for (const elPopup of elForm.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[data-close-reason-popup]')) {
   130	    const reason = elPopup.getAttribute('data-close-reason-popup')!;
   131	    const field = Array.from(reasonFields).find((el) => el.getAttribute('data-close-reason') === reason)!;
   132	    const elField = elPopup.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.field')!;
   133	    const elInput = elPopup.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input')!;
   134	    const isUsable = () => elInput.type === 'number' ? /^[1-9]\d*$/.test(elInput.value) : Boolean(elInput.value.trim());
   135	    const tippy = createTippy(elPopup, {
   136	      content: elPopup,
   137	      trigger: 'manual',
   138	      placement: 'bottom-end',
   139	      interactive: true,
   140	      hideOnClick: true,
   141	      getReferenceClientRect: () => elButtons.getBoundingClientRect(),
   142	    });
   143	    const elPreview = elPopup.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[data-close-duplicate-preview]');
   144	    const preview = elPreview ? initDuplicatePreview(elPreview, elInput, () => tippy.popperInstance?.update(), (number) => {
   145	      field.value = number;
   146	      applyStatusTexts();
   147	    }) : null;
   148	    // the popup lives outside the form while shown, so its input fills the form's hidden field, only with a usable value
   149	    elInput.addEventListener('input', () => {
   150	      elField.classList.remove('error'); // typing answers the error; the preview marks a number it can't use again
   151	      field.value = preview || !isUsable() ? '' : elInput.value; // a duplicate's number counts once the preview has accepted it
   152	      preview?.update();
   153	      applyStatusTexts();
   154	    });
   155	    // a duplicate says what it needs; the description box's own placeholder already asks for it
   156	    const markUnusable = preview ? preview.showUnusable : () => elField.classList.add('error');
   157	    elInput.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
   158	      if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === 'Escape') {
   159	        e.preventDefault(); // Enter only confirms the value; closing stays a deliberate click on the button
   160	        tippy.hide();
   161	        statusButton.focus();
   162	      }
   163	    });
   164	    popups.push({reason, field, elPopup, elInput, isUsable, markUnusable, tippy});
   165	  }
   166	
   167	  // a close whose popup has no usable value yet sends nothing, not even the comment, and reopens that popup instead,
   168	  // the way a browser points at a required field on submit
   169	  statusButton.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
   170	    const popup = popups.find((p) => p.reason === reasonInput.value);
   171	    if (!popup || popup.field.value) return;
   172	    e.preventDefault();
   173	    if (!popup.isUsable()) popup.markUnusable(); // otherwise it is being looked up, or its preview says why not
   174	    popup.tippy.show();
   175	    setTimeout(() => popup.elInput.focus(), 0);
   176	  });
   177	
   178	  // a plain click listener rather than the dropdown's onChange; the template marks the items js-aria-clickable, so Enter clicks them too
   179	  elReasonMenu.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
   180	    const elItem = (e.target as Element).closest<HTMLElement>('.item[data-value]');
   181	    if (!elItem) return;
   182	    elPickedItem = elItem;
   183	    reasonInput.value = elItem.getAttribute('data-value')!;
   184	    for (const popup of popups) {
   185	      const isNeeded = popup.reason === reasonInput.value;
   186	      popup.field.disabled = !isNeeded; // a disabled field is not sent; its popup keeps what was typed
   187	      if (isNeeded) {
   188	        popup.tippy.show();
   189	        setTimeout(() => popup.elInput.focus(), 0); // after the dropdown's own click handling, which keeps the focus on itself
   190	      } else {
   191	        popup.tippy.hide();
   192	      }
   193	    }
   194	    applyStatusTexts();
   195	  });
   196	}

```text
  "version": "2.1.0",
index.d.mts
index.mjs
//#region src/index.ts
const DEBOUNCE_DEFAULTS = { trailing: true };
/**
Debounce functions
@param fn - Promise-returning/async function to debounce.
@param wait - Milliseconds to wait before calling `fn`. Default value is 25ms
@returns A function that delays calling `fn` until after `wait` milliseconds have elapsed since the last time it was called.
@example
```
import { debounce } from 'perfect-debounce';
const expensiveCall = async input => input;
const debouncedFn = debounce(expensiveCall, 200);
for (const number of [1, 2, 3]) {
console.log(await debouncedFn(number));
}
//=> 1
//=> 2
//=> 3
```
*/
function debounce(fn, wait = 25, options = {}) {
	options = {
		...DEBOUNCE_DEFAULTS,
		...options
	};
	if (!Number.isFinite(wait)) throw new TypeError("Expected `wait` to be a finite number");
	let leadingValue;
	let timeout;
	let resolveList = [];
	let currentPromise;
	let trailingArgs;
	const applyFn = (_this, args) => {
		currentPromise = _applyPromised(fn, _this, args);
		currentPromise.finally(() => {
			currentPromise = null;
			if (options.trailing && trailingArgs && !timeout) {
				const promise = applyFn(_this, trailingArgs);
				trailingArgs = null;
				return promise;
			}
		});
		return currentPromise;
	};
	const debounced = function(...args) {
		if (options.trailing) trailingArgs = args;
		if (currentPromise) return currentPromise;
		return new Promise((resolve) => {
			const shouldCallNow = !timeout && options.leading;
			clearTimeout(timeout);
			timeout = setTimeout(() => {
				timeout = null;
				const promise = options.leading ? leadingValue : applyFn(this, args);
				trailingArgs = null;
				for (const _resolve of resolveList) _resolve(promise);
				resolveList = [];
			}, wait);
			if (shouldCallNow) {
				leadingValue = applyFn(this, args);
				resolve(leadingValue);
			} else resolveList.push(resolve);
		});
	};
	const _clearTimeout = (timer) => {
		if (timer) {
			clearTimeout(timer);
			timeout = null;
		}
	};
	debounced.isPending = () => !!timeout;
	debounced.cancel = () => {
		_clearTimeout(timeout);
		resolveList = [];
		trailingArgs = null;
	};
	debounced.flush = () => {
		_clearTimeout(timeout);
		if (!trailingArgs || currentPromise) return;
		const args = trailingArgs;
		trailingArgs = null;
		return applyFn(this, args);
	};
	return debounced;
}
async function _applyPromised(fn, _this, args) {
	return await fn.apply(_this, args);
}

//#endregion
export { debounce };

Part 3 is done. It found four real problems in the browser code, all introduced by this branch, plus six minor points. Each one was reproduced by the reviewer and then again by its skeptic. It used about 758k tokens (6 agents, about 29 minutes), so the review is at about 1.68M across the three parts.

**Should fix:**
1. **Firefox can save the wrong reason.** Pick Other, type a description, then reload the page: Firefox puts the old hidden values back. The button says "Close as completed" but saves Other with the old text, and nothing warns you. That breaks AC1 and AC3. Chromium doesn't do this.
   - Fix: when the page starts, reset the hidden reason fields to match the menu.
2. **Wrong button text after going Back.** When the browser restores a typed comment on Back without its page cache, the button drops "…with comment", yet it still posts the comment. My start-up read happens before Chrome puts the text back. On `main` the text was set later, so this is a regression.
   - Fix: refresh the button once the editor finishes starting, which is when `main` did it.
3. **Japanese and Chinese typing.** In the Other box, the Enter that confirms a character conversion also closes the popup. In the skeptic's test the next Enter would have closed the issue with half a sentence. Every other Enter handler in Gitea skips this case.
   - Fix: add `if (e.isComposing) return;`, a one-line change.
4. **A flaky unit test.** My new `updateIssuesMeta` test fails when the test runner happens to run `repo-issue-list.test.ts` first, because the two files share a module. On machines with few cores, which is likely in CI, it failed 1 or 2 times in 5.
   - Fix: reload the module inside the test, the pattern Gitea's other tests use.

**Minor:**

5. Tab from inside a popup jumps to the bottom of the page. Gitea's other popups do the same, and Enter or Escape already leads back to the button.
6. The duplicate preview's messages aren't linked to the number box, so screen readers don't read them. Adding `aria-describedby` is cheap.
7. "01" reports "No #01 found" even though #1 exists.
8. Two of the preview's stale-answer guards are tested only through a setup that can't happen with the real debounce, or not at all.
9. Nothing tests that focus moves into the popup and back.
10. The whole-number check is written twice.

**Clean:** no way to inject markup, the bulk picker works, ESLint and the type-check pass, and the reviewers' 23 deliberate code breaks caught 17. All six that slipped through are in points 8–9 or have no visible effect.

**My recommendation:**
- **Fix 1–4** (all small) and **6, 7, 9, 10**, which are cheap and close real gaps.
- **Rework the test for 8** while I'm in that file.
- **Leave 5,** because it matches the rest of Gitea.

As before, I'd make two commits: the four fixes with their tests, then the small ones. Which of these do you want? After that, Part 4 is the last one: the integration tests against the ACs, the `.claude-students` docs, and your PR description's claims.

The reviewers also left issues #32–#44 and one review comment on PR #18 in `ai/close-reason-check`, so add those to the cleanup list with the 13 test repos.

// Shows the issue with the typed number beside the duplicate box, found by the same search as the comment box's # list,
// which only returns what the viewer can read. A number is accepted once that issue is found, so a close that would be
// refused (the issue itself, or no such issue) is never sent with its comment; if the search fails, the server decides.
function initDuplicatePreview(elPreview: HTMLElement, elInput: HTMLInputElement, onResize: () => void, onAccepted: (number: string) => void) {
  const {ownerName, repoName, indexString} = parseIssueHref(window.location.href);
  const elField = elPreview.closest('.field')!;
  let wantedNumber = ''; // an answer that arrives for an older number is dropped
  const show = (...children: Array<Node | string>) => {
    elField.classList.remove('error');
    elPreview.replaceChildren(...children);
    toggleElem(elPreview, children.length > 0);
    onResize(); // the popup grows or shrinks with the preview
  };
  // a number that can't be used: Gitea's red "error" field around the box, and the reason in red beside it
  const showError = (text: string) => {
    show(createElementFromAttrs('span', {class: 'tw-text-red'}, text));
    elField.classList.add('error');
  };
  const lookUp = debounce(async (number: string) => {
    let issues: Issue[];
    try {
      issues = await matchIssue(ownerName, repoName, indexString, number);
    } catch {
      if (number !== wantedNumber) return;
      show(); // no preview then, and the server checks the number on close
      onAccepted(number);
      return;
    }
    if (number !== wantedNumber) return;
    const issue = issues.find((i) => String(i.number) === number);
    if (issue) {
      show(
        createElementFromHTML(svg(getIssueIcon(issue), 16, [getIssueColorClass(issue)])),
        `#${issue.number}`,
        createElementFromAttrs('span', {class: 'gt-ellipsis'}, issue.title), // a text node, so a title can't inject markup
      );
      onAccepted(number);
    } else {
      showError(elPreview.getAttribute('data-locale-not-found')!.replace('%s', number));
    }
  }, 300); // the same delay as the # list
  // text, or a number like 0, -3 or 1.5, gets the same error as a number with no issue;
  // a number box reads letters as '', so for those there is nothing to name and only the box is marked
  const showUnusable = () => {
    if (elInput.value) {
      showError(elPreview.getAttribute('data-locale-not-found')!.replace('%s', elInput.value));
    } else {
      show();
      elField.classList.add('error');
    }
  };
  const update = () => {
    const isEmpty = !elInput.value && !elInput.validity.badInput; // text that isn't a number reads as '' too, but is "bad input"
    const number = /^[1-9]\d*$/.test(elInput.value) ? elInput.value : '';
    wantedNumber = number;
    if (isEmpty) {
      show();
    } else if (!number) {
      showUnusable();
    } else if (number === indexString) {
      showError(elPreview.getAttribute('data-locale-self')!);
    } else {
      lookUp(number);
    }
  };
  return {update, showUnusable};
}

import re, os, glob
root='web_src/js'
def imports(path):
    try: s=open(path).read()
    except: return []
    out=[]
    for m in re.finditer(r'''(?:import|from)\s*(?:[^'"]*?from\s*)?['"](\.{1,2}/[^'"]+)['"]''', s):
        p=os.path.normpath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(path), m.group(1)))
        if os.path.exists(p): out.append(p)
    return out
def mocks(path):
    s=open(path).read()
    return {os.path.normpath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(path), m.group(1))) for m in re.finditer(r"vi\.mock\(['\"](\.{1,2}/[^'\"]+)['\"]", s)}
target='web_src/js/utils/match.ts'
for t in sorted(glob.glob(root+'/**/*.test.ts', recursive=True)):
    mocked=mocks(t)
    seen=set(); stack=[(t,[t])]; path_found=None
    while stack:
        f,chain=stack.pop()
        for d in imports(f):
            if d in mocked or d in seen: continue
            seen.add(d)
            if d==target: path_found=chain+[d]; break
            stack.append((d,chain+[d]))
        if path_found: break
    if path_found and not t.endswith('match.test.ts'):
        print(t, ' <- ', ' -> '.join(p.replace('web_src/js/','') for p in path_found[1:]))
EOF

# Design Decisions for the first commit (adding list of reasons to the model)

### Decision 1: The reason names are kept in one place, next to the reasons

**Decision:** The words the page uses for each reason (`completed`, `not_planned`, `duplicate`, `other`) are listed once, beside the reasons themselves.
**Alternatives Considered:** Keep the list on the close form, and give bulk close its own copy.
**Rationale:** The close button, bulk close and the page's menu all need the same words. With one list they can't drift apart, and the API can reuse it.
**Consequences:** Renaming a word breaks anything still sending the old one. Reviews keep their own list on their form, so both styles exist in the codebase.


### Decision 2: The server decides which reason the close button starts on (i.e, a hard-coded default)

**Decision:** An issue's close button starts on completed and a pull request's on not planned (AC1). A close with no reason still records none.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) The page picks the default itself. (b) Treat a close with no reason as the default.
**Rationale:** This is how Gitea handles buttons that start on a choice: the merge button and the "Update branch" button both get their default from the server, from a built-in value that settings can override. Thus, hard-coded values can be easily overridden.
**Consequences:** A setting to change the default can be added later on top of the built-in one, the way `DEFAULT_MERGE_STYLE` works for merges. The future API can use the same default or keep its own, as the API's branch update already does.
--
author:	ab-wm
association:	collaborator
edited:	false
status:	none
--
# Design Decision for the second main commit (adding the menu to the buttons [no functionality])

### Decision 3: A leftover style/rule was removed from repo.css

**Decision:** The comment box's button row had a style that cut off anything reaching outside it (`overflow: hidden` in `web_src/css/repo.css`), which hid the close reason menu. The style has been deleted.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Keep the style and override it for this row only. (b) Build the menu as a popup attached to the whole page, which no box can cut off, as a few of Gitea's small menus are.
**Rationale:** A deep analysis of the repo showed that it applies to nothing else, and that this was a leftover from a replacement in 2025. Changes were confirmed visually, and the menu now pops up, confirming that as the single cause..
**Consequences:** If anything in the row ever does reach outside it, such as a very long translated button label on a phone, it will now show instead of being cut off.
--
author:	ab-wm
association:	collaborator
edited:	false
status:	none
--
# Design Decision for the third main commit (removal of old locale strings)

### Decision 4: The old close button strings are deleted

**Decision:** "Close Issue", "Close Pull Request" and "Close with Comment" are deleted from `locale_en-US.json`, since the close button now names its reason and nothing else uses them. The other languages are left for the translation platform to clean up (AC10).
**Alternatives Considered:** Keep them in the file, unused.
**Rationale:** An unused string still reaches translators, who would keep translating text no page shows.
**Consequences:** Bringing back any of these labels means adding the key again, and it starts with no translations.
--
author:	ab-wm
association:	collaborator
edited:	false
status:	none
--
# Design Decision for the forth main commit (button refactor)

### Decision 5: The close/reopen button gets its own piece of page code

**Decision:** The code that sets the close/reopen button's text ("…with comment" once a comment is typed) and disables it during uploads moves out of the comment box's setup into its own feature, `web_src/js/features/repo-issue-status-button.ts`. It is switched on by a `data-global-init` attribute on the button in the template.
**Alternatives Considered:** Leave the button's code in the comment box's setup, and add reason picking there.
**Rationale:** `data-global-init` is the wiring Gitea requires, per its docs, and existing code does use this pattern, including the "Update branch" split button. Moving the button's existing code as well means one place decides everything the button shows, instead of two pieces of code writing the same text.
**Consequences:** Despite the fact that existing code use `data-global-init`, this will be is the first feature to follow a comment box it did not set up, since it relies on the box's events reaching the for. The move also touches existing upstream code, so the change is bigger than the reason picking alone.
--
author:	ab-wm
association:	collaborator
edited:	true
status:	none
--
# Design Decision for the fifth main commit (click listener vs deprecated Fomantic components)

### Decision 6: Picking a reason is processed with a plain click listener, not Fomantic's change callback

**Decision:** The page notices a pick with an ordinary click listener on the menu's items, along with a `js-aria-clickable` class for accessbility and the ability to _click._ with the enter button with the help of Gitea's dropdown change.
**Alternatives Considered:** Fomantic's `onChange` callback, as the "Update branch" split button uses.
**Rationale:** Gitea froze Fomantic (upstream #33845) and replaces it by rewriting modules. Using a click listener will survive such rewriting as Fomantic components had to be done. This is especially important when issue #25 plans to make dropdowns accessible, so this sets a precedent within the repo.
**Consequences:** Keyboard picking depends on the `js-aria-clickable` class, which only two of Gitea's menus use. The page's integration test checks every item carries it, so a later edit can't drop it unnoticed. It also departs from the only other split button, which still uses `onChange`.
--
author:	ab-wm
association:	collaborator
edited:	false
status:	none
--
# Design Decision for the sixth main commit (implementation of the duplicate issue picker and other issue box)

### Decision 7: Duplicate and Other ask for their detail in a small popup, and the close button shows the result

**Decision:** Picking "Duplicate" or "Other" opens a small popup under the close button, like the markdown editor's "Add table" popup. For a duplicate, you type the original's number: that issue appears beside the box (its icon, number and title), and the button reads "Close as duplicate of #12". 
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) A box above the buttons with the `#` suggestions from the comment box. (b) A search picker like the sidebar's "add dependency". (c) Greying out Close, with or without a tooltip saying why.
**Rationale:** The button already says what closing will do, so it is where the choice belongs. (a) left only "#12" in the box, and the backend had to accept text to fit the widget, and would need to be modified to do so (b) is a larger control built on Fomantic's JavaScript. The server posts the comment before it checks the close, so the page has to stop a close that would be refused. Answering the click, the way a browser points at a required field, still explains it after the popup is closed, which a greyed-out button can't.
**Consequences:** The preview uses the `#` list's search, so an issue the viewer can't read counts as not found. Finding an issue by its title is left out. A change between typing and clicking, such as the original being deleted, still ends with the comment posted and the close refused.



--

# Design Decision for the seventh main commit (close reason labels and icons)

### Decision 8: Each close reason gets its own icon, in the colours Gitea already uses for "done" and "set aside"

**Decision:** A closed issue or pull request shows why it was closed, in lists, in the label at the top of its page and on its close event in the timeline. Completed is a purple closed icon; not planned, duplicate and other are grey, with a skip, duplicate and note icon. Items closed without a reason (older closes, merges, automatic closes) keep today's red closed icon.
**Alternatives Considered:** Keep completed red like today's closed icon, and give new icons only to the other reasons.
**Rationale:** Gitea's colours already have meanings: purple is done, as for a merged pull request, and grey is set aside, as for a draft or a skipped job. Following them makes the reasons readable without learning anything new.
**Consequences:** The icon depends only on the reason, so a pull request closed as not planned looks like an issue closed as not planned; its link still says which it is.

# Design Decision for the eight main commit (bulk close)

### Decision 9: The list's Close button works like the one on an issue's page

**Decision:** When items are selected on the issue or pull request list, Close becomes the same button as on an item's page.
**Alternatives Considered:** A menu whose items close straight away, like the Labels and Milestone menus beside it; and on the Pull Requests tab, a plain "Close as not planned" button with no ▾.
**Rationale:** Closing works the same way everywhere, and the button always says what it will do. Both menus come from the reasons the model allows, leaving out Duplicate and Other, whose number or description belongs to a single item; so a new reason shows up without changing the page.
**Consequences:** The Pull Requests tab's menu holds a single item for now.

Closes #54

## What changed and why

#53 stores and checks why an issue or pull request was closed, but nothing on the page let you choose a reason or see one. This PR adds the UI for it.

- **Close button:** on an issue or pull request page it becomes a split button that names its reason. The ▾ lists the reasons that item may use, and the button text follows the pick, with or without a comment typed. This was done for both showing the default reason that would be submitted, but also to reflect the chosen option.
- **Duplicate and Other:** each asks for its detail in a small popup under the button, reusing, for the most part, components that already existed in Gitea. A close without a usable value isn't sent; the popup reopens with the box marked red instead.
- **Timeline:** the close event says why: "closed this as not planned", "closed this as a duplicate of #N" with a link to it, or the Other text, shown as plain text.
- **Icons and labels:** closed items show their reason in lists, in the label at the top of the page and on the timeline badge. The color scheme follows what the current Gitea follows to keep things consistent. Items closed without a reason look as they do today.
- **Bulk close:** the list's Close button works the same way. The Issues tab offers Completed and Not planned, and the Pull Requests tab only Not planned (only a single option, but maintained the split for consistency).
- **Two of #53's known limitations are resolved:** a duplicate's title and link are only shown to viewers who can read the original, and the reason names now live in the model rather than the form, so #55's API can reuse them.
- The old, now unused button strings are removed, and the docs in `.claude-students` are updated.

## How the changes relate to the ACs

- **AC1:** the button starts on Completed for an issue and Not planned for a pull request, so a plain click closes with that reason.
- **AC2:** the menu offers Completed, Not planned, Duplicate and Other on an issue, and the same without Completed on a pull request. Merging is unchanged.
- **AC3:** picking another reason updates the button text, with or without a comment, and the last pick is the one saved.
- **AC4:** a number that isn't an issue or pull request in the repository, or is the item itself, is marked red with a message and the close isn't sent; the server refuses it too (#53). A valid number closes it, and the timeline links to the original.
- **AC5:** an empty description blocks the close, and the box stops at 255 characters; the server refuses both too (#53). The text is saved and shown as plain text.
- **AC6:** bulk Close offers Completed and Not planned on the Issues tab and only Not planned on the Pull Requests tab, and every selected item closes with the picked reason.
- **AC7:** the close event states the reason.
- **AC8:** each reason has its own icon and label; items with no reason look as before.
- **AC9:** reopening brings back the open look, and the earlier close event keeps its reason.
- **AC10:** every new string is in `locale_en-US.json`, and no other locale file changed.


## How it was tested

Testing was done in three distinct parts. 
- Vitest tests and integration tests to prove the functioning of the UI in the code itself. The tests themselves were tested by deliberately breaking code to see the changes and tests fail.
- A visual inspection of the changes by running a local instance. Since the changes were performed in small sets, the checks ensured only the behavior of the targeted portions changed, and nothing else.
- Claude running a headless browser with its own credentials to test the program and fix issues as it spotted them.

| AC | What the tests check |
| --- | --- |
| AC1 | Each page's button starts on its default, and a plain close saves it |
| AC2 | The menu's reasons and labels on an issue and a pull request; a closed item only offers Reopen |
| AC3 | Picking changes the button text and the reason sent, with and without a comment typed |
| AC4 | The preview of the typed number; a missing number, the item itself, text or a non-whole number blocks the close; the timeline link |
| AC5 | Other's text is sent as typed; empty or spaces-only blocks the close; the 255 limit; HTML and Markdown in the timeline stay plain text |
| AC6 | Both tabs' menus; bulk closing several issues with each reason and a pull request as not planned; a refused reason leaves the item open |
| AC7 | The timeline text for each reason, and for a close with no reason |
| AC8 | The list icon, page label and timeline badge for each reason and for none; a merged pull request still looks merged |
| AC9 | Reopening shows the open look again, and the earlier close keeps its reason |
| AC10 | Labels are checked as rendered text, so a missing key would show up as the key itself |

The tests are in `models/issues/issue_close_reason_test.go`, `tests/integration/issue_test.go`, `web_src/js/features/repo-issue-status-button.test.ts`, `repo-issue-list.test.ts` and `repo-common.test.ts`. The Playwright test `tests/e2e/issue-comment.test.ts` now clicks the renamed button.


## Known limitations

- The hover popup on issue links still shows the old icon. It reads the API, so it is out of scope.
- Bulk close shows no message when the server refuses a close, whether for a blocked dependency or a reason only a hand-made request can send. A "FIXME" was present for the relevant code, but was not changed since that would be way out of scope, impacting behavior that should not belong to this set of changes.
- Closing with a comment still posts the comment if the server then refuses the close. This should be highly unlikely, but since it is a general pattern to have the server be the final verifier of rules, blocking such behavior would not follow convention.
- A pull request closed as not planned has the same icon as an issue closed as not planned; its link still says which it is (Decision 8).
- The red message in the duplicate popup isn't announced by screen readers. Gitea doesn't use `aria-invalid` anywhere, so this follows it.

Read maintenance rules and check script

```text
<!-- markdownlint-disable MD029 -->
<!-- Rules are numbered continuously 1-15 across the sections below; check.sh error
     messages and all 34 docs cite them by number, so the sequence must not restart. -->

# Maintenance rules

Five people maintain one shared set of docs. These rules exist so the set stays *one* set. Read
them before editing anything in `.claude-students/`. Rules marked **[checked]** are enforced by
`./.claude-students/check.sh`.

## Scope discipline

1. **Upstream wins.** `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/guidelines-*.md` are authoritative.
   Docs here summarise them and link to them; they never restate a rule differently and never
   contradict one. A contradiction is a bug in this folder, not in the project.
2. **One fact, one home.** Every fact lives in exactly one doc — the one whose `scope:` owns that
   path. Everywhere else, link to it. Duplicated facts are how five maintainers end up with five
   different answers.
3. **Durability test.** Record a fact only if it (a) took more than one discovery step to find and
   (b) will still be true after the next upstream merge. A one-off workaround, a sprint detail or
   anything about your own task fails this test — that belongs in `ai-logs/`.
4. **No process notes.** No TODOs, no open questions, no first person, no student names, no dates
   other than `verified-at`. This is a map of the code, not a journal.

## Form

5. **Template only [checked].** Use the `## ` headings from `_TEMPLATE.md`, all of them, in that
   order, with nothing added. If a section has nothing to say, write one line saying so.
6. **120-line cap [checked].** Going over means the scope is too broad. Split the doc, and add the
   new `INDEX.md` row in the same commit. `INDEX.md` itself is capped at 60 lines.
7. **Cite or delete [checked, partially].** Every claim names a repo path. A claim with no path is
   unverifiable by the next reader — delete it.
8. **Symbols, not line numbers [checked].** Write `models/db/context.go` → `WithTx`, never
   `models/db/context.go:143`. Line numbers rot at the next upstream merge and a stale number is
   worse than no number. Code fences stay at 10 lines or fewer — point at the file instead of
   copying it.
9. **Repo-relative paths [checked].** `models/db/context.go`, never `/home/you/gitea/models/...`.
10. **Whitespace [checked].** No trailing whitespace, LF endings, final newline — same as the rest
    of the repo (`.editorconfig`).

## Change control

11. **One universal set.** These docs live on `main` and nowhere else. Never keep a personal copy,
    a per-student folder, or a long-lived branch of them.
12. **Changes land by PR**, titled `docs(context): <subject>` per `AGENTS.md` Conventional Commits,
    with an `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer and no `Co-Authored-By` or
    `Signed-off-by`.
13. **Fix in place.** If you discover while working that a doc is wrong or incomplete, correct it
    in the *same* PR as your code change and update `verified-at` to the commit you checked
    against. Leaving a doc stale for someone else to hit is the exact failure this folder exists to
    prevent. This rule applies to AI sessions too.
14. **New docs need three things in one commit [checked]:** the file, its `INDEX.md` row, and a
    `scope:` that does not overlap any existing doc's. If the scope overlaps, you wanted to edit
    that doc, not add one.
15. **`./.claude-students/check.sh` passes before you push [checked].** It is dependency-free and
    finishes in under a second.

## The guide layer (rules 16-22)

`guide/` holds a plain-English page for each reference page in `docs/`, same filename. It exists so
a person new to Go and to this codebase can get oriented. It is **derived**, not independent.

16. Every guide carries `source:`, `source-hash:` and `verified-at:` in its frontmatter **[checked]**.
17. A guide's `source:` names a real `docs/*.md` with the **same filename** **[checked]**.
18. `source-hash:` is the first 16 characters of `sha256sum docs/<name>.md`. If the reference page
    changes and the guide is not regenerated, `check.sh` reports **drift** **[checked]**. Regenerating
    means: reread the reference page, rewrite the guide, update the hash and `verified-at`.
19. Guide headings match `guide/_TEMPLATE.md` exactly and in order **[checked]**.
20. Guides are capped at **200 lines**, code fences at **30** **[checked]** — teaching needs more room
    than reference does.
21. **A guide adds explanation, vocabulary and worked steps. It adds no new facts.** Every repo path
    a guide cites must also be cited by its source page **[checked]**. If you need a fact the
    reference page lacks, add it *there* first, which bumps the hash and forces the guide to be
    regenerated in the same commit — exactly the intended order.
22. `guide/START-HERE.md` has no source page. It is exempt from rules 17, 18 and 21, and is where
    cross-cutting material lives that no single reference page owns.

**Never fix a fact in `guide/`.** If the two layers disagree, the reference page is the truth and
the guide is stale: fix `docs/`, regenerate the guide, ship both in one PR. A disagreement is a bug
report against `docs/`, not an editing job in `guide/`.

**Known limitation:** a hand-edit to a guide that only rewords prose is not mechanically
detectable. Rule 21 catches invented facts; rule 18 catches a stale guide; review catches the rest.

## Updating `verified-at`

`verified-at` is the short SHA the doc was last checked against, from `git rev-parse --short HEAD`.
Bump it whenever you confirm or correct a doc. A doc whose `verified-at` is far behind `main` has
not been checked recently — treat its details as hints and confirm them in the code before relying
on them.
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Validates .claude-students against the mechanical rules in MAINTENANCE.md.
# Dependency-free. Run from anywhere: ./.claude-students/check.sh
set -uo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1

DIR=".claude-students"
TEMPLATE="$DIR/_TEMPLATE.md"
INDEX="$DIR/INDEX.md"
MAX_LINES=120
MAX_INDEX_LINES=60
MAX_FENCE=10

fail=0
err() {
  printf '%s: %s\n' "$1" "$2" >&2
  fail=1
}

for required in "$TEMPLATE" "$INDEX" "$DIR/MAINTENANCE.md" "$DIR/README.md"; do
  [ -f "$required" ] || err "$required" "missing"
done
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || exit 1

check_whitespace() {
  local file="$1" line
  line=$(grep -n '[[:space:]]$' "$file" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
  [ -z "$line" ] || err "$file:$line" "trailing whitespace (rule 10)"
  [ -z "$(tail -c 1 "$file")" ] || err "$file" "no final newline (rule 10)"
}

for meta in "$TEMPLATE" "$INDEX" "$DIR/MAINTENANCE.md" "$DIR/README.md"; do
  check_whitespace "$meta"
done

want_h2=$(grep '^## ' "$TEMPLATE")

index_lines=$(wc -l < "$INDEX")
if [ "$index_lines" -gt "$MAX_INDEX_LINES" ]; then
  err "$INDEX" "$index_lines lines, cap is $MAX_INDEX_LINES (rule 6)"
fi

claimed=""
found_doc=0

for doc in "$DIR"/docs/*.md; do
  [ -e "$doc" ] || break
  found_doc=1
  name="${doc##*/}"

  lines=$(wc -l < "$doc")
  if [ "$lines" -gt "$MAX_LINES" ]; then
    err "$doc" "$lines lines, cap is $MAX_LINES - split it (rule 6)"
  fi

  check_whitespace "$doc"

  if [ "$(head -1 "$doc")" != "---" ]; then
    err "$doc:1" "must open with a --- frontmatter block (rule 5)"
  fi

  scope_line=$(sed -n '2,10{/^scope:/p;}' "$doc")
  [ -n "$scope_line" ] || err "$doc" "frontmatter has no scope: (rule 14)"
  [ -n "$(sed -n '2,10{/^verified-at:/p;}' "$doc")" ] ||
    err "$doc" "frontmatter has no verified-at: (rule 13)"

  got_h2=$(grep '^## ' "$doc")
  if [ "$got_h2" != "$want_h2" ]; then
    err "$doc" "## headings must match _TEMPLATE.md exactly and in order (rule 5)"
  fi

  long_fence=$(awk -v max="$MAX_FENCE" '
    /^```/ {
      if (open) { if (NR - start - 1 > max) print start; open = 0 }
      else { open = 1; start = NR }
    }
  ' "$doc" | head -1)
  [ -z "$long_fence" ] ||
    err "$doc:$long_fence" "code fence over $MAX_FENCE lines - cite the file instead (rule 8)"

  lineref=$(grep -nE '\.(go|ts|vue|tmpl|css|md|yml|json):[0-9]+' "$doc" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
  [ -z "$lineref" ] ||
    err "$doc:$lineref" "cites a line number - use the symbol name instead (rule 8)"

  abspath=$(grep -nE '(^|[[:space:]`(])(/home/|/Users/|/root/|[A-Za-z]:\\)' "$doc" |
    head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
  [ -z "$abspath" ] || err "$doc:$abspath" "absolute path - use a repo-relative one (rule 9)"

  grep -q "docs/$name" "$INDEX" || err "$INDEX" "no row pointing at docs/$name (rule 14)"

  while read -r path; do
    [ -n "$path" ] || continue
    [ -e "$path" ] || err "$doc" "scope path does not exist: $path (rule 7)"
    owner=$(printf '%s' "$claimed" | awk -F'|' -v p="$path" '$1 == p { print $2; exit }')
    if [ -n "$owner" ]; then
      err "$doc" "scope path $path is already owned by docs/$owner (rule 2)"
    else
      claimed="${claimed}${path}|${name}
"
    fi
  done < <(printf '%s\n' "${scope_line#scope:}" | tr ',' '\n' |
    sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//')
done

[ "$found_doc" -eq 1 ] || err "$DIR/docs" "contains no docs"

while read -r ref; do
  [ -f "$DIR/$ref" ] || err "$INDEX" "points at $ref, which does not exist (rule 14)"
done < <(grep -oE 'docs/[a-z0-9.-]+\.md' "$INDEX" | sort -u)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- guide/ (rules 16-22)
GUIDE_TEMPLATE="$DIR/guide/_TEMPLATE.md"
MAX_GUIDE_LINES=200
MAX_GUIDE_FENCE=30
guide_count=0

if [ -f "$GUIDE_TEMPLATE" ]; then
  want_guide_h2=$(grep '^## ' "$GUIDE_TEMPLATE")
  check_whitespace "$GUIDE_TEMPLATE"

  for g in "$DIR"/guide/*.md; do
    [ -e "$g" ] || break
    gname="${g##*/}"
    case "$gname" in _TEMPLATE.md) continue ;; esac

    check_whitespace "$g"

    lines=$(wc -l < "$g")
    if [ "$lines" -gt "$MAX_GUIDE_LINES" ]; then
      err "$g" "$lines lines, cap is $MAX_GUIDE_LINES (rule 20)"
    fi

    long_fence=$(awk -v max="$MAX_GUIDE_FENCE" '
      /^```/ {
        if (open) { if (NR - start - 1 > max) print start; open = 0 }
        else { open = 1; start = NR }
      }
    ' "$g" | head -1)
    [ -z "$long_fence" ] ||
      err "$g:$long_fence" "code fence over $MAX_GUIDE_FENCE lines (rule 20)"

    # START-HERE.md has no source doc: exempt from rules 17, 18, 21 (rule 22)
    case "$gname" in START-HERE.md) continue ;; esac

    got_guide_h2=$(grep '^## ' "$g")
    if [ "$got_guide_h2" != "$want_guide_h2" ]; then
      err "$g" "## headings must match guide/_TEMPLATE.md exactly and in order (rule 19)"
    fi
```

```text
### User Story

As a repository maintainer, I want a way to set a close reason for an issue and a PR so there is historical context for why the closing occurred. Furthermore, I want to be able to clearly and quickly see the reason behind the closing of an issue or PR in the UI.

### User Scenario

#### Writing the Reasons
A user who is attempting to close an issue or PR can either close the issue with a default reason by clicking the current "close issue/PR" button or by clicking the split button that will show a drop down to select from set responses:

| Reason | Special Semantics |
| --- | ---| 
| "Completed" | **Default** option for Issue. **NOT AVAILABLE FOR PR**. |
|"Not Planned" | **Default** for PR |
| "Duplicate" | Asks for the original issue number and links to the relevant issue |
| "Other" | Shows a text box to fill (required, and max 255 characters) (shown in plain text) |

This applies to the issue/PR bulk "Close" action button, but only "completed and not planned" are the possible reasons for issues and "not planned" for PRs.

The button text will reflect the chosen reason.

**Note: The choice/reason can be changed before closing the issue or PR**.

#### Display
Show the reason on the "close timeline comment." Closed items will also show a distinct icon/label per reason for quick visual feedback.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given an open issue, when the user clicks the main Close button without opening the dropdown, then it closes as "Completed"; an open PR closed the same way closes as "Not planned".
- [ ] AC2: Given an open issue, when the user opens the Close button's dropdown, then it offers Completed, Not planned, Duplicate and Other; for a PR it offers the same list without Completed, and merging a PR still needs no reason.
- [ ] AC3: Given a reason picked from the dropdown, when the user picks a different one before closing (with or without a comment typed), then the button text shows the latest choice and that reason is the one saved.
- [ ] AC4: Given "Duplicate" is chosen, when the number entered is not an issue or PR in the same repository, or is the item itself, then the close is refused with an error message and the item stays open; a valid number closes it, and the timeline links to the original.
- [ ] AC5: Given "Other" is chosen, when the text box is empty or longer than 255 characters, then the close is refused with an error message; otherwise the text is saved and the timeline shows it as plain text, with HTML and Markdown not rendered.
- [ ] AC6: Given several open issues selected on the Issues tab, when the user bulk-closes them as Completed or Not planned, then every selected issue closes with that reason; on the Pull Requests tab, the bulk dropdown offers only Not planned.
- [ ] AC7: Given an item closed with a reason, when its timeline is viewed, then the close event states the reason, e.g. "closed this as not planned", "closed this as a duplicate of #N" or "closed this: <text>".
- [ ] AC8: Given closed items with different reasons, when viewed in the issue or PR list and on the item's page, then each reason shows its own icon or label; items closed before this feature, which have no reason, look exactly as they do today.
- [ ] AC9: Given an item closed with a reason, when it is reopened, then the list and page no longer show the reason's icon or label, and the timeline keeps the earlier close event with its reason.
- [ ] AC10: Given the new dropdown, text box, error messages and timeline text, when a page shows them in English, then each string comes from a key in `options/locale/locale_en-US.json`, and no other locale file is changed.


### Out of Scope

- Pop up icon. Will be implemented alongside the API and automated changes in issue #55  since that impacts the API layer.
- Closing reason via Gitea's automated closing services: Same as above, to be implemented in issue #55.

### Open Questions

- ~~Should marking something as duplicate require the user to input a number (with pop ups like in the issues and PR editors), or a drop-down.~~: **Answered by decision 7**

### Scope

medium
```

```text
feat(issues): frontend implementation of close issue reason 

Closes #54

## What changed and why

#53 stores and checks why an issue or pull request was closed, but nothing on the page let you choose a reason or see one. This PR adds the UI for it.

- **Close button:** on an issue or pull request page it becomes a split button that names its reason. The ▾ lists the reasons that item may use, and the button text follows the pick, with or without a comment typed. This was done for both showing the default reason that would be submitted, but also to reflect the chosen option.
- **Duplicate and Other:** each asks for its detail in a small popup under the button, reusing, for the most part, components that already existed in Gitea. A close without a usable value isn't sent; the popup reopens with the box marked red instead.
- **Timeline:** the close event says why: "closed this as not planned", "closed this as a duplicate of #N" with a link to it, or the Other text, shown as plain text.
- **Icons and labels:** closed items show their reason in lists, in the label at the top of the page and on the timeline badge. The color scheme follows what the current Gitea follows to keep things consistent. Items closed without a reason look as they do today.
- **Bulk close:** the list's Close button works the same way. The Issues tab offers Completed and Not planned, and the Pull Requests tab only Not planned (only a single option, but maintained the split for consistency).
- **Two of #53's known limitations are resolved:** a duplicate's title and link are only shown to viewers who can read the original, and the reason names now live in the model rather than the form, so #55's API can reuse them.
- The old, now unused button strings are removed, and the docs in `.claude-students` are updated.

## How the changes relate to the ACs

- **AC1:** the button starts on Completed for an issue and Not planned for a pull request, so a plain click closes with that reason.
- **AC2:** the menu offers Completed, Not planned, Duplicate and Other on an issue, and the same without Completed on a pull request. Merging is unchanged.
- **AC3:** picking another reason updates the button text, with or without a comment, and the last pick is the one saved.
- **AC4:** a number that isn't an issue or pull request in the repository, or is the item itself, is marked red with a message and the close isn't sent; the server refuses it too (#53). A valid number closes it, and the timeline links to the original.
- **AC5:** an empty description blocks the close, and the box stops at 255 characters; the server refuses both too (#53). The text is saved and shown as plain text.
- **AC6:** bulk Close offers Completed and Not planned on the Issues tab and only Not planned on the Pull Requests tab, and every selected item closes with the picked reason.
- **AC7:** the close event states the reason.
- **AC8:** each reason has its own icon and label; items with no reason look as before.
- **AC9:** reopening brings back the open look, and the earlier close event keeps its reason.
- **AC10:** every new string is in `locale_en-US.json`, and no other locale file changed.


## How it was tested

Testing was done in three distinct parts. 
- Vitest tests and integration tests to prove the functioning of the UI in the code itself. The tests themselves were tested by deliberately breaking code to see the changes and tests fail.
- A visual inspection of the changes by running a local instance. Since the changes were performed in small sets, the checks ensured only the behavior of the targeted portions changed, and nothing else.
- Claude running a headless browser with its own credentials to test the program and fix issues as it spotted them.

| AC | What the tests check |
| --- | --- |
| AC1 | Each page's button starts on its default, and a plain close saves it |
| AC2 | The menu's reasons and labels on an issue and a pull request; a closed item only offers Reopen |
| AC3 | Picking changes the button text and the reason sent, with and without a comment typed |
| AC4 | The preview of the typed number; a missing number, the item itself, text or a non-whole number blocks the close; the timeline link |
| AC5 | Other's text is sent as typed; empty or spaces-only blocks the close; the 255 limit; HTML and Markdown in the timeline stay plain text |
| AC6 | Both tabs' menus; bulk closing several issues with each reason and a pull request as not planned; a refused reason leaves the item open |
| AC7 | The timeline text for each reason, and for a close with no reason |
| AC8 | The list icon, page label and timeline badge for each reason and for none; a merged pull request still looks merged |
| AC9 | Reopening shows the open look again, and the earlier close keeps its reason |
| AC10 | Labels are checked as rendered text, so a missing key would show up as the key itself |

The tests are in `models/issues/issue_close_reason_test.go`, `tests/integration/issue_test.go`, `web_src/js/features/repo-issue-status-button.test.ts`, `repo-issue-list.test.ts` and `repo-common.test.ts`. The Playwright test `tests/e2e/issue-comment.test.ts` now clicks the renamed button.


## Known limitations

- The hover popup on issue links still shows the old icon. It reads the API, so it is out of scope.
- Bulk close shows no message when the server refuses a close, whether for a blocked dependency or a reason only a hand-made request can send. A "FIXME" was present for the relevant code, but was not changed since that would be way out of scope, impacting behavior that should not belong to this set of changes.
- Closing with a comment still posts the comment if the server then refuses the close. This should be highly unlikely, but since it is a general pattern to have the server be the final verifier of rules, blocking such behavior would not follow convention.
- A pull request closed as not planned has the same icon as an issue closed as not planned; its link still says which it is (Decision 8).
- The red message in the duplicate popup isn't announced by screen readers. Gitea doesn't use `aria-invalid` anywhere, so this follows it.

## AI assistance

Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) drafted the code, tests, docs and other changes. I made the decisions, refused to let Claude commit on my behalf, and made commits as small as possible so I can review them with tests.

# Design Decisions for the first commit (adding list of reasons to the model)

### Decision 1: The reason names are kept in one place, next to the reasons

**Decision:** The words the page uses for each reason (`completed`, `not_planned`, `duplicate`, `other`) are listed once, beside the reasons themselves.
**Alternatives Considered:** Keep the list on the close form, and give bulk close its own copy.
**Rationale:** The close button, bulk close and the page's menu all need the same words. With one list they can't drift apart, and the API can reuse it.
**Consequences:** Renaming a word breaks anything still sending the old one. Reviews keep their own list on their form, so both styles exist in the codebase.


### Decision 2: The server decides which reason the close button starts on (i.e, a hard-coded default)

**Decision:** An issue's close button starts on completed and a pull request's on not planned (AC1). A close with no reason still records none.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) The page picks the default itself. (b) Treat a close with no reason as the default.
**Rationale:** This is how Gitea handles buttons that start on a choice: the merge button and the "Update branch" button both get their default from the server, from a built-in value that settings can override. Thus, hard-coded values can be easily overridden.
**Consequences:** A setting to change the default can be added later on top of the built-in one, the way `DEFAULT_MERGE_STYLE` works for merges. The future API can use the same default or keep its own, as the API's branch update already does.
--

# Design Decision for the second main commit (adding the menu to the buttons [no functionality])

### Decision 3: A leftover style/rule was removed from repo.css

**Decision:** The comment box's button row had a style that cut off anything reaching outside it (`overflow: hidden` in `web_src/css/repo.css`), which hid the close reason menu. The style has been deleted.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Keep the style and override it for this row only. (b) Build the menu as a popup attached to the whole page, which no box can cut off, as a few of Gitea's small menus are.
**Rationale:** A deep analysis of the repo showed that it applies to nothing else, and that this was a leftover from a replacement in 2025. Changes were confirmed visually, and the menu now pops up, confirming that as the single cause..
**Consequences:** If anything in the row ever does reach outside it, such as a very long translated button label on a phone, it will now show instead of being cut off.
--

# Design Decision for the third main commit (removal of old locale strings)

### Decision 4: The old close button strings are deleted

**Decision:** "Close Issue", "Close Pull Request" and "Close with Comment" are deleted from `locale_en-US.json`, since the close button now names its reason and nothing else uses them. The other languages are left for the translation platform to clean up (AC10).
**Alternatives Considered:** Keep them in the file, unused.
**Rationale:** An unused string still reaches translators, who would keep translating text no page shows.
**Consequences:** Bringing back any of these labels means adding the key again, and it starts with no translations.
--

# Design Decision for the forth main commit (button refactor)

### Decision 5: The close/reopen button gets its own piece of page code

**Decision:** The code that sets the close/reopen button's text ("…with comment" once a comment is typed) and disables it during uploads moves out of the comment box's setup into its own feature, `web_src/js/features/repo-issue-status-button.ts`. It is switched on by a `data-global-init` attribute on the button in the template.
**Alternatives Considered:** Leave the button's code in the comment box's setup, and add reason picking there.
**Rationale:** `data-global-init` is the wiring Gitea requires, per its docs, and existing code does use this pattern, including the "Update branch" split button. Moving the button's existing code as well means one place decides everything the button shows, instead of two pieces of code writing the same text.
**Consequences:** Despite the fact that existing code use `data-global-init`, this will be is the first feature to follow a comment box it did not set up, since it relies on the box's events reaching the for. The move also touches existing upstream code, so the change is bigger than the reason picking alone.
--

# Design Decision for the fifth main commit (click listener vs deprecated Fomantic components)

### Decision 6: Picking a reason is processed with a plain click listener, not Fomantic's change callback

**Decision:** The page notices a pick with an ordinary click listener on the menu's items, along with a `js-aria-clickable` class for accessbility and the ability to _click._ with the enter button with the help of Gitea's dropdown change.
**Alternatives Considered:** Fomantic's `onChange` callback, as the "Update branch" split button uses.
**Rationale:** Gitea froze Fomantic (upstream #33845) and replaces it by rewriting modules. Using a click listener will survive such rewriting as Fomantic components had to be done. This is especially important when issue #25 plans to make dropdowns accessible, so this sets a precedent within the repo.
**Consequences:** Keyboard picking depends on the `js-aria-clickable` class, which only two of Gitea's menus use. The page's integration test checks every item carries it, so a later edit can't drop it unnoticed. It also departs from the only other split button, which still uses `onChange`.
--

# Design Decision for the sixth main commit (implementation of the duplicate issue picker and other issue box)

### Decision 7: Duplicate and Other ask for their detail in a small popup, and the close button shows the result

**Decision:** Picking "Duplicate" or "Other" opens a small popup under the close button, like the markdown editor's "Add table" popup. For a duplicate, you type the original's number: that issue appears beside the box (its icon, number and title), and the button reads "Close as duplicate of #12". 
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) A box above the buttons with the `#` suggestions from the comment box. (b) A search picker like the sidebar's "add dependency". (c) Greying out Close, with or without a tooltip saying why.
**Rationale:** The button already says what closing will do, so it is where the choice belongs. (a) left only "#12" in the box, and the backend had to accept text to fit the widget, and would need to be modified to do so (b) is a larger control built on Fomantic's JavaScript. The server posts the comment before it checks the close, so the page has to stop a close that would be refused. Answering the click, the way a browser points at a required field, still explains it after the popup is closed, which a greyed-out button can't.
**Consequences:** The preview uses the `#` list's search, so an issue the viewer can't read counts as not found. Finding an issue by its title is left out. A change between typing and clicking, such as the original being deleted, still ends with the comment posted and the close refused.



--

# Design Decision for the seventh main commit (close reason labels and icons)

### Decision 8: Each close reason gets its own icon, in the colours Gitea already uses for "done" and "set aside"

**Decision:** A closed issue or pull request shows why it was closed, in lists, in the label at the top of its page and on its close event in the timeline. Completed is a purple closed icon; not planned, duplicate and other are grey, with a skip, duplicate and note icon. Items closed without a reason (older closes, merges, automatic closes) keep today's red closed icon.
**Alternatives Considered:** Keep completed red like today's closed icon, and give new icons only to the other reasons.
**Rationale:** Gitea's colours already have meanings: purple is done, as for a merged pull request, and grey is set aside, as for a draft or a skipped job. Following them makes the reasons readable without learning anything new.
**Consequences:** The icon depends only on the reason, so a pull request closed as not planned looks like an issue closed as not planned; its link still says which it is. 
--

# Design Decision for the eight main commit (bulk close)

### Decision 9: The list's Close button works like the one on an issue's page

**Decision:** When items are selected on the issue or pull request list, Close becomes the same button as on an item's page.
**Alternatives Considered:** A menu whose items close straight away, like the Labels and Milestone menus beside it; and on the Pull Requests tab, a plain "Close as not planned" button with no ▾.
**Rationale:** Closing works the same way everywhere, and the button always says what it will do. Both menus come from the reasons the model allows, leaving out Duplicate and Other, whose number or description belongs to a single item; so a new reason shows up without changing the page.
**Consequences:** The Pull Requests tab's menu holds a single item for now.
--

diff --git a/models/issues/issue_close_reason.go b/models/issues/issue_close_reason.go
index 77ed1293a0..d2971f6a69 100644
--- a/models/issues/issue_close_reason.go
+++ b/models/issues/issue_close_reason.go
@@ -27,6 +27,34 @@ const (
 // CloseReasonUnknown is never stored: it stands for an unrecognised reason name, so that Validate rejects it.
 const CloseReasonUnknown CloseReason = -1
 
+// closeReasonNames are what forms and pages send instead of the stored numbers, so existing names must never change.
+// CloseReasonNone has no name: an empty name means no reason.
+var closeReasonNames = map[CloseReason]string{
+	CloseReasonCompleted:  "completed",
+	CloseReasonNotPlanned: "not_planned",
+	CloseReasonDuplicate:  "duplicate",
+	CloseReasonOther:      "other",
+}
+
+// String returns the reason's name, or "" for no reason.
+func (r CloseReason) String() string {
+	return closeReasonNames[r] // a map rather than CommentType's slice, so CloseReasonUnknown can't index out of range
+}
+
+// AsCloseReason returns the reason with the given name; an empty name means no reason,
+// and an unknown one returns CloseReasonUnknown so that Validate rejects it.
+func AsCloseReason(name string) CloseReason {
+	if name == "" {
+		return CloseReasonNone
+	}
+	for reason, reasonName := range closeReasonNames {
+		if reasonName == name {
+			return reason
+		}
+	}
+	return CloseReasonUnknown
+}
+
 // CloseReasonTextMaxLength matches the VARCHAR(255) close_reason_text column and the close form's MaxSize(255)
 // rule. Validate counts characters the same way MaxSize does, so paths that skip the form get the same limit.
 // MSSQL's NVARCHAR counts UTF-16 units instead, so text with many emoji can pass this limit and still not fit.
@@ -41,6 +69,22 @@ func AllowedCloseReasons(isPull bool) []CloseReason {
 	return []CloseReason{CloseReasonCompleted, CloseReasonNotPlanned, CloseReasonDuplicate, CloseReasonOther}
 }
 
+// BulkCloseReasons lists the reasons offered when closing several items at once: the allowed ones that need
+// nothing more, as a duplicate's number and an "other" description each belong to a single item.
+func BulkCloseReasons(isPull bool) []CloseReason {
+	return slices.DeleteFunc(AllowedCloseReasons(isPull), func(r CloseReason) bool {
+		return r == CloseReasonDuplicate || r == CloseReasonOther
+	})
+}
+
+// DefaultCloseReason is the reason the close button starts on; consumers may still send any allowed reason, or none.
+func DefaultCloseReason(isPull bool) CloseReason {
+	if isPull {
+		return CloseReasonNotPlanned
+	}
+	return CloseReasonCompleted
+}
+
 // CloseReasonOptions is the reason a person gives when closing an issue or pull request.
 type CloseReasonOptions struct {
 	Reason         CloseReason

+func TestCloseReasonNames(t *testing.T) {

+	}
+	assert.Empty(t, issues_model.CloseReasonNone.String())
+	assert.Empty(t, issues_model.CloseReasonUnknown.String())
+}

+func TestIssueCloseReasonMenu(t *testing.T) {
+	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()
+	session := loginUser(t, "user2")
+
+	// the button texts each menu item hands to the button when it is picked
+	itemTexts := map[string][2]string{
+		"completed":   {"Close as completed", "Close as completed with comment"},
+		"not_planned": {"Close as not planned", "Close as not planned with comment"},
+		"duplicate":   {"Close as duplicate", "Close as duplicate with comment"},
+		"other":       {"Close with other reason", "Close with other reason and comment"},
+	}
+
+	// closeFromPage checks the close button and its menu, then closes with the reason the page itself sends
+	closeFromPage := func(t *testing.T, link, wantText, wantTextWithComment string, wantReasons, wantLabels []string) {
+		htmlDoc := NewHTMLParser(t, session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", link), http.StatusOK).Body)
+		button := htmlDoc.doc.Find("#comment-form .ui.buttons #status-button")
+		assert.Equal(t, wantText, strings.TrimSpace(button.Find(".status-button-text").Text()))
+		assert.Equal(t, wantTextWithComment, button.AttrOr("data-status-and-comment", ""))
+
+		var reasons, labels []string
+		htmlDoc.doc.Find("#comment-form .ui.buttons .menu .item").Each(func(_ int, item *goquery.Selection) {
+			reason := item.AttrOr("data-value", "")
+			reasons = append(reasons, reason)
+			labels = append(labels, strings.TrimSpace(item.Text())) // a missing locale key would show as the key
+			rendered := [2]string{item.AttrOr("data-status", ""), item.AttrOr("data-status-and-comment", "")}
+			assert.Equal(t, itemTexts[reason], rendered, "reason %q", reason)
+			assert.True(t, item.HasClass("js-aria-clickable"), "reason %q: without it, Enter does not pick the item", reason)
+		})
+		assert.Equal(t, wantReasons, reasons)
+		assert.Equal(t, wantLabels, labels)
+
+		// what duplicate and other need is typed in their popups into fields that are switched off, so not sent, until picked
+		assert.Equal(t, 1, htmlDoc.doc.Find(`#comment-form input[type="hidden"][name="close_duplicate_index"][disabled]`).Length())
+		assert.Equal(t, 1, htmlDoc.doc.Find(`#comment-form input[type="hidden"][name="close_reason_text"][disabled]`).Length())
+		duplicatePopup := htmlDoc.doc.Find(`#comment-form [data-close-reason-popup="duplicate"]`)
+		assert.Equal(t, "Close as duplicate of #%s", duplicatePopup.AttrOr("data-locale-status", ""))
+		assert.Equal(t, "Close as duplicate of #%s with comment", duplicatePopup.AttrOr("data-locale-status-and-comment", ""))
+		assert.Equal(t, 1, duplicatePopup.Find(`.field label[for="close-duplicate-index"] + input#close-duplicate-index[type="number"][min="1"]`).Length(), "in a field, so an unusable number can be marked as an error")
+		preview := duplicatePopup.Find(`[data-close-duplicate-preview]`)
+		assert.Equal(t, "close-duplicate-preview", duplicatePopup.Find("#close-duplicate-index").AttrOr("aria-describedby", ""), "its message is read with the box")
+		assert.Equal(t, "close-duplicate-preview", preview.AttrOr("id", ""))
+		assert.Equal(t, "No #%s found in this repository", preview.AttrOr("data-locale-not-found", ""))
+		assert.Equal(t, "Can't be a duplicate of itself", preview.AttrOr("data-locale-self", ""))
+		assert.Equal(t, 1, htmlDoc.doc.Find(`#comment-form [data-close-reason-popup="other"] .field input[type="text"][maxlength="255"]`).Length())
+
+		reason, exists := htmlDoc.doc.Find(`#comment-form input[name="close_reason"]`).Attr("value")
+		require.True(t, exists, "The template has changed")
+		action, exists := htmlDoc.doc.Find("#comment-form").Attr("action")
+		require.True(t, exists, "The template has changed")
+		session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", action, map[string]string{"status": "close", "close_reason": reason}), http.StatusOK)

+func TestIssueCloseReasonIcons(t *testing.T) {
+	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()
+	session := loginUser(t, "user2")
+
+	// the octicon and colour classes of an icon, which are what tell the reasons apart, sorted since their order means nothing
+	iconClasses := func(svg *goquery.Selection) string {
+		var classes []string
+		for class := range strings.FieldsSeq(svg.AttrOr("class", "")) {
+			if strings.HasPrefix(class, "octicon-") || strings.HasPrefix(class, "tw-") {
+				classes = append(classes, class)
+			}
+		}
+		slices.Sort(classes)
+		return strings.Join(classes, " ")
+	}
+	// closeFromPage posts the close form of an issue or pull request page with the given reason fields
+	closeFromPage := func(t *testing.T, link string, fields map[string]string) {
+		action, exists := NewHTMLParser(t, session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", link), http.StatusOK).Body).doc.Find("#comment-form").Attr("action")
+		require.True(t, exists, "The template has changed")
+		fields["status"] = "close"
+		session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", action, fields), http.StatusOK)
+	}
+	type look struct{ listIcon, label, labelColor, badge string }
+	// lookOf reads an item's icon in its list, its state label, and the badge of its latest close event
+	lookOf := func(t *testing.T, kind string, index int64, listState string) look {
+		link := fmt.Sprintf("/user2/repo1/%s/%d", kind, index)
+		list := NewHTMLParser(t, session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", fmt.Sprintf("/user2/repo1/%s?state=%s", kind, listState)), http.StatusOK).Body)
+		row := list.doc.Find(fmt.Sprintf(`a.list-item-large-title[href="%s"]`, link)).Closest(".item")
+		require.Equal(t, 1, row.Length(), "%s is in the %s list", link, listState)
+
+		page := NewHTMLParser(t, session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", link), http.StatusOK).Body)
+		label := page.doc.Find(".issue-title-meta .issue-state-label")
+		labelColor := ""
+		for _, color := range []string{"red", "purple", "grey", "green"} {
+			if label.HasClass(color) {
+				labelColor = color
+			}
+		}
+		var badge string // the last close event's; a merged pull request has none
+		page.doc.Find(".timeline-item.event").Each(func(_ int, event *goquery.Selection) {
+			if strings.Contains(event.Find(".comment-text-line").First().Text(), "closed this") {
+				b := event.Find(".badge")
+				badge = strings.Join(strings.Fields(b.AttrOr("class", "")+" "+iconClasses(b.Find("svg"))), " ") // "badge " when it has no colour
+			}
+		})
+		return look{iconClasses(row.Find(".item-leading svg")), strings.Join(strings.Fields(label.Text()), " "), labelColor, badge}
+	}
+
+	for _, c := range []struct {
+		name   string
+		fields map[string]string
+		want   look
+	}{
+		{
+			"completed is purple, like a merge",
+			map[string]string{"close_reason": "completed"},
+			look{"octicon-issue-closed tw-text-purple", "Closed as completed", "purple", "badge tw-bg-purple tw-text-white octicon-issue-closed"},
+		},
+		{
+			"not planned is grey, like a skipped job",
+			map[string]string{"close_reason": "not_planned"},
+			look{"octicon-skip tw-text-text-light", "Closed as not planned", "grey", "badge octicon-skip"},
+		},
+		{
+			"duplicate",
+			map[string]string{"close_reason": "duplicate", "close_duplicate_index": "1"},
+			look{"octicon-duplicate tw-text-text-light", "Closed as duplicate", "grey", "badge octicon-duplicate"},
+		},
+		{
+			"other keeps the plain title, its text is in the timeline",
+			map[string]string{"close_reason": "other", "close_reason_text": "superseded"},
+			look{"octicon-note tw-text-text-light", "Closed", "grey", "badge octicon-note"},
+		},
+		{
+			"no reason looks as it always did",
+			map[string]string{},
+			look{"octicon-issue-closed tw-text-red", "Closed", "red", "badge tw-bg-red tw-text-white octicon-issue-closed"},
+		},
+	} {
+		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			issueURL := testNewIssue(t, session, "user2", "repo1", "Icon check", "Description")
+			closeFromPage(t, issueURL, c.fields)
+			index, err := strconv.ParseInt(path.Base(issueURL), 10, 64)
+			require.NoError(t, err)
+			assert.Equal(t, c.want, lookOf(t, "issues", index, "closed"))
+		})
+	}
+
+	t.Run("reopening shows the open look again, and the earlier close keeps its badge", func(t *testing.T) {
+		issueURL := testNewIssue(t, session, "user2", "repo1", "Icon check", "Description")
+		closeFromPage(t, issueURL, map[string]string{"close_reason": "not_planned"})
+		session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", issueURL+"/comments", map[string]string{"status": "reopen"}), http.StatusOK)
+		index, err := strconv.ParseInt(path.Base(issueURL), 10, 64)
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		got := lookOf(t, "issues", index, "open")
+		assert.Equal(t, look{"octicon-issue-opened tw-text-green", "Open", "green", "badge octicon-skip"}, got)
+	})
+
+	t.Run("a pull request shows its reason; a merged one still looks merged", func(t *testing.T) {
+		closeFromPage(t, "/user2/repo1/pulls/3", map[string]string{"close_reason": "not_planned"})
+		assert.Equal(t, look{"octicon-skip tw-text-text-light", "Closed as not planned", "grey", "badge octicon-skip"}, lookOf(t, "pulls", 3, "closed"))
+		// pull request #2 is merged in the fixtures, but its issue is left open, which a real merge never does
+		mergedIssue := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 2})
+		mergedIssue.IsClosed = true
+		require.NoError(t, issues_model.UpdateIssueCols(t.Context(), mergedIssue, "is_closed"))
+		merged := lookOf(t, "pulls", 2, "closed")
+		assert.Equal(t, "octicon-git-merge tw-text-purple", merged.listIcon)
+		assert.Equal(t, "purple", merged.labelColor)
+	})
+}
